docs.title: fdia-graph
docs.text:
A Python package that builds attacked measurement timelines on power-grid test systems, with a second toolkit to analyse them. Download a ready timeline or generate your own.

A timeline is the meter readings of one grid, frame by frame, with false data injection attacks (FDIA) placed in it and labelled per bus.

docs.title: Two toolkits
docs.text:
Toolkit Package What it does fdia-graph fdia_graph generates a timeline and loads it fdia-analysis fdia_analysis runs estimators and localizers on a timeline

fdia-analysis holds state estimation, attack localization, federated training, trusted-meter selection and a results store. It depends on fdia-graph. fdia-graph never imports it.

docs.title: Test systems
docs.text:
System Buses Data IEEE and other public cases 14, 30, 57, 89, 118, 145, 200, 300 released datasets, downloaded by fg.load New York grid 140 case file in the package; you build the dataset

Each released dataset is one timeline of 72,000 frames. The New York grid is a MATPOWER case file with 140 buses and 227 branches. It goes through the same generator, and Build the operating points starts its dataset.

The generator makes two attack families: At, a slow load ramp, and Am, a line overload. The released files hold seven families: five that the generator does not make (Aq, Ad, As, Ar, Al), and an Am that drives no line to its limit. The attack families has the details.

docs.title: Three steps
docs.text:
1. Load a released dataset.

import fdia_graph as fg

# downloads the IEEE-118 timeline once, then caches it
train = fg.load("ieee118", split="train")
arrays = train.export()
print(arrays["node_x"].shape, arrays["y"].shape)

2. Generate your own, then load it by name.

# needs fdia-graph[generate]
# downloads the IEEE-14 pool of solved operating points
# about five minutes on a laptop
fg.generate("ieee14", name="my_run", frames=2000)
mine = fg.load("my_run", split="train")

3. Analyse it with an estimator.

# needs fdia-analysis[se]
from fdia_analysis.se.methods import WLS

test = fg.load("ieee118", split="test")
est = WLS().fit(train)
print(est.score(test))

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Command Gives pip install fdia-graph the loader: opens a timeline, exports splits as numpy arrays pip install "fdia-graph[torch]" adds PyTorch: single records, batches and the DataLoader pip install "fdia-graph[generate]" adds pandapower, to generate timelines pip install "fdia-analysis[se]" the analysis toolkit with state estimation

Every extra of both toolkits is listed in Install and data versions.

docs.title: Citation
docs.text:
• Al (released files) and the load bound of Am: Yuan, Li & Ren, Modeling load redistribution attacks in power systems, IEEE T-SG 2(2), 2011.
  • At: Haghshenas, Hasnat & Naeini, A Temporal GNN for Cyber Attack Detection and Localization in Smart Grids, IEEE ISGT 2023.
  • Measurement model: Zaman & Lin, PING: Physics-Informed GNNs to Generalize FDIA Localization, NAPS 2025.
  • Meter noise: Asprou, Kyriakides & Albu, Variable Weights in a WLS State Estimator, IEEE T-IM 63, 2014.
  • Protocol: Boyaci et al., Joint Detection and Localization of Stealth FDIA, IEEE T-SG, 2022.
  • Local false states, Am, trusted meters: Wu, Wang, Hu, Ye & Tang, Dynamic PMU configuration for stealthy multi-snapshot FDIA mitigation, IEEE T-SG 17(1), 2026.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: Every release lists what a user of the package can see change. "No user-visible change" means the public API, the generated files and the numbers are the same as the previous release.

docs.title: Unreleased
docs.text:
• A reading order for the attack code (no change in behaviour). The files of engine/ that hold a part, and every file of engine/attacks/, open with one sentence saying what the file does and name what it calls; engine/attacks/__init__.py lists the files in the order to read them. FdiaGenerator has a class docstring listing every attribute, with the shape and unit of each array. NodeChannel says once that injections are positive for load. docs/reference/FORMULAS.md has a new section, "[WU26] equation by equation", mapping the [WU26] equations the code cites to where they are cited. The search's BLAS thread limit is its own module, engine/attacks/blas.py (one_blas_thread). The tests use the source's names (knobs, support, boundary, area). With docstrings removed, every changed source file but the moved block is identical to before, and every IEEE timeline is byte for byte what it was.

  • The search's cost and a snapshot's moved channels are named records (the search finds the same supports; the cost's layout under the "channels" objective changes). AttackWindow.cost returns a SupportCost(devices, channels, size) (models/frames.py) where it returned a bare tuple whose first two slots swapped with the objective, so under "channels" a caller reading cost[0] now gets the devices; SupportCost.key gives the order the search compares, and AttackWindow.rank and counts, which packed and unpacked the tuple, are gone. The channels a snapshot moves beyond noise are a MeterLayers of masks (node, edge, current), where they were three positional arrays. Every IEEE timeline is byte for byte what it was.

  • The false state of a goal has one entry point, in FalseState (no change in behaviour). goal_state moves from Minimizer to FalseState (g.false_state.goal_state), with load_goal_state and flow_goal_state beside it. The load goal's solve was written twice (once for the ramp's frames, once for the search) and is now written once. So the search's window no longer calls back into the search, and an overload frame no longer goes through it. Leftover parameters are gone: RampFrames.attack_frame(x_true, family, design, knobs) is ramp_frame(x_true, design, knobs) (the family could only be At), and EpisodeDesigns.am_overload_design(X, t, length, knobs, rng) is am_overload_design(states, knobs, rng) (it was only ever given a whole window). Every IEEE timeline is byte for byte what it was.

  • One word for each set of buses in the attack code (no change in behaviour). The code used about eight words for four things. Now: the area is where the attacker may act, the support is the set of buses a false state re-solves, the boundary is the buses one branch outside it, and the reach is the support with its boundary. The glossary defines each.

Was Now local_region AttackArea.hop_area interior (a parameter, and the field of AttackDesign) support interior of AttackArea.boundary and grow_over_zero_injection, and of formulas.attacks.within_limits buses (each takes an area, a support or a reach) S (a support) support touched, touched_buses reach with_region with_support formulas.network: the interior parameter of local_ac_solve, local_flow_solve and their helpers support

A call that passed interior= or S= by keyword must use support= (buses= for the three in the last row). Every IEEE timeline is byte for byte what it was.

  • Names in the attack code say what the thing is (no change in behaviour). Xt and Xa are x_true and x_false; Lp and Lq are p_load and q_load; the attack knobs a function takes are knobs, not k (so AttackWindow.k is AttackWindow.knobs). On the generator, C, E and ei are n_bus, n_branch and edge_index. The parameters of formulas.attacks.within_limits and of the ScanLoads methods are renamed with them, so a call that passed Xt=, Xa=, Lp=, Lq= or k= by keyword must use the new name. Every IEEE timeline is byte for byte what it was. The attacks page and the glossary are corrected where they said something the code does not do: a ramp's targets need not be neighbours; a ramp stays one step away from the true load after its return and can end before the return is complete; the search tries the whole area first; a ramp checks the generator limits inside the buses it re-solves and not on the buses one branch outside, where an overload does; the third rating source "delta"; the tamper threshold is the rated accuracy for At and the paper noise for Am; the designs are methods of EpisodeDesigns; and a search that finds no support records -1 devices and the ramp runs on its whole area.

  • One file layout. A timeline has flows at the from end of a branch and PMU currents as real and imaginary part, on every test system; nothing in the package wrote any other form since the New York source left, so the other form is gone from the package.

  • Removed: LayerSet (both_ends, temporal) and the spec argument of FdiaGenerator and TimelineWriter; MeterKind.I and IA, PolarCurrentChannel, EdgeChannel.P_TO and Q_TO; schema.CURRENT_POLAR; Capability.RECTANGULAR_CURRENTS; FdiaGraph.current_form. MeterKind.IR and II are now 6 and 7 (a plan's kinds are not stored in a file).
  • A file that declares another layout (four flows in edge_feat, or a current_form other than rectangular) is refused with NotATimeline when it is opened (models.inputs.ReadableLayout), where before an estimator refused a polar file at the fit. Every released file opens as before.
  • The notes file that sat inside the package is deleted; the rules it restated are in CONTRIBUTING.md and the tests.

  • Every IEEE timeline is byte for byte what it was.

  • The two densest files of the attack core are split by job. No method's logic changed, and every IEEE timeline is byte for byte what it was.

  • engine/attacks/frames.py, the new part AttackFrames (g.attack_frames): frame_from_state, frame_from_vector, attack_vector, current_attack, currents_with_attack and changed_meters, out of false_state.py, which keeps the solves and the limits.

  • engine/attacks/window.py: AttackWindow (was _Window in minimize.py), what a candidate support costs over a window. minimize.py keeps the search over supports.

  • The generator is made of parts, not mixins. FdiaGenerator held every method through a stack of mixins; it now holds one object per job, named after its class, so a call names the class its method is in.

Part On the generator Was Emitter (engine/measurement.py) g.emitter MeasurementMixin ScanLoads (engine/physics.py) g.scan_loads PhysicsMixin AttackArea (engine/attacks/area.py) g.area AreaMixin FalseState (engine/attacks/false_state.py) g.false_state FalseStateMixin RampFrames (engine/attacks/ramp_frames.py) g.ramp_frames StealthyMixin, and AttackMixin.attack_frame Minimizer (engine/attacks/minimize.py) g.minimizer MinimizeMixin Overload (engine/attacks/overload.py) g.overload OverloadMixin EpisodeDesigns (engine/attacks/episodes.py) g.episode_designs EpisodeDesignMixin

A method keeps its name and moves to its part: g.benign_frame(X) is g.emitter.benign_frame(X), g.solve_flow_local(...) is g.false_state.solve_flow_local(...), and so on. GridBase and AttackMixin are gone; a part is an engine.base.Part. No method's code changed, and every IEEE timeline is byte for byte what it was.

  • Docs: a page that maps each claim of the package to the test that checks it (no change to the packages). docs/guides/verify.md, "Check the package yourself": the set-up, the command for one test and for all, what each test needs, and what the tests do not show.

  • One source and one set of attack designs for every test system. The New York grid's own OPF designs and the source built around them leave the package; the New York case stays, as a test system of the one source, SearchSource.

Removed In its place generation.newyork (NewYorkSource, SingleEpisodeSource), models.config.NewYorkSettings, NewYorkRelease SearchSource.for_pool(net, pool, settings) with TimelineSettings engine.attacks.opf, interface (InterfaceFdia), attacker (Attacker), ramp (Ramp), systems.interfaces the search-based ramp and overload, on any case sensing.meters.plan_meters (meters by ownership, the smallest PMU set) MeterPlan.from_coverage; with own= each meter belongs to the client of its bus data.pool.peak_ratings, Case.with_voltage_margin, the constants BASEPOINT_BAND, Q_SHARE, RELEASE_INTERFACE, NEW_YORK_FAMILIES nothing: only the removed designs used them the two timeline build scripts of pipelines/newyork/ SearchSource.for_pool(...).generate(path)

New on SearchSource and for_pool (IeeeSource takes families= too): - families={"At": MyFamily()} runs a design family of your own (AttackFamily) in place of the search family of that name; its episodes are placed, written and recorded like the package's own. - own=Ownership(...) gives each meter to the client of its bus and records the clients in the file, which then reads as one view per client (dataset.clients.Dataset). MeterPlan.from_masks takes the file's current form, so the client reader handles rectangular and polar files.

The file layout is unchanged: it still allows flows at both branch ends and currents as magnitude and angle, and the readers accept such files; the package's source writes from-end flows and rectangular currents. FdiaGenerator._meter is now use_plan. Every IEEE timeline is byte for byte what it was. A New York timeline is now what for_pool writes; the files of the removed source are no longer produced by this package. Counted code in fdia_graph: 8,976 to 7,625 lines.

  • The original generator reads a dispatched pool, and picks its targets on the grid's own buses. New setting loads of TimelineSettings (LoadRule): "scaled" (default) reads a bus's load and generation by the one factor a scaled pool applied to both, as before; "net" reads a pool solved by an OPF, where a bus with a unit is all generation and any other bus all load. The two rules are the classes ScaledSplit and NetSplit (engine/physics.py), and FdiaGenerator takes one as split. Case.own_bus marks the grid's own buses (every bus of an IEEE case, the 46 New York buses of the New York case); ramp targets, the units an overload may move and an overload's target branches are held to them, and Attacker reads the same mark where it read the meter plan's owners. SearchSource.for_pool(net, pool, settings) runs the original generator on a New York pool file. Removed: formulas.attacks.bus_load (now LoadSplit.load), FdiaGenerator.load_base and gen_base (now split.base_load, ScaledSplit.gen_base), Attacker.owner (now Attacker.own); formulas.attacks.operating_limits takes the pool's generator output in place of the pool and the base tables. Every IEEE timeline and every New York release timeline is byte for byte what it was; a file records loads only when it is not the default.

  • Docs: the six remaining wide diagrams are redrawn for a phone (no change to the packages). concepts_one_record, localization_flow, se_estimators, se_gated_prior, se_jacobian_weighting and trust_flow are now top to bottom, at most 8 nodes and 900 px wide, checked against the code, with alt texts that describe them. NOT_YET_REDRAWN in tools/prereview.py and the stylesheet's exempt list hold pipeline only. What changed in the pictures:

Diagram Change concepts_one_record shows the three layers and the labels of one record, with the function that makes each; the list of attack families is gone se_estimators the steps of SEBase and the step each estimator changes; the page cites ac_measurement in formulas/measurement.py, where it is se_jacobian_weighting the change is taken against the previous frame's estimate, as the code does, not against its clean state se_gated_prior adds the secured meters, which keep their weight; the gate is any fitted localizer localization_flow one chain from fit to score, in the order of the code trust_flow adds the alarm level, which fit calibrates before the selection

docs/concepts/solving.md has a new section, "Repeating a solve": how closely a New York pool repeats on the reference machine and on the Linux test runner, and what the test compares.

  • Docs: one guide for every test system, three tutorials and three new concept pages (no user-visible change to the packages). The New York grid no longer has pages of its own; it is a test system in the pages every system shares.
Kind Pages tutorials docs/getting-started/load.md, generate.md, analyse.md guides docs/guides/generation.md (rewritten), operating_points.md, extending.md, troubleshooting.md concepts docs/concepts/meters.md, attacks.md, layers.md

The five New York pages are removed and their content folded into the pages above, into docs/concepts/test_systems.md and into CONTRIBUTING.md (the New York tests and snapshots). The loading part of docs/reference/EXAMPLES.md is the load tutorial. The generation flow diagram is redrawn for every system, and the New York pipeline diagram is removed. NOT_YET_PLAIN in tools/prereview.py is empty: no docs page holds an internal decision code. Docstrings that cited a moved page cite its new place. The example examples/nygrid/custom_attack_family.py labels its episode with a family name of fg.FAMILIES ("Ad"; it was "Ab", which a timeline cannot write) and also designs through EpisodeFamily.designed, the call a timeline makes.

  • The original generator is built on a Network, and IeeeSource builds it for an IEEE case (every IEEE file is byte for byte the same, and so are the New York release's files). fdia_graph.generation.search.SearchSource(net, X, settings, seed, time) is the source IeeeSource was, on a Network and its pool; IeeeSource(system, states, settings, seed, time) is unchanged for callers.
Before Now the generator of an IEEE case FdiaGenerator(system, seed, meters, max_load_mw, plan) FdiaGenerator(Network.from_ieee(n), seed, meters, max_load_mw, plan) the generator of the New York grid FdiaGenerator.from_network(net, plan, seed, spec) FdiaGenerator(net, seed, plan=plan, spec=spec): the one constructor a source with no default path NewYorkSource refused generate() every source but IeeeSource refuses it: "a timeline needs the path of its file" a family the generator does not make refused when the source is built refused when the TimelineSettings are built, with the same message
  • FdiaGenerator.from_network is removed, with no alias, and FdiaGenerator(...) takes a Network where it took an IEEE system. Network.from_ieee(n) is the network of the IEEE case of n buses. GeneratorSpec.system is GeneratorSpec.net.

  • The original designs are built for a pool that scales each bus's load and generation by one factor (generate_states); they are not offered on the New York pool. The meter placement is not a setting: the search-based designs run on coverage meters and the New York release's designs on owned meters (docs/guides/generation.md).

  • How a timeline's splits are cut is a setting of every test system, split_by (the default of each is what it did before: the IEEE and New York files made without the setting are byte for byte the same). "time" cuts three blocks in time order, "week" draws whole weeks into the three splits.

Before Now an IEEE timeline three blocks in time order, always split_by="time" by default; fg.generate(..., split_by="week", time=times) cuts whole weeks a New York timeline NewYorkSettings.split_by, "week" by default the same setting, read by the shared step (TimelineSource.split_codes) a pool without time not asked split_by="week" is refused with the reason (ConfigError, declared on the model SplitRule) each frame's time (data/time) written by a New York file written by any file whose source has the frames' time an episode and a gap in time not asked (no IEEE file had time; the New York pool has no gap) with the frames' time, no episode is placed across a step that differs from the median step
  • fg.generate, generate_timeline and IeeeSource take time, each frame's time [T] (an IEEE pool stores none, so the caller passes it): numpy datetime64 values, one per frame, strictly increasing. Numbers, strings, Python datetime objects, timezone-aware times and NaT are refused when the source is built (SplitRule).
  • TimelineSettings.split_by is recorded in a file only when it is not "time", the value every file made before the setting meant (the rule WhenSet(legacy="time") of models.validation), so the recorded settings and their hash of those files are unchanged.

  • A split by weeks does not check that every split gets a week: a pool of fewer weeks than splits leaves a split empty, as the New York days' pool of the tests does.

  • The pool-building step takes one solve setting, SolveSettings(method, engine), for every test system (the default of each builder is what it did before: the IEEE and New York pools built without the setting are byte for byte the same). method is "power_flow" or "opf", engine is "pandapower" or "ipopt". generate_states(..., solve=SolveSettings("opf", "ipopt")) builds an IEEE pool by a least-cost AC OPF per step (the case's limits and its own cost curve, linear and quadratic), in either engine; the pool is the same for any number of workers, and a case with no optimum at any step raises DataConditionError. PoolBuilder.from_settings(case, loads, dispatch, renew, ramp, solve=None) builds the New York pool; it refuses a power flow and pandapower's OPF with the reason (ConfigError, declared on the model NewYorkSolve), and SolveSettings refuses a power flow in Ipopt. docs/concepts/solving.md has the table.

  • The two engines are classes of one interface, fdia_graph.data.solver.Solver: fdia_graph.data.ipopt_solver.IpoptSolver (the package's OPF, with Compensation) and fdia_graph.data.pandapower_solver.PandapowerSolver (the power flow, and pandapower's OPF). Both have opf(pd, qd, costs), and a solve returns an OperatingPoint or, from an OPF, an OpfPoint (fdia_graph.models.grid), read by attribute or as the dict it was.
  • AcSolver is removed, with no alias. Its project and dispatch are IpoptSolver's, its power_flow and net are PandapowerSolver's.
  • PandapowerSolver.net carries the case's bus shunts and each branch's shunt conductance (as bus shunts), where AcSolver.net carried neither. Both are zero on the New York case, so its net is the same.
  • A power flow given no start now starts flat where it started from a DC solution; the pool build always gives a start. power_flow and opf return None only when pandapower reports no convergence; any other error is raised.
  • Case.pandapower_costs(net) reads each unit's linear and quadratic cost from a pandapower net into a UnitCosts (fdia_graph.models.inputs); the constant term is not read.

  • tests/nygrid/test_solve_engines.py compares the two OPF engines on IEEE-14, 30 and 118 and on the New York case: the cost agrees within 0.01 % and every unit within 0.1 MW.

  • The load data and the operating points get their own package, fdia_graph.data; the folder generation/nygrid/ and the module profiles.py are gone (a move: no function or class changes, and no file changes: thirty IEEE timelines are byte for byte the files the previous code writes, and the five New York digests are unchanged). fg.generate_states, fg.load_profile and fg.fetch_profile are called as before. A module imported by its old path is imported by its new one; no old path is kept.

New York is a test system like an IEEE case, so no folder holds "the New York code". What was in generation/nygrid/ is three general things: where the load data comes from and how the operating points are solved (data/, for every test system), a fact about the grid (its interfaces, systems/) and the grid as a timeline source (generation/newyork.py, beside generation/ieee.py). The imports point one way: constants, models, formulas, systems, sensing, data, then engine, generation and dataset. data imports nothing of engine, generation or dataset, and systems and sensing nothing of data (tests/test_models_package.py).

Before Now fdia_graph.profiles: load_profile, fetch_profile, LoadSource, RawSeries, CsvColumn, IsoFolder, LoadFeed, NyisoArchive, GridstatusFeed, nyiso_pal_month, nyiso_zone_load fdia_graph.data.profiles fdia_graph.profiles: generate_states, K_DEFAULT, SIGMA_DEFAULT, CLIP_DEFAULT fdia_graph.data.ieee_pool fdia_graph.generation.nygrid.config (Settings, rng, stream_key) fdia_graph.data.config fdia_graph.generation.nygrid.inputs fdia_graph.data.inputs fdia_graph.generation.nygrid.load_sources fdia_graph.data.load_sources fdia_graph.generation.nygrid.loads fdia_graph.data.loads fdia_graph.generation.nygrid.dispatch fdia_graph.data.dispatch fdia_graph.generation.nygrid.solver (AcSolver) fdia_graph.data.solver fdia_graph.generation.nygrid.pool (Pool, PoolBuilder, peak_ratings) fdia_graph.data.pool fdia_graph.generation.nygrid.io (read_pool, write_pool) fdia_graph.data.pool fdia_graph.engine.solvers (ipopt) fdia_graph.data.ipopt fdia_graph.generation.nygrid.interfaces (Interface, hourly_interfaces) fdia_graph.systems.interfaces fdia_graph.generation.nygrid.source (NewYorkSource, SingleEpisodeSource, PoolDesigner, Survey) fdia_graph.generation.newyork the packaged generation/nygrid/ny_bus_locations.csv data/ny_bus_locations.csv

engine.solvers moved because the pool's solver (data/solver.py) and the attack OPFs (engine/attacks/) both run on it, and data may not import engine. A pool file is read by its path, so an existing pool.h5 reads as before. The survey cache keeps its _v2 chunks: a chunk pickles models.plan.Episode with numbers and text, and no pickled class moved. The rules of the New York modules not yet under the SDK's gates were a notes file inside the package (since deleted).

  • One path generates a timeline on any grid, and New York adopts the original generator's noise, walk and move rule (a New York file changes; an IEEE file does not: the two IEEE digests are unchanged, and thirty-two IEEE timelines are byte for byte the files the previous code writes). fg.generate, generate_timeline, IeeeSource(system, states, settings, seed) and NewYorkSource(pool, attacker, families, own, settings, build) are called as before.

The steps are written once, in TimelineSource (generation/source.py): opening the file, the truth layers, cutting the splits, placing, the design stage with its moves, the walk and finishing the file. A source is built from a generator over its grid, its pool, the designer of its attack families, its settings, the names of the families it places and a seed (TimelineSource(g, X, designer, settings, placed, seed)); IeeeSource and NewYorkSource build those and say only what is their own.

"Design an attack for this window" has one shape. A family is an EpisodeFamily (engine/attacks/family.py) with one method, designed(onset, X, rng): the episode over the window of true states X [L, N, 4], or None. What it returns is a DesignedEpisode, which the walk emits by one loop (begin, a frame per scan, record). The original search designs are the families SearchRamp and SearchOverload (engine/attacks/search.py: each scan re-solved, with the same random draws in the same order; a ramp is still designed as the walk reaches it, now inside RampEpisode.begin), and a New York family (AttackFamily, unchanged for those who write one: design(window, rng) gives an Episode) yields a VectorEpisode, the true scan plus the episode's row of its stored attack vector. A source's Designer (generation/design.py) holds the families and the processes their designs run on: SearchDesigner on an IEEE pool, PoolDesigner on the New York pool.

Before Now the noise of a New York frame one stream (rng(build, "noise")) run over the frames in time order the frame's own stream, keyed (seed, JITTER_STREAM, pool frame), as on an IEEE timeline: the benign scans do not depend on the attacks placed, and one pool frame reads the same in a timeline and in a single-episode file a New York frame under an episode float32(z_benign + a) from the float64 benign scan the stored float32 benign scan plus a, as an IEEE attacked frame is built (FdiaGenerator.frame_from_vector) how New York frames are written NewYorkSource._write_block, block frames at a time (NewYorkSettings.block) frame by frame, by the walk every timeline uses;   • Constructors take settings models. Estimators, localizers, federated localizers and trust selectors take their models.config settings (SolveConfig, PriorConfig, LearnedConfig, FederatedSettings, TrustConfig, DqnConfig, ...) instead of flat keywords.

  • The New York grid's study scripts and design log leave the repository. pipelines/newyork keeps the build tools (run_pool.py, build_timeline.py, build_single_episodes.py, matlab/); the study drivers, their result files under results/ and the design log are removed. The library, its defaults and its outputs are unchanged.

  • An Ipopt that ends abnormally is a failed solve (New York grid). OperatorOpf.solve returns None when Ipopt does not exit normally (killed, out of memory), so the AC operator retries from the AC point instead of ending the study that ran it.

  • The AC operator solves its relief only where an interface binds (New York grid). AcSced.step solves the dispatch without interface limits (for relief_usd) only when an interface row binds, the only case where it can differ, with the commitment the dispatch used (it allowed every quick-start unit, so a congestion-free scan could show relief) and without moving the next scan's starting point. A scan that moves without congestion takes one solve, not two; relief_usd under the AC operator changes, the other numbers do not.

  • The AC operator holds the units' voltage schedule (New York grid). AcSced now holds each unit bus's voltage near the AC point's (V_WEIGHT, the OperatorOpf voltage term), as the true grid's power flow holds it. Its voltages were free, so under least movement its model flows could part from the true grid's and the closed loop read that gap as a flow to relieve: one benign day of 24 moved a median of 224 MW. With it the benign twin holds on all 24 (ac and ac_cost) and the least-cost results change by at most 1 MW of transfer on the three days rechecked; least-movement results from the earlier code change and are rerun.

  • An AC operator (New York grid). OperatorPolicy(dispatch="ac") and dispatch="ac_cost" run the operator's dispatch as an AC optimal power flow each scan (AcSced, Pyomo and Ipopt, OperatorOpf): the loads it reads (the true loads plus what the attack changed in its New York injection meters; the accounting operator adds the false interchange back over New York's loads by their size), the units within the pool's own bounds (PoolFrames, pool_frames, PoolBuilder.frame_limits) and their five-minute ramps from its previous dispatch, hydro and external units under the pool's anchor, bus voltage and reactive limits, the four interfaces' AC flows within their limits, and the shed, shortage and balance prices of DcSced. ac moves the least generation; ac_cost clears at least cost and prices every bus at its AC balance dual (Twin.price). Its benign twin stays at the AC points (both solve the pool's problem). The closed loop re-solves on what the operator reads after its own dispatch (true AC flows less its AC model), not on shift factors, the N-1 screen is an AC power flow per outage (TrueGrid(day, ac=True), ac_power_flow), shedding and the zone levers use AC sensitivities (ac_shift). The DC dispatches and their results are unchanged.

  • A least-cost dispatch that keeps the AC operating points (New York grid). DcSced(objective="cost_lf") and OperatorPolicy(dispatch="cost_lf") (--dispatch cost_lf on every study tool) run the market dispatch around the AC operating point, as an RTO's incremental dispatch is: each unit's cost counts per MW delivered to the reference bus (loss_factors, the power flow Jacobian's delivery factors at the frame's true AC state), the balance is written on the delivered change, the first scan ramps from the basepoint, offline quick-start units start only when the committed units leave a constraint unmet, and the AC point's implied values (DcSced.implied: the least bus and unit adders that make the AC point this model's least-cost dispatch) carry what the AC dispatch priced and the DC model does not see. The plain least-cost dispatch moves its benign twin 1.2 to 4.1 GW off the AC points on at-limit days; this one keeps it there. Each run now reports every bus's price (Twin.price, DcSced.prices), and area_damage's payments use it. The movement and cost dispatches are unchanged.

  • Shunt compensation and reactive limits as a sensitivity (New York grid). AcSolver(case, compensation=...) takes a Compensation: switched shunt banks the dispatch sets frame by frame, a generator voltage schedule held by a penalty, an operating voltage band and unit reactive limits (unit_q_limits, power factor 0.85 lagging and 0.95 leading on Pmax where NYgrid left plus or minus 9999 MVAr). PoolBuilder applies its limits and records each bank's output (shunt_q), which enters the power flow and the pool's injections. Without a Compensation the model, the pool and every released file are unchanged.

  • Overruns counted against the benign twin (New York grid). summarize's over_scans, over_run_scans, over_mwh and over_iface now count only the scans on which the attacked run is further over a true interface limit than its benign twin, and that excess energy. The least-cost dispatch holds a binding interface at its shift-factor limit, so its true flow can pass the limit with no attack, which the old counts charged to the attack. benign_margin_min_mw reports the benign twin's tightest margin. Results of the least-movement dispatch, whose benign twin never passed a limit, are unchanged.

  • The least-cost operator from the command line (New York grid). experiments.add_dispatch_argument (and add_study_arguments) declares --dispatch cost once for a driver that runs the operator. The default stays the least-movement dispatch, so every existing result is unchanged.

  • Market prices that a market could set (New York grid). The least-cost dispatch (DcSced(objective="cost")) now prices the flow it leaves over an interface on the 2019 transmission shortage curve (350, 1,175 and 4,000 $/MWh, SHORTAGE) and load it cannot match at the energy offer cap (ENERGY_CAP, 1,000 $/MWh), instead of the least-movement dispatch's slack weight of 10^6. A shadow price no longer reaches the slack weight on a congested day, so the load payments area_damage reports stay at prices a market could set. The default dispatch is unchanged.

  • A least-cost dispatch with prices, and the idealized operator (New York grid). DcSced(objective="cost") and OperatorPolicy(dispatch="cost") dispatch as a market clears, each MW moved charged MOVE_USD, and report each interface's shadow price and the energy price (Step.congestion, Step.energy, and per scan on Twin). Under it area_damage prices what each zone's and utility's load pays at the moved prices (payments_usd). The default least-movement dispatch is unchanged: every golden value holds, and the operator snapshots gain only the two new arrays, empty under it.

  • Who bears an attack's damage (New York grid). New fdia_graph.nyfed.operator.areas: area_damage splits an operator run, attacked less benign, by New York zone, by utility and by neighboring area. Each zone and utility gets the energy its units lose, the fuel saved and the sales lost at the zone's real price, the load shed, and the transfer cut into it and margin lost on the interfaces that feed it (FEEDS). Each neighbor gets the inadvertent interchange it supplied, priced at its NYISO proxy bus (PROXY, neighbor_prices), and the system row gives the attack's net cost once the borrowed energy is priced. attack_surface counts the meters an attack tampers per zone and utility, and zone_levers measures how far each zone's plausible false load and output could move each interface. node_lbmp reads NYISO's hourly price at any zone or proxy bus. No change to existing results.

  • The New York grid's tests run in CI (New York grid). A new workflow, nyfed.yml, installs the [ny] extra and Ipopt from conda-forge, downloads NYgrid's public inputs with fetch_inputs (cached under the pinned commit) and runs tests/nygrid on pull requests that touch the New York grid, on main and weekly. Before it, no CI job installed Pyomo, so the whole folder, the examples' test included, was left out of every run. Two damage-study days, the single-episode day and the 2019 pool's frames of those days are checked in under tests/nygrid/data/days (6.7 MB), so the operator's tests and 33 of the 35 golden snapshots run there too; the tests that need the whole pool (the attack families, the builder, the timeline and the interface attack's design) still run only where it is built. tests/nygrid/inputs.py names every input in one place and says which tests it lets run, in place of a path block repeated in nine test files. No user-visible change.

  • Docs to read the New York grid by, and to extend it (New York grid). docs/getting-started/new_york_walkthrough.md follows one attack through every stage with the call that does each step (each snippet checked on the 2019 data); docs/guides/extending_new_york.md names the extension points (an attack family, an alarm rule, an operator, a study), each with a runnable example under examples/nygrid/ that CI runs; docs/concepts/new_york_grid.md opens with a rendered diagram of the stages and its principles as they now hold, in place of an ASCII diagram that predated the operator and the detectors.

  • The load model in one module per job (New York grid). scenario/loads.py (676 lines) keeps LoadSeries, LoadModel and its constants; the downloads and readers of its inputs move to load_sources.py, the fit of its within-hour constants to load_fit.py (public as fluctuation_fit and switching_fit, for refitting them), and the validation measures to load_metrics.py. The code moved as it was.

  • Study helpers, and the research tools as thin drivers (New York grid). New fdia_graph.nyfed.experiments: study_days (a study's day files), variant (at the limit or damaging), load_calib (the interchange check's calibration), add_study_arguments (the options every tool shares) and run_parallel (a process pool that writes the CSV as results come in, sorted by file at the end, so its rows no longer depend on which worker finished first). The study tools under pipelines/newyork/ use them in place of their own copies, and the interchange-check tool takes --data instead of a fixed path. The tools' results are unchanged.

  • The overload attacks read plainly (New York grid). The OPF attack's per-support model and prepared window are named records (_OpfModel, _Prepared) instead of tuples unpacked by position; the interface attack keeps its per-support state on that model rather than writing it onto the shared window; windows are built by keyword; and the unused OpfFdia.reachable is gone. Each class's docstring now says which step of the search it replaces (MsFdia the target choice and support search, OpfFdia the solve, InterfaceFdia the goal and the design). Attack designs are unchanged; OpfFdia.reachable, which nothing called, is no longer available.

  • The operator's choices as one record, and an operator interface (New York grid). OperatorPolicy holds mode, delay, over, entry, closed_loop and after, each checked when the record is built (OperatorMode, AlarmAnswer and Entry name the allowed values); respond(day, policy=...) takes one, and its keywords still build one, so existing calls are unchanged. Operator is the protocol a partner's operator implements (return a Response and summarize works on it), and NyisoOperator(policy) is this package's.

  • The operator in one module per job (New York grid). fdia_graph.nyfed.operator.response (730 lines) is split into day (reading an attacked day), ties (the interchange check), truegrid (the AC power flows on the true grid), policy (the operator's choices), run (the scan-by-scan loop) and summary (its consequence), the code moved as it was. response re-exports every name, so existing imports keep working. The interchange check's alarm is public as interchange_alarm.

  • Detection as building blocks (New York grid). New fdia_graph.nyfed.detect: the residual test's AC weighted least squares (wls, returning a WlsFit that says whether it converged), the noise-free fit of a state (exact_state), the persistence rule with its calibration (PersistenceRule, PersistenceRule.fit) behind an AlarmRule protocol any other rule can implement, and other meter fleets (with_fleet, fleet_bias). TrueGrid.state and TrueGrid.run_state give the true state after the operator acts, with the load it shed (the research tools left the shed load out; no studied day sheds load, so no number changes). The six detection tools under pipelines/newyork/ now drive these instead of carrying their own copies and importing each other.

  • Settings are arguments, not patches (New York grid). production_builder takes v_margin and gen_v_tol, the attacker's voltage sensitivities (N71, N75); v_margin widens the limits on the attacker's own copy of the case (Case.with_voltage_margin). Before, the damage study widened the shared case's arrays in place, so a timeline written from that builder recorded the widened limits. InterfaceFdia.with_overshoot returns a variant as a copy, and max_overshoot searches on one, instead of swapping overshoot in and out; build_episode(using=...) designs with such a variant. hourly_dispatch(hold_externals=False) replaces the AC ablation's monkeypatch.

  • A public surface for the New York grid. Every fdia_graph.nyfed package (grid, scenario, sensing, attacks, timeline, operator, and fdia_graph.nyfed itself) now has a docstring that says what its stage does, what goes in and comes out, and how it fails, and an __all__ of its public names, loaded on first use (reading a dataset still never imports pandapower or Pyomo). Helpers the research tools reached into became public: operator.response.TrueGrid and entry_share (the old private names _TrueGrid and _entry_share are gone), Attacker.absorb and TimelineBuilder.episode_lengths.

  • Named errors and a troubleshooting page (New York grid). fdia_graph.nyfed raises the SDK's named errors: ConfigError for a wrong argument, DataConditionError (or NoAdmissibleTarget, NotFitted) for data that does not meet a condition, instead of bare ValueErrors and asserts. Both subclass ValueError, so existing handlers keep working. The input CSV tables are read through one reader that closes them (fdia_graph.nyfed.tables), and the research tools no longer silence warnings. docs/guides/troubleshooting_new_york.md lists what each stage reports when it fails and what to do.

  • A failed power flow reads as unknown, not safe (New York grid). The operator's Twin gains pf_failed [T], the scans whose AC power flow on the true grid failed, and summarize reports pf_failed_scans and pf_failed_benign_scans. Before, those scans' NaN margins counted as within the limit with no trace. respond now rejects an unknown after (before, a typo ran as an operator that never answers the alarm), and an unknown mode, after or entry raises fdia_graph.errors.ConfigError (a ValueError, as before).

  • Why a design found no attack (New York grid). AttackFamily.design_explained returns the episode or the reason there is none (one of fdia_graph.nyfed.attacks.episode.MISSES: no_target, infeasible, solver_error), also kept in last_miss, and TimelineBuilder.build reports missed and, with the onset survey, survey_missed: the count of each reason per family. build_episode's error names the reason. Before, a timeline with few attacks gave no way to tell an empty window from a failing solver.

  • A missing solver now says so (New York grid). fdia_graph.nyfed.solvers.ipopt finds Ipopt in the environment, checks that it starts, and raises the new fdia_graph.errors.SolverUnavailable with the fix when it does not. Before, an Ipopt that could not start (a missing DLL, exit code 0xC0000135) made every attack design read as infeasible, so a timeline built with no overload attacks and no error. The attack OPF now reads only an abnormal stop on its own model as an infeasible support, and counts those in solver_errors.

  • Answering a residual alarm (New York grid). respond(after=...) models the operator's response to an alarm (switch to the benign scans, freeze with the AGC on the falsified ties, freeze with it on the common source) (N78).

  • The residual test with the meters' noise (New York grid). respond(alarm_at=...) models an operator that falls back at the first residual alarm (N77).

  • The closed loop (New York grid). respond(closed_loop=True) has the operator read the true flows after its dispatch (N76).

  • Voltage checks and the overload record (New York grid). production_builder(gen_v_tol=...) holds generator voltages near their schedule (N75), and summarize reports how long an interface stays past its true limit.

  • Entry patterns and many meter fleets (New York grid). respond(entry=...) chooses where the inadvertent interchange enters (N72).

  • Where the inadvertent interchange lands, and the certificate's reach (New York grid). The shortfall the trusting operator leaves is now taken up by the synchronous units outside New York in proportion to their capacity rather than by the reference bus, and every scan reports the tightest true interface margin (margin, summary margin_min_mw and margin_lost_mw) (N69). production_builder(v_margin=...) widens the attacker's voltage limits (N71). A failed power flow now leaves the margin unknown.

  • Three operators and a calibrated interchange check (New York grid). respond(mode=...) runs the trusting operator, whose AGC reads the falsified New York-end tie meters, the accounting operator, which takes its load and ACE from the agreed interchange (BAL-005), and the oracle upper bound (N66; replaces defended). The neighbours' tie meters carry their own accuracy-class noise (neighbour_reads); respond(calib=...) takes the alarm's calibration (N67). The consistent attacker's area stays inside New York. The target interface comes first, the shed clock runs per interface, and the oracle falls back at decision time.

  • The interchange-consistent attacker and the interchange check (New York grid). Attacker(hold_external=True) (and production_builder(..., hold_external=True)) keeps every bus outside New York at its true injection, so the attack cannot move New York's net interchange (N62). The operator gets the matching check, tie_gap: the interchange read at the New York ends of the ties less what the neighbours meter. respond(..., defended=True) stops acting on the tampered scans from the first alarm (N65). The operator now enforces all four mapped interfaces, each with its own 15-minute clock and shortage price. It may start the quick-start units of zones J and K, and it caps regulation at 275 MW, reporting the rest as an ACE excursion (N63, N64). Shed load takes its reactive demand with it, and a reused day keeps its meter count.

  • The damaging attack and the operator's escalation (New York grid). InterfaceFdia(overshoot=...) takes the reported interface flow past its limit, designed under every bound as a real attack, and max_overshoot finds the largest overshoot an onset allows by bisection (N58). The operator now escalates as NYISO's emergency procedures do (N59): redispatch first, the flow it cannot relieve priced at the 2019 transmission shortage curve (shortage_usd, N60), and load relief after 15 minutes over the limit at the buses where shedding relieves the interface. Step carries the shed load and the cost of relieving the interface.

  • The grid operator under attack (fdia_graph.nyfed.operator). DcSced is the operator's real-time dispatch on what it sees: a DC dispatch on shift factors around the pool basepoint, with unit limits, five-minute ramps from its previous dispatch and the interface limit (the benign model flow plus the hour's real 2019 headroom). It moves as little as it must, then at least cost. respond(day, delay, over) runs it on a day's attacked scans and on their benign twin, in closed loop on the dispatch. The true load never changed, so regulation picks up the generation the dispatch removed, and an AC power flow gives the true interface flow and the worst single 345 kV outage. summarize reports the attack's consequence, attacked less benign: dispatch moved, regulation (MW, MWh, by utility), unrelieved flow, the true interface and N-1 changes, production cost and the energy settled at the real zonal LBMP (N50 to N57).

An action trusts one more PMU at the next configuration step (Sec. IV-D2, "one PMU per step"); the reward is the rise in the fewest-tamper search's cost under the schedule so far (eq. 33 per step, eqs. 28-32), in measurements by default or devices (WuDefenseConfig.unit, new choice CostUnit, the plan's E3); the state is what Fig. 1 lists, the node and flow readings at the step's snapshot, the target lines' load rate and the trusted mask.   • [WU26]'s own attack construction as the overload attack's support method (OverloadSettings.support_method, "search" by default or "rref"; new choice SupportMethod, FrameKnobs.support_method, file attribute support_method). The paper states it twice: the attacker "can utilize the transpose of the measurement matrix h, applying multiple elementary row transformations and column exchanges to find the optimal attack vector solution [25]" (p. 655, [YAN17]), and Solution 1's steps 1-5 (p. 657). New formulas.trust.sparsest_rows (the reduction, the column exchanges with their tracking order, the rows mapped back) and engine.attacks.rref.RrefMixin.rref_support: at each snapshot the Jacobian of the attack area's attackable channels (scaled by [WU26]'s noise, a trusted PMU's bus left out, eqs. 27 and 29) with respect to |V| and angle, for each target line the sparsest row whose state change moves its flow, the window's support the union over the snapshots (eq. 28), the magnitudes from the AC local flow solve so the goal, the limits and the D16 bounds hold. Ours: the chase starts from the transpose's own rows (the single-variable attacks), it chases the sparsest goal-moving row rather than the sparsest outright, and a support that cannot reach the goal grows by the next sparsest rows. On [WU26]'s scenarios the search matches Table II better: at k = 1.1 the trust schedule raises the search's devices 20% and 29% (the paper 24% to 35%) and the reduction's -14% and +13%; on IEEE-118 the search's devices rise 20% (the paper 16.4% mean) and the reduction's fall. The reduction is 0.5 to 0.8 s per 20-snapshot IEEE-14 window against the exhaustive search's 16 to 33 s, and 2.4 to 3.2 s per 10-snapshot IEEE-118 window against 2.8 to 9.6 s at budget 256. [WU26]'s reference now lists the paper's authors and pages (S. Wu, Q. Wang, J. Hu, Y. Ye, Y. Tang; pp. 651-665).

Its products are too small for threads to pay: on a many-core machine starting them cost more than the arithmetic. The limit is process-wide: while any search runs, other BLAS work in the process is on one thread too, and overlapping searches share one limit, so the caller's setting comes back when the last of them leaves. Under either meter model the search charges an angle channel only at a PMU bus. (3)] at the far end of every PMU-metered branch fill the |V| and angle slots no meter reads, weighted in the measured calibration by their first-order propagated variance (formulas.estimation.pmu_pseudo_links, pmu_pseudo_voltages). New models MeterModel, CurrentColumns, CurrentIndex, CURRENT, PmuCurrentFields, PseudoLinks and PseudoVoltages; AttackVector is a named tuple with an optional current. The v0.8.3 recipe and the strict frozen suite are bit-exact.

  • The documentation states what the stealthy families take from [WU26]: its constraints (13)-(18) and (21)-(23) (the SCADA measurements, the PMU voltage magnitudes and angles, and the operating limits; and, in new generation, whose PMUs read branch currents, the current phasors (19)-(20) as well). New generation also solves its objective, eq. (12), for At and Am, and Am is its overload attack (below); the released files' Aq, Al and Am drew their targets at random and drove no line to its limit.
  • New generation makes the multi-snapshot families of [WU26], At and Am, both on the fewest-tamper search (docs/plans/WU_MSFDIA_PLAN.md, decisions D2 and D6): generate_timeline and fg.generate default to families=("At", "Am"), min_tamper=True and am_attack="overload". Am is the overload attack of [WU26, eqs. 24-25]: a rated branch whose flow is metered and whose true flow stays below its rating over the window is driven, snapshot by snapshot, until the flow the tampered measurements carry before noise reaches the rating, on the support that tampers the fewest devices. An episode tries at most eight eligible branches in a random order (each try is a full search), a bounded heuristic: when none of them admits an attack the episode stays benign and is counted. Each snapshot's false state frees the attackable loads of the support and holds every other bus's injection, the least-norm voltage change that meets the flow (formulas.network.local_flow_solve, FalseStateMixin.solve_flow_local). The ratings are the rate_a of the PGLib-OPF v23.07 versions of IEEE-14, 118 and 300 (CC BY 4.0), stored in fdia_graph.ratings and matched to the branches by their end buses (formulas.attacks.branch_ratings, OverloadMixin.line_ratings); pandapower rates every branch 9,900 MVA, the "no limit" placeholder. Other cases refuse Am with the new named error NoLineRatings. Each overload episode writes its branch, rating, reached noiseless flow and emitted flow under episodes/ (am_*); new models FlowGoal and AmOverloadDesign; new knob stealth_scale (a multiplier on the stealth bound, 1 by default; At's alone since D11). Am's tamper count (and, until D11, its stealth bound) use [WU26]'s own case-study noise, 0.03 pu on SCADA channels and 0.01 pu on PMU channels in the stored units (formulas.noise.WU26_NOISE, paper_sigma; the plan's D8), while At keeps the meters' rated accuracy (D7). Snapshot t's goal is the true flow plus a linear share of what separates the window's last true flow from the rating (D9), so the attack rides on the load's own drift instead of cancelling it and reaches the rating at the last snapshot. Generating Aq, Ad, As, Ar or Al warns (DeprecationWarning) and is refused from 0.22; released files holding them load unchanged. timeline.LEGACY_FAMILIES with am_attack="redistribution" and min_tamper=False reproduces data release v0.8.3 (its build script and the frozen test timeline use it; the strict frozen suite is bit-exact). Under the meters' rated accuracy (D7) no overload window was stealthy, since moving one line's flow moves the injections and flows around its ends by several times that change, beyond the rated accuracy of the small loads there. The reported noiseless flow reaches the rating exactly.
  • The fewest-tamper search of [WU26, eq. 12], behind generate_timeline(min_tamper=True) (on for new generation; min_tamper=False walks the released files' recipe). Each At episode is held on the support (the buses its false state moves) that tampers the fewest devices over the episode, a device being one SCADA terminal or one PMU per bus and a change under a meter's accuracy-class sigma not counted. A support is held for the whole episode and must solve at every snapshot inside the operating limits and move no metered channel by more than its accuracy-class sigma from one snapshot to the next, the first snapshot measured from the frame before the episode (its attack vector when that frame was attacked, since episodes may be adjacent). The search solves candidate supports in the attacker's area smallest first, each closed over the zero-injection buses of its boundary, starting from the region the episode was accepted on; a local solve that does not converge proves nothing, so those candidates are counted (min_unsolved) and the optimum over held supports is claimed only among converged solves, when it exhausts the area or reaches the devices the goal forces above their accuracy-class sigma, settles after min_budget candidates otherwise, and treats a support moving no device beyond its sigma as no attack, and records min_devices = -1 when no held support meets every constraint (the episode then runs on its region). Each search is written under episodes/ (min_support_*, min_devices, min_unsolved, min_channels, min_proven, min_evaluated, min_lower_bound). New formulas formulas.noise.jitter_sigma (the emitter's per-scan noise rule, emission only) and accuracy_sigma (a meter's rated accuracy at a reading, the measured calibration's rule through accuracy_class_sigma, what the search counts against), formulas.attacks.tampered_channels and tampered_devices; new models LoadGoal and MinimizerResult; MeasurementMixin.meter_masks gives the masks without a random draw.

This code was spread over engine/records.py, engine/physics.py, engine/attacks.py and timeline.py; records now emits a benign scan and hands an attacked family to the mixin, and timeline decides when and where each episode runs. No user-visible change: the generated files are bit for bit the same. The public names keep their old import paths; a moved private name (such as engine.records._stealthy_frame or timeline._AmShape) still imports from its old module with a DeprecationWarning naming its new home, until 0.22.

Each consumer's settings are one model in fdia_graph.models.config (LoadOptions, WindowSpec, HuberConfig, PriorConfig, LearnedConfig, FederatedSettings, TimelineKnobs and the rest), whose fields declare their rules (Annotated[float, Positive()], OneOf(Units)); one engine, models.validation, checks them when the model is built. A profile date is a 'YYYY-MM-DD' string, a date or a datetime on every Python version (from 3.11 '20240131' and the integer 20240131 used to parse too). load_profile refuses a source that is not a LoadSource, an operator name, a CSV path or a 1-d series of loads (a scalar used to pass as a one-point profile); generate's states must be an array or a path; and export(fields=...) takes a list or tuple of names, so a lone string, a mapping or a set is a ConfigError. A value no model can even read (a number past the float range, a mapping where a sequence belongs) is a ConfigError, never a raw OverflowError, KeyError or AttributeError; tests/test_malformed_inputs.py sweeps every config and input model with values of the wrong kind and the public entry points with one bad argument each. SEBase.fit(ds, calibrate="measured") sets every meter's sigma from its accuracy class (formulas.estimation.accuracy_class_sigma, the classes now one definition, engine.base.ACCURACY_CLASS, shared with the noise model), takes the angle reference from the case and the linearization point from the mean estimate of the benign training scans, and reads no clean layer.   • Estimators, numbers change. ResidualRemoval is classical largest-normalized-residual removal: one meter per record per pass (the largest above the threshold), re-solved, until none exceeds it; a removal the observability guard refuses keeps that meter. It used to remove every meter above the threshold at once, taking out the honest neighbours a single gross error smears onto. Meter sigma (and the trust selectors' alarm level) is calibrated on benign records spread evenly over the train split instead of the first ones, which on a timeline are one early load regime.   • The local power flow of a stealthy frame is a damped Newton: each step is halved until the mismatch drops, the full step first, so every frame the plain method solved is bit-identical. A step the region still cannot absorb is halved (an Aq step at most three times and never under the noise floor, a ramp or Am frame at most six times) so the frame stays attacked at the largest step with a solution, an Al frame halves its redistribution and then redraws its line (up to forty), and an Aq, At or Am episode tests its design (the full step, the ramp's peak, the held redistribution's peak) on every frame it will occupy, each with the step that frame will carry (an Aq episode's whole span, every frame of the ramp and of the Am rise, plateau and return), and redraws it, up to forty times, when no stealthy state exists on any of them, so an accepted design cannot fall back, and a span with no admissible design stays benign and is counted; an Am redistribution is also tried at halved sizes above the floor before it is redrawn. A ramp or Am frame never carries a zero step (the profile's first frame and return leg floor at one rate), so every frame labelled attacked carries an attack. fallback_benign now counts every frame the draw meant to attack that is benign, whether or not an episode record exists for it (an Am episode with no admissible redistribution left no record and was not counted). An Aq episode now draws its direction like the ramp, a load rise or a load drop with the same 5% to 20% scale: on a case that runs below its voltage limits (IEEE-57) a rise near the low buses has no admissible state and a drop is the attack that fits. Loads above max_load_mw (new knob, default 2000 MW) are never targets: the IEEE-145 case lumps whole areas into loads of 4 to 58 GW, and a 5% step on one has no local solution, which left 30% of that system's attack frames benign; no other ladder system has a load above 1.1 GW, so their files do not change. fallback_benign is zero on every released file. Every false state also satisfies the security and operational constraints of Wu et al. 2026 (OperatingLimits, their equations 21 to 23): each bus voltage within the case's own limits (a bus the true state already holds outside a limit may not be made worse, IEEE-57 runs below its own minimum) and, for the generators of the attacked subnetwork as in the paper (a boundary bus is outside it, its voltage held true and its injection whatever balances the region), the implied output within its P and Q limits widened per bus to the range the benign pool ran it over (the pools scale generation with load and never enforced nameplate), the true output recovered exactly from the pool's common load and generation scale, and the pretended load change at a target bus not counted against its generator; a false state outside them is rejected and its step halved like an unsolvable one. The file records the widest bus limits as v_lo and v_hi.
  • A stealthy frame (Aq, At, Al, Am) is the true scan plus the attack vector a = h(x_false) - h(x_true) of its local false state: every meter keeps its own noise draw and the tampered meters are shifted by exactly what the false state moves them, so observed - benign is the attack for every family and a WLS residual test flags the stealthy families at the benign rate. Until now the tampered meters were re-emitted from the false state, which drew their noise from the false reading; where a boundary bus has a structurally zero injection (the IEEE-14 synchronous condenser's P, a zero-injection bus) that noise is several times what the estimator calibrates for the meter, and the residual test flagged about a third of the Aq, Al and Am frames on the full IEEE-14 timeline. An Al frame whose drawn target line has no feasible redistribution in its region redraws the line (up to ten) instead of falling back to a benign frame.
