The generator's measurement emission and the loader's admittance and clean-flow computations call them; the estimator's torch measurement function is pinned to them by a test, so the package has one AC model.

Readability series, steps 2 and 3 (docs/plans/READABILITY_PLAN.md): one attack frame for shards and streams, both generators split into named steps. No user-visible change: a seeded shard and a seeded stream are bit-identical to the previous release (tests/test_frozen.py, strict mode).

  • fdia_graph.engine.records: attack_frame builds one scan of any family from a stored operating point, for generate and generate_stream alike; FrameKnobs carries the two switches that differ between them; replay_frame and remember_benign name the replay policy.
  • generate and generate_stream are sequences of named draws and episodes; the swing scale, the temporal features and the ramp profile are functions with their source keys, shared by both.
  • Shard records are a named Record tuple and the writer reads them by field name; the writer is split into the attributes, graph, data and clean groups.
  • No public name changed. The private stream helper _swing_scale now lives in generation; streams._swing_scale stays as a deprecated alias that warns, removed one minor version later.

Readability series, step 1 (docs/plans/READABILITY_PLAN.md): the safety net. No user-visible change.

  • tests/test_frozen.py: a generated shard, a generated stream, and the estimator and localizer scores on the test shard are compared with frozen references (tests/frozen/): exactly in strict mode; otherwise arrays to 1e-7 relative and estimator and localizer scores to 1e-4 relative, the cross-platform tolerances the test module documents. tools/freeze_reference.py rewrites the references when a change to the generator or an estimator is intended.
  • tools/readability.py: the readability measures (complexity, nesting, closures, parameters, positional indexing) as a report over the package and as a gate on the functions a change touched; runs in CI.
  • docs/reference/FORMULAS.md and REFERENCES.md: the catalogue of formulas and their sources, with the docstring template every formula function follows.
  • docs/plans/READABILITY_PLAN.md, docs/plans/RESTRUCTURE_PLAN.md: the plans for the series.

• edge_clean_full: the exact clean power flow on every branch, computed on load from the clean state through the branch admittance matrix; in the record dict, PyG data, collate, to_numpy and the per-unit view.
• Per-record normal matrices are built by chunked matrix products instead of one einsum; the IEEE-300 estimators run in minutes instead of days. Same numbers.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
Other groups load these packages in their experiments, so the rules keep their numbers stable. Every rule is a command you can run.

The repository holds two toolkits, and every rule below covers both. The generation toolkit is the distribution fdia-graph, the package fdia_graph under src/, with its tests in tests/: it generates a timeline and loads it. The analysis toolkit is the distribution fdia-analysis, the package fdia_analysis under analysis/src/, with its tests in analysis/tests/ and its own analysis/pyproject.toml: state estimation, localization, federated training, trusted-meter selection and the results store's code. The dependency points one way: fdia_analysis imports fdia_graph, and nothing in fdia_graph imports fdia_analysis (tests/test_toolkit_boundary.py). A model or a formula the generator or the loader uses lives in fdia_graph (models/, formulas/); one only the analysis packages use lives in fdia_analysis; no name is exported by both.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/myersben9/fdia-graph
cd fdia-graph
pip install -e ".[generate,torch,dev]" -e "./analysis[se,federated]"   # both toolkits, from this checkout
pytest -n auto                                # both suites (tests, analysis/tests) in parallel (pytest-xdist,
                                              # in the dev and test extras); each worker builds its own tiny
                                              # timeline and pool download. Always from the repository root:
                                              # its conftest.py holds the fixtures of both suites

docs/concepts/flow.md is the map and the reading order; docs/reference/MODULES.md says what every file does.

Every diagram is a rendered image, never a Mermaid block: the README is also the PyPI page, and the docs are read in the GitHub mobile app, and neither renders Mermaid. Each diagram's source is a docs/figures/diagrams/<name>.mmd next to its <name>.png and <name>.svg; edit the source and re-render with python tools/render_mermaid.py docs/figures/diagrams/<name>.mmd (Playwright with Chromium), which writes both images, then commit all three. A hand-written flow diagram is drawn for a phone: the renderer uses 20 px type and the site's teal palette, and puts the diagram at its natural size on a white card 450 px wide with rounded corners, so the PNG (two device pixels per CSS pixel) is 900 px wide and reads on a dark page and on a light one. python tools/prereview.py fails a hand-written flow diagram that is not flowchart TB, has more than 8 nodes or has a PNG wider than 900 px, or names a node otherwise than name["label"]; the diagrams not yet redrawn are listed in NOT_YET_REDRAWN in tools/prereview.py. On the docs site docs/stylesheets/extra.css shows a phone diagram at most 450 px wide, and names the same exempt diagrams. The class and module diagrams of docs/reference/CLASS_MAP.md are generated: python tools/class_diagrams.py rewrites their sources from the code (CI fails when they are stale), then render them the same way; the renderer knows them by name (classes_*, modules), keeps them wide (Mermaid's default theme on a 1400 px page) and the gate exempts them. README images use the raw.githubusercontent.com URL so PyPI shows them; docs pages use relative paths.

The Models section of docs/reference/DATA_DICTIONARY.md is generated too: python tools/models_doc.py rewrites it from the dataclasses in the two models/ packages (src/fdia_graph/models/, analysis/src/fdia_analysis/models/) and the comment beside each field. Edit the comment in the source, never the section, and rerun the tool; the tests fail when it is stale.

The docs site is built from docs/ plus the three root pages by mkdocs.yml: the Vercel build serves the main branch at the custom domain, and .github/workflows/docs.yml deploys one copy per package version to GitHub Pages with mike (a tag push deploys that version as latest, a push to main deploys dev), so every release's docs stay readable after the next release; the version picker on each page switches between them. python tools/site_index.py && python -m mkdocs build --strict checks a docs change locally.

The pages are sorted by kind, one folder each (DOCS in tools/layout.py): tutorials in docs/getting-started/, tasks in docs/guides/, explanations in docs/concepts/, studies in docs/analysis/ and facts to look up in docs/reference/. python tools/prereview.py fails a page under docs/, or the README, that holds a fenced Mermaid block or an internal decision code (a capital N or D followed by one to three digits, as a word of its own); the pages not yet cleaned are listed in NOT_YET_PLAIN in tools/prereview.py, each with its reason. CHANGELOG.md is not read.

docs.title: The rules
docs.text:
rule means command nothing a user sees changes without a changelog entry public API, file formats, the numbers a timeline, estimator or localizer produces; a private name (a leading underscore) carries no promise and gets no alias when it moves CHANGELOG.md, ## Unreleased every change is proven behaviour-free, or its effect is measured the tests pin the fewest-tamper search's answers (tests/test_search_speed.py), [WU26]'s scenarios (tests/test_overload_case_studies.py), the formulas and models, and whole generated files: every dataset and attribute of an IEEE timeline against stored digests (tests/test_timeline_digests.py; bit for bit on the machine that recorded them, skipped elsewhere, tests/digests.py); a change that moves a generated number states the delta and rewrites the snapshot with FDIA_UPDATE_DIGESTS=1 pytest -W "error::DeprecationWarning:fdia_graph" tests code reads as its subject complexity 10, nesting 3, no closure captures, at most 7 parameters, no positional record indexing; every equation a named function in formulas/ with a source key; every returned bundle a model in models/ python tools/readability.py --report, --check --base origin/main an input is checked in one place a new argument is a field on its consumer's model in models/config.py, with its rules in the annotation (Annotated[float, Positive()], OneOf(<Choice>)) and cross-field rules in invariants(); a dataset precondition is a ds.require(...) capability; a condition only the data reveals raises a named error from errors.py; never a raise ValueError in a function body python tools/readability.py --check (refuses a new one) everything is typed every parameter, return and field carries its real type; an optional dependency's type (pandapower, torch, h5py, scipy, pandas) is imported under if TYPE_CHECKING: so the import stays lazy; Any only where the value can be anything, listed in ANY_ALLOWED in tools/readability.py with the reason python tools/readability.py --check (refuses an unlisted Any and a stale entry), pyright in CI typed, formatted, linted pyright at zero, ruff format and check clean pyright src/fdia_graph analysis/src/fdia_analysis, ruff format --check src/fdia_graph analysis/src/fdia_analysis conftest.py tests analysis/tests tools pipelines, ruff check src analysis/src conftest.py tests analysis/tests tools pipelines generated docs match the code the class and module diagram sources and the data dictionary's Models section python tools/class_diagrams.py --check, python tools/models_doc.py --check no measured number is typed into markdown a harness writes what it measures through fdia_analysis.results.run.Run into the results store (results/, see its README); a doc shows a number or a table through a results block (<!-- results: <query> ... -->, queries in results/queries.py), a CHANGELOG entry names the experiment; settings and published values from papers stay as text python tools/results_docs.py --write, --check; --lint lists typed decimals a file's name says what it does plain words: never its folder's name again (tests/nygrid/test_grid.py, not test_nygrid_grid.py), never a sibling's name plus a short ending (reduce.py beside reduced.py), no digit, no citation key or first author's surname from REFERENCES.md python tools/layout.py --check every file says what it does, and every page keeps up every Python file opens with a docstring whose first paragraph is its line in docs/reference/MODULES.md; every package has a page (PAGES in tools/layout.py) that names each of its modules; every module or name a doc or docstring cites in a code span exists; every folder at the root and under docs/ has its role in the tool's repository map python tools/layout.py writes the file map; --check in the pre-review and CI a constant has one home a value nothing in a run changes (a physical or regulatory fact, a column position, a code, a pinned input, a fitted number) is defined once in the generation toolkit's constants/ package, with its unit and source, or in schema.py when it is part of the file protocol; a value a user tunes is a field of a settings model in models/config.py; a module-level UPPER_CASE name anywhere else in fdia_graph is listed in EXEMPT in tools/layout.py with its reason, and fdia_analysis may add none to the ones EXEMPT_ANALYSIS lists python tools/layout.py --check speed is tracked per-record timings against the last row from this machine, 3x tolerance python tools/bench.py --check before a release, python tools/bench.py after

Docstrings are short, and say what the signature does not:

  • a module docstring is at most about 10 lines: what the module is for and where it fits, no history;
  • a class docstring is at most about 6 lines: what the class represents (a class whose docstring is the table of its attributes, as FdiaGenerator's, may be longer);
  • a function or method docstring is 1 to 3 lines (a few more when an equation or an argument table needs them): what it returns or does, the units, the equation with its source key, and the one thing a caller would not guess.

docs.title: The pull request
docs.text:
python tools/prereview.py                                      # every gate, locally, on this checkout's source
python tools/prereview.py --also-python <path-to-python3.12>  # and the suite on a second Python, as CI runs 3.9 and 3.12
python tools/pr.py create my-branch "One-line title" body.md   # a draft; body: what, why, what you checked
python tools/pr.py ready 80                                    # once clean: ready for the owner
python tools/pr.py wait 80                                     # until CI has finished
python tools/pr.py comments 80
python tools/pr.py reply 80 <comment-id> "what changed"
python tools/pr.py summary 80 summary.md                       # the four-sentence summary for the owner
python tools/pr.py merge 80                                    # refuses unless green

Green means: every job of the smoke workflow (tests, tests (3.9), tests (windows), typecheck, format, readability, the two installs) is a completed success on the head (a job that has not started yet counts as not green) and every other listed check has finished without failure. A pull request merges when it is green and the owner approves it. The repository runs no automated review. A pull request is opened as a draft while it is worked on and marked ready once it is clean. Related work goes in one pull request per theme rather than one per step, and an open pull request is rebased only for a real conflict. The order:

  1. python tools/prereview.py until it passes: the CI gates, the test suite, and the checks CI does not run (changelog, cited paths, vacuous tests, integer fields, rendered diagrams).
  2. The review checklist, docs/reference/REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md, against the diff and every touched file read whole, searching outward from every change (a /code-review in Claude Code with the checklist does this). Fold what it finds into the branch.
  3. Before the pull request leaves draft, one review of the diff by Claude Code review agents (no paid review service); its findings are fixed in one round, not looped, and its four-sentence summary of the change is posted on the pull request (tools/pr.py summary) for the owner.
  4. Mark the draft ready and merge it on green once the owner approves.

tools/pr.py uses the token the Git Credential Manager holds for git push, so it needs no gh CLI. Commit as yourself, with a message that says what the change does. If CI does not start on a push, check the account's Actions minutes first.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
The two toolkits are released together at one version: the root pyproject.toml, fdia_graph.__version__, analysis/pyproject.toml and fdia_analysis.__version__ say the same number, and fdia-analysis requires exactly fdia-graph==<version> (tests/test_versions.py; tools/release.py refuses a tag where it does not hold). The bump PR changes all five lines, and a tag vX.Y.Z publishes both distributions (publish.yml).

Before the first tag that publishes fdia-analysis, the project needs a pending trusted publisher on PyPI (pypi.org, Your account, Publishing: owner myersben9, repository fdia-graph, workflow publish.yml); without it the upload of fdia-analysis is refused after fdia-graph is already out. A publish run that failed part-way can be run again: each upload skips the files PyPI already has.

After the release that ships the new README.md, delete docs/figures/diagrams/pipeline.mmd, its .png and its .svg, and take pipeline off NOT_YET_REDRAWN in tools/prereview.py and off docs/stylesheets/extra.css: until then the published PyPI page loads that PNG from main.

A released version is never re-cut; fix forward. Data releases (timelines, pools) have their own tags, data-v<x.y.z> (the bare v0.x.y tags belong to package versions), and do not move the package version. The registry maps the short name (fg.load(..., release="v0.8.0")) to the tag, and tools/upload_assets.py v0.8.0 <files> refuses to touch a package tag.

The files of a data release are one pool_ieee{N}.h5 and one timeline_ieee{N}.h5 per system. python tools/upload_assets.py vX.Y.Z notes.md <files> creates the data-vX.Y.Z release and uploads them; it never replaces an asset already on the release. The sha256 of each file then goes in SHA256 in src/fdia_graph/constants/releases.py, and PINNED_RELEASE in the same module is moved last.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text:
The first four rows are the generation toolkit (src/fdia_graph/), the next four the analysis toolkit (analysis/src/fdia_analysis/); a record or a formula is in the models/ or formulas/ of the toolkit that uses it.

you want to change look in an attack family, the plausibility band, the meter model engine/, formulas/attacks.py, formulas/noise.py what a timeline file contains generation/ by stage: plan.py (splits and placement), design.py (the overload Am, in parallel), emit.py (the frames), write.py (the file); generation/__init__.py (the pool and generate); source.py holds the one path of every timeline (TimelineSource.generate) and the grids are its subclasses (ieee.py an IEEE case, newyork.py the New York grid); timeline.py is the IEEE entry point; then docs/reference/DATA_DICTIONARY.md a generation setting its model in models/config.py (TimelineSettings and the nested RampSettings, SearchSettings, OverloadSettings, MeterSettings, SplitSettings); generate_timeline takes every field as a flat keyword too how a timeline is loaded or exported dataset/, one concern per file an estimator se/methods.py, its algebra in formulas/estimation.py a localizer localization/methods.py or learned.py the trusted-meter selectors trust/, its algebra in fdia_analysis/formulas/trust.py (the row reduction it builds on, which the attack search also uses, in fdia_graph/formulas/trust.py) the federated localizers and prior federated/, its algebra in formulas/federated.py a returned record's fields models/ a formula formulas/, and its row in docs/reference/FORMULAS.md any file, to learn what it does docs/reference/MODULES.md, the first paragraph of every file's docstring a study's numbers or figures its runs in the results store (results/), its page under docs/analysis/ how released New York data is built pipelines/newyork/ a new folder its role in REPO or DOCS in tools/layout.py first; the gate fails a folder without one

docs.title: State estimation with fdia_analysis.se
docs.text:
Given a scan of noisy, possibly attacked measurements, estimate the true bus voltages and angles. Every timeline ships a noiseless clean layer, so the estimate is scored against exact ground truth.

import fdia_graph as fg
from fdia_analysis.models.config import PriorConfig
from fdia_analysis.se.methods import WLS, AdaptiveWeighting, SubspacePrior

train = fg.load("ieee14", split="train")
test = fg.load("ieee14", split="test")

est = SubspacePrior(prior=PriorConfig(rank_frac=0.2, reweight="huber", c=1.5)).fit(train)
xhat = est.estimate(test)  # [n, 2N-1] = [theta rad (non-slack) | V pu (all buses)]
rep = est.score(test)  # per-family angle/voltage MAE vs the clean truth

needs pip install "fdia-analysis[se]", a timeline (data release v0.8.3), units="physical" walkthrough ../../guides/state_estimation.md state 2N-1: every voltage magnitude, every non-slack angle; slack angle fixed to one reference angle, theta_ref, taken from the training split at fit time (the case's reference angle on the released pools)

docs.title: The method classes
docs.text: Class What it changes Knobs WLS Nothing. The audited baseline: least squares weighted by accuracy-class meter error ResidualRemoval Classical largest-normalized-residual removal: the one largest residual above the threshold per pass, re-solved, with an observability guard threshold AdaptiveWeighting Iteratively reweighted least squares (the Huber M-estimator) c SubspacePrior Restricts the solve to a low-rank benign operating subspace, optionally composed with Huber (reweight="huber", which GatedPrior inherits) rank_frac, reweight JacobianWeighting Huber weights from the physically unexplained part of the scan-to-scan measurement change (the Jacobian-informed digest), one solve; reweight="huber" adds the classical passes on top c, reweight, huber_c GatedPrior The proposed estimator with a localizer gating the weights: meters on flagged buses and their incident flows are down-weighted so the prior fills in the state there; secured meters are never down-weighted gate, gate_factor, secured

docs.title: Files
docs.text: file holds se/base.py SEBase: the measurement function and the chord Jacobian (ac_measurement and ac_jacobian of formulas/measurement.py), meter weights from benign residuals, the chord-Newton loop, calibration and scoring, shared by every estimator se/methods.py the method classes above, each a subclass of SEBase that changes one thing se/jacobian.py JacobianFeatures: the measurement Jacobian as a transform of the scan-to-scan measurement change, the features JacobianWeighting and the learned localizers read se/detect/rules.py the alarm rules (AlarmRule, PersistenceRule): a statistic per scan turned into a first alarm, described in the extending guide

docs.title: Jacobian-informed weighting
docs.text:
The change is Δz = z_t − h(x̂_{t−1}), this scan against the readings the previous frame's estimate predicts. The explained part is r∥ = P_H Δz with P_H = H (HᵀWH)⁻¹ HᵀW, and the unexplained rest is r⊥ = (I − P_H) Δz. The weight of meter i is its fitted weight times Huber's factor min(1, c / (|r⊥_i| / σ_i)); H and W are the fitted chord Jacobian and meter weights.

result 14 118 300 WLS angle error reduction (%) 17 23 21 Ar, WLS → Jacobian weighting (deg) 0.231 → 0.123 0.0516 → 0.0155 0.128 → 0.031 Aq, WLS → Jacobian weighting (deg) 0.413 → 0.413 0.0235 → 0.0235 0.0274 → 0.0274 against iterated Huber (deg, geometric mean) 0.076 vs 0.057 0.0156 vs 0.0139 0.0213 vs 0.0198

The gain comes from the in-place families; the stealthy families are untouched, as (I − P_H)a = 0 predicts. The temporal unexplained residual carries what Huber already recovers from the estimate's own residual, so this route cannot move the proposed estimator. The routes that can are a localizer gate and, ahead of it, a trusted set of meters.

docs.title: Localization-gated estimation

docs.title: Federated localization with fdia_analysis.federated
docs.text:
Status. The results on this page are on data release v0.8.1 and predate the measurements-only feature rules (swing from observed frames, the Jacobian block against the previous frame's estimate, measured calibration) and the one-frame Aq and Al. They are not yet rerun on v0.8.3; the centralized numbers in ../localization/README.md are current.

The federated localization papers' protocol, run by the SDK on the v0.8.1 timelines with the 14-dim per-bus vector plus the Jacobian block.

import fdia_graph as fg
from fdia_analysis.federated.localizer import FedBusCNN
from fdia_analysis.models.config import FederatedSettings, LearnedConfig

rel = dict(release="v0.8.1")  # the release these results are on
zs = dict(families=[0, 1, 2], **rel)  # benign + Aq + Ad
train = fg.load("ieee118", split="train", **zs)
val = fg.load("ieee118", split="val", **zs)
test = fg.load("ieee118", split="test", families=[0, 1, 2, 3, 4], **rel)  # adds As and Ar

loc = FedBusCNN(
    federated=FederatedSettings(K=3, rounds=60, local_epochs=3), learned=LearnedConfig(features="full14+jac")
).fit(train, val=val)
tab = loc.score_perbus(test, buses="attackable", fr_over="all")  # the paper's Table IV block

release= pins the built-in data only: a dataset registered locally under the same name loads in its place. fg.list_datasets()["ieee118"] reads "builtin" when these are the release's records, and the study did not fit otherwise.

clients K utilities from the spectral partition of the bus graph (random_state 42); each client reads only its own buses and its own flow meters for the power balance training FedAvg with uniform weights, 60 rounds of 3 local epochs, AdamW lr 5e-4, weight decay 0.01, batch 256, gradient clip 1.0, the final-round weights features the papers' 14-dim per-bus vector built per client, plus the 8-channel Jacobian block, computed once centrally and shared, the one feature a client does not build from its own meters threshold the papers' validation-best global tau on the 0.05 to 0.95 grid, from per-client confusion counts summed at the server what crosses a boundary per-channel moments once, the model weights every round, the per-bus confusion counts once, and the central Jacobian block

The papers report CNN macro F1 of 0.963, 0.963 and 0.952 on the v0.4.1 record shards, and the SDK reproduces them within half a point on the v0.7.2 shards. On a timeline the 14-dim vector alone drops, because its temporal features compare each frame with the frame one minute before rather than with the benign scan before an attacked snapshot. The Jacobian block reads each frame's physics instead of its history, which recovers most of that drop on 118 and 300 and about half of it on 14; the centralized comparison with and without the block is in ../localization/README.md.

docs.title: Localization with fdia_analysis.localization
docs.text:
Which buses are under attack, per scan.

import fdia_graph as fg
from fdia_analysis.localization.learned import BusCNN, BusMLP
from fdia_analysis.localization.methods import SwingThreshold, DeltaThreshold, ResidualLocalizer
from fdia_analysis.models.config import LocalizerConfig

train = fg.load("ieee14", split="train")
test = fg.load("ieee14", split="test")

loc = SwingThreshold(localizer=LocalizerConfig(fa_target=0.01)).fit(
    train
)  # thresholds set on benign records only
flag = loc.localize(test)  # [n, N] bool: which buses are called attacked
rep = loc.score(test)  # per-family metrics + benign false alarms

For each attacked family loc.score reports the strict localization accuracy, the node precision, recall and F1, the per-bus macro F1, the per-sample F1 and the detection rate. For the benign records it reports the record-level false-alarm rate and the mean per-bus alarm rate, and an all entry pools every record.

shared metrics and the benign-quantile calibration in LocalizerBase; a threshold arm changes only the per-bus score, a learned arm also overrides fit to train on every record and, given val, the threshold budget every method is calibrated to the same false-alarm target (fa_target), set per bus on benign training records, and the measured test FR differs by method; the one exception is a learned arm given val, which picks one global validation-best threshold from labelled records (the papers' zero-shot protocol) "all" entry pools every record; the papers' per-bus macro F1, DR and FR over the buses attacked somewhere in the scored split

docs.text:
Class Score Needs SwingThreshold The dataset's windowed swing feature: each scan's injection change as a z-score of the bus's typical recent change numpy only DeltaThreshold The raw one-scan change scaled by the bus's benign RMS. Same signal without the windowing, so the gap shows what windowing buys numpy only ResidualLocalizer Largest normalized residual from a state-estimation solve (any fdia_analysis.se estimator, default WLS), aggregated to each bus's own meters and incident flows. Textbook bad-data identification [se] extra BusMLP The papers' lightweight arm: one 4x128 MLP applied to every bus's own 14-dim vector (readings, meter mask, partial KCL residual, delta, swing). 52k parameters [torch] extra BusCNN The papers' best localizer: a 1-D convolution across the bus axis over the same 14-dim vector, 4 layers of 128 channels, kernel 3. No graph read. 154k parameters [torch] extra

The learned arms train on the records they are given, so the protocol is the load call. fit(train, val=val) picks the papers' validation-best threshold instead of the false-alarm one.

docs.title: Trusted meters with fdia_analysis.trust
docs.text:
Which meters to secure so that a stealthy attack stops being stealthy.

import fdia_graph as fg
from fdia_analysis.models.config import DqnConfig, TrustConfig
from fdia_analysis.trust.base import TrustedMeters
from fdia_analysis.trust.meter_dqn import TrustedMetersDQN

train = fg.load("ieee14", split="train")
test = fg.load("ieee14", split="test", order="time")

tm = TrustedMeters(TrustConfig(k=20)).fit(train)  # the greedy row-reduction selection on the Jacobian
tm.order, tm.cost  # the meters secured in order, the attack cost after each
rep = tm.score(test)  # residual detection per family, with and without the trust

rl = TrustedMetersDQN(TrustConfig(k=20), dqn=DqnConfig(episodes=200)).fit(
    train
)  # the same selection as an MDP with a DQN policy

docs.title: The idea
docs.text:
A stealthy attack a = H c moves the meters the way a real state change c would, so the residual test does not see it. A meter the attacker cannot write pins its row: a_S = 0, so H_S c = 0 and the attack lives in the null space of the secured rows. Every secured meter shrinks that space; once H_S has full column rank there is no stealthy attack left. The attack cost is how many meters the cheapest attack in the open subspace must touch (the sparsest row of its reduced row echelon basis, an upper bound on the exact NP-hard minimum). Both selectors read the same kernel, fdia_analysis.formulas.trust (on the row reduction of fdia_graph.formulas.trust).

class picks the next meter by needs TrustedMeters the greedy rule: on the cheapest open attack, the meter whose protection leaves the attacker the costliest cheapest attack [se] TrustedMetersDQN a Q-network trained on the MDP (state the secured set, reward the cost rise), rolled out greedily; one rollout of m forward passes picks a set where the greedy rule re-evaluates every candidate at every step [se], [torch]

score(test) needs a time-ordered timeline view: on every attacked frame the secured meters are set back to their benign reading (the attacker cannot write them) and a WLS residual test at the benign false-alarm level says whether the attack now shows. detected_before is the residual test with every meter writable, detected_after with the trust in place.

The package holds the trusted-meter selectors on a dataset.

docs.title: What the secured meters do for estimation and localization
docs.text:
The residual test is one consumer of a trusted set. tm.secured_copy(ds, out, name) writes a copy of the timeline in which the selected meters read their benign value on every frame (the attacker locked out of them, the tamper masks and the stored temporal features following), so every estimator and localizer of the other two guides can be scored with the set secured; the study does that for the greedy and the DQN selections and writes runs of trust.secured_localization and trust.secured_estimation to the results store.

Rule: a localization gate never down-weights a secured meter. GatedPrior scales every meter of a flagged bus by a thousandth. On a secured copy those meters include the secured ones, the only true readings inside the attacked region, so a plain gate throws away the evidence the trusted set provides. GatedPrior(GateConfig(gate), secured=tm.select()) keeps the secured meters at full weight, and that arm wins on IEEE-14.

docs.title: The attack families
docs.text:
A timeline holds attacks so that a detector can be trained and scored on them. This page says what an attack in a timeline is, which families the generator makes, and which class produces each. It describes what the dataset contains. The equations are in Formulas, each with its source.

Paths are under src/fdia_graph/.

docs.title: An episode
docs.text: An attack is an episode: a run of consecutive frames under one design. An episode has a family, an onset, a length and the buses it attacks. Episodes never overlap, so a frame has at most one active family. Every frame of an episode carries the attack, except a frame whose scan cannot be built: it is stored benign and counted in fallback_benign.

docs.title: The local false state
docs.text:
Both families the generator makes are built on one idea, the local false state of [WU26].

The attacker wants the operator to believe a state of the grid that is not the true one. A detector that checks the readings against the grid's equations would catch readings that fit no state. So the attacker picks a false state that the equations allow:

  1. Choose a small area of the grid: the buses within a few branches of the targets. A ramp has up to five targets, which need not be neighbours, so its area can be several neighbourhoods.
  2. Change the loads inside the area (and, for an overload, the generator outputs).
  3. Solve the AC equations of the area again, with every voltage outside it held true.
  4. Add the difference of the readings to the true scan.

The attack vector is a = h(x_false) - h(x_true), where h is the measurement function (Meters and noise). It is zero on every meter the area does not reach. Each meter keeps its usual noise. So the observed scan looks like a normal noisy scan of the false state, and a residual test finds nothing wrong.

A false state must also be plausible. Inside the buses it re-solves it stays within the bus voltage limits and the generator limits of the case [WU26, eqs. 21-23]. The buses one branch outside take up the change in their reported injection. An overload checks the generator limits there too; a ramp does not.

docs.title: The two families
docs.text:
Family Code What the attacker does At, the slow ramp 5 a false load that moves away from the true load a little each frame (up or down), holds, and returns to one step away from it Am, the overload 7 the reported flow of a line rises to its rating

At is hard to see because each step is small, so a detector that looks for jumps sees none. Its ramp profile is described in [DAT26], and the published attack it follows is in the citation list.

Am is the multi-snapshot overload attack of [WU26, eqs. 24-25]. Over the window the reported flow of the target moves from its true value to its limit. The operator sees a line about to overload that is not.

docs.title: The designs
docs.text:
A design decides what an episode changes on each frame. The package's designs are search-based, and they run on every test system: the IEEE cases and the New York case.

At Am Family class SearchRamp SearchOverload Targets up to 5 loads one or two lines, at their ratings False state from a local AC solve in numpy a local AC solve in numpy Designed as the walk reaches it before its split is walked

Every family answers the same question for the timeline: the episode of a window (EpisodeFamily.designed in engine/attacks/family.py). That is why one path generates every timeline (Generate a timeline).

The designs read a scan's load and generation from its state. How a bus's injection divides into the two is the setting loads (How a pool's load is read).

docs.title: The search-based designs
docs.text:
The designs are methods of EpisodeDesigns, the generator's episode_designs: ramp_design and am_overload_design (engine/attacks/episodes.py). Settings are in TimelineSettings (the tables).

The fewest-tamper search. [WU26, eq. 12] asks for the attack that tampers the fewest devices. The search tries supports, the sets of buses the false state moves: the whole area first, then smaller ones, smallest first. It keeps the one whose attack changes the fewest devices beyond noise (engine/attacks/minimize.py). It solves at most min_budget supports per search.

At.

  • The targets are up to 5 loads drawn at random among the stealthy loads: attackable loads that are not on a generator bus [BOY22]. An attackable load has nonzero active power, is not on the slack bus and is at most max_load_mw.
  • One load factor moves all of them: it rises ramp_rate per frame, holds, and returns at the same rate. The rise lasts 20 % to 45 % of the episode and the hold 0 % to 25 % (draw_ramp). The factor never falls below one ramp_rate, so every frame of the episode carries an attack: after the return the episode stays one step away from the true load until it ends, and a ramp with a long rise can end before its return is complete. A ramp goes up or down with equal chance.
  • With min_tamper (the default) the search keeps only supports on which no metered channel moves by more than its rated accuracy times stealth_scale between frames. With min_tamper off, or when the search finds no such support (the episode's record then shows -1 devices), the ramp runs on its whole area with no such bound.
  • A step with no local solution is halved, up to 6 times (STEP_HALVINGS).
  • A design is tested on every frame it will occupy before it is accepted, up to 40 draws (ONSET_DRAWS).

Am.

  • The targets are lines that are rated, flow-metered, below their rating at every snapshot of the window, and near a load or a generator the attacker can move (eligible_lines). Each episode overloads n_lines lines, two by default as in the case studies of [WU26].
  • The ratings are 1.25 times each branch's peak true flow over the pool (rating_source="pool"). rating_source="pglib" uses the PGLib-OPF ratings instead, which exist for IEEE-14, 118 and 300; another case raises NoLineRatings. rating_source="delta" rates each line from its own window: its true flow at the window's last snapshot plus rating_delta (per unit of the system base).
  • The goal of each snapshot is a linear share of the way from the true flow to the rating, and the last snapshot reaches the rating (overload_goal).
  • The loads and generators of the support are free inside their limits. The load a bus shows changes by at most load_cap times its true load [YUA11].
  • A device counts as tampered when it moves beyond the noise of [WU26]'s own case studies: 0.03 p.u. on a SCADA channel and 0.01 p.u. on a PMU channel.
  • Nothing bounds how far Am moves a channel between snapshots, as in [WU26].
  • support_method="rref" picks the support by the row reduction of [WU26] instead of the search (engine/attacks/rref.py).

The overload episodes these settings build, measured with families=("Am",) and seed 1 (experiment generation.am_overload). Every line of every built episode reaches its rating.

system recipe frames episodes fallen back devices (mean) channels (mean) largest change, pu (median / max episode) s per episode IEEE-14 one line, without the load and generator bounds 3000 25 0 5.3 15.0 0.18 / 5.74 15 IEEE-14 one line, with the load and generator bounds 3000 25 0 3.9 9.9 0.14 / 0.82 30 IEEE-14 two lines, with the load and generator bounds (default) 3000 25 0 6.8 19.3 0.17 / 1.59 39 IEEE-30 one line, without the load and generator bounds 600 5 0 3.8 8.8 0.09 / 0.29 20 IEEE-118 one line, without the load and generator bounds 2000 17 0 6.8 21.4 1.05 / 44.94 43 IEEE-118 one line, with the load and generator bounds 2000 17 0 9.6 30.4 0.40 / 3.29 71 IEEE-118 two lines, with the load and generator bounds (default) 2000 17 0 17.8 72.0 1.33 / 3.39 78

docs.title: A family of your own
docs.text:
A source takes design families of your own, each in place of the search family of one name (Generate a timeline). The simplest is a subclass of AttackFamily (engine/attacks/family.py). It returns an Episode (models/plan.py) from design(window, rng), or None when the window holds no attack. The window is the true state over the frames the episode would cover. The episode holds one attack vector: a value for every meter on every frame. The walk adds each row to the true scan of its frame (VectorEpisode).

A design that finds no attack can say why (design_explained): a reason the family sets in last_miss, solver_error when the family counted a failed solve, else infeasible. Add a design family, an alarm rule or a test system has the steps.

docs.title: Labels and the tamper masks
docs.text:
In the file Shape Meaning data/y [T, N] 1 at each attacked bus data/family [T] the family code; 0 is benign data/seq_id [T] the episode's row; -1 is benign attack/node_tamper, attack/edge_tamper as the readings 1 at a tampered meter attack/pmu_i_tamper as the currents 1 at a tampered PMU current episodes/ one row per episode onset, length, family, buses

What a 1 in a tamper mask means depends on the family that designed the episode.

Family A meter is tampered A bus is attacked SearchRamp, SearchOverload where the attack changed the stored reading at the buses the design names a family of your own that designs an attack vector where the vector moves the reading by more than the meter's accuracy class where a tampered meter sits at the bus

The file's attribute tamper, on attack/, states the rule of the package's own families, and both rules when the source was given a family of your own.

In every file the observed scan minus the benign scan is the attack, exactly (Layers and labels).

docs.title: What the released files additionally contain
docs.text:
The released files of data release v0.8.3 hold seven families. The current generator makes two.

Code Family In released files Generated today 1 Aq, stealthy load scaling yes no 2 Ad, meter corruption yes no 3 As, meter scaling yes no 4 Ar, replay yes no 5 At, slow ramp yes yes 6 Al, load redistribution yes no 7 Am yes, as a load redistribution yes, as the overload

The older families are read-only. Their codes stay in the label table fg.FAMILIES, and the files that carry them load, filter and score by name:

import fdia_graph as fg

old = fg.load("ieee14", release="v0.8.3", families=["Aq"])

The generator refuses them. In those files Aq, Al, Ad, As and Ar are one frame each, and the Am episodes drive no line to its limit. Those files also have an angle reading at every voltmeter bus and no PMU currents (Meters and noise). fg.STEALTHY_FAMILIES is the set of codes that are local false states: Aq, At, Al and Am.

docs.title: Where the code is
docs.text:
File Holds engine/attacks/family.py EpisodeFamily, AttackFamily, DesignedEpisode, VectorEpisode: what every family answers engine/attacks/search.py SearchRamp, SearchOverload and their episodes engine/attacks/episodes.py ramp_design, am_overload_design engine/attacks/area.py the attacker's area and its boundary engine/attacks/false_state.py the local false state: the area re-solved engine/attacks/frames.py the attack vector of a false state, written onto the true scan engine/attacks/ramp_frames.py one scan of At: a false state added to the true scan engine/attacks/overload.py the overload goal, the ratings, the eligible lines engine/attacks/minimize.py the fewest-tamper search engine/attacks/blas.py one BLAS thread for the length of a search engine/attacks/window.py one attack window, and what a support costs over it engine/attacks/rref.py the support by row reduction

To add a family of your own, see Add a design family, an alarm rule or a test system.

docs.title: How the package flows
docs.text:
A timeline is the meter readings of one grid, frame by frame, with attacks placed in it and labelled per bus. The package builds one in the same stages for every test system. What differs between systems is the settings, and how the operating points are solved.

The sections follow the picture; box 3 is two sections, the meters and then the attacks. Paths are under src/fdia_graph/ unless a section says otherwise.

Three folders serve every stage. formulas/ holds the mathematics as pure functions, one per equation. models/ holds every bundle of values that is passed or returned. constants/ holds the fixed values, each with its unit and its source.

docs.title: Test system
docs.text:
The grid: its buses, branches and generating units, with a base operating state.

  • Case (systems/case.py) holds one grid as a frozen record of arrays.
  • Network (systems/network.py) builds the admittances of a Case once. It gives the injections, flows and currents of any state.

Case.from_ieee(118) gives an IEEE case and nygrid_case() gives the New York grid. Both return the same class. Test systems lists every system.

You now have: a Case and its Network, which describe the grid.

docs.title: Operating points
docs.text:
One AC operating point per frame, in time order. The set is called the pool. data/ holds where it comes from, for every test system: first the load data, then the solve.

The load data:

  • data/profiles.py reads a load series from a file (load_profile) or fetches it from an operator's feed (fetch_profile). The result is a load profile, one number per step.
  • The New York grid takes a load per bus. data/inputs.py downloads and reads its public input tables, data/load_sources.py fetches the building and sales data, and LoadModel in data/loads.py builds each bus's load from them. data/config.py holds that build's settings.

The solve:

  • IEEE cases: generate_states in data/ieee_pool.py scales the loads along a load profile and solves one power flow per step.
  • New York grid: data/dispatch.py sets each hour's dispatch. PoolBuilder in data/pool.py then solves one optimal power flow per five-minute frame, with IpoptSolver (data/ipopt_solver.py), which runs on the Ipopt that data/ipopt.py finds and checks, and one power flow at its outputs, with PandapowerSolver (data/pandapower_solver.py). data/pool.py also reads and writes the pool file.
  • Both solvers are engines of one interface, Solver (data/solver.py). A SolveSettings passed to either builder picks the kind of solve and the engine (Solving).

The IEEE pools are released, so fg.generate downloads one and you do not build it. Solving explains the two kinds of solve, and what happens to a frame that does not solve. Build the operating points has the steps.

You now have: the pool, the true state of the grid at every frame.

docs.title: Meters and noise
docs.text:
What the operator reads from a state. The three classes are in sensing/ and serve every grid.

  • MeterPlan (meters.py): every meter as one row of a table, with its kind, its place, its owner and its accuracy class.
  • Measurement (measure.py): the measurement function h(x), the readings a state gives, and its Jacobian.
  • NoiseModel (noise.py): each meter's accuracy class, split into a constant bias and a jitter drawn again at every scan.

A benign scan is h(x) of a pool state plus noise. It needs no new solve. Meters and noise explains the plan, the accuracy classes and the noise.

You now have: one benign scan per frame, the readings with no attack.

docs.title: Attacks
docs.text:
An attack is an episode: a run of consecutive frames under one design. engine/ holds the generator (core.py) and, under engine/attacks/, the attack designs of every grid. There are two families.

  • At, the slow ramp: a false load that rises a little each frame.
  • Am, the overload: the reported flow of a line rises to its rating.

Each attacked frame is the reading of one false AC state. The attacker re-solves a small area of the grid and holds every voltage outside it true. The attack vector is h(x_false) - h(x_true), added to the benign scan.

Family Design Family class At ramp_design SearchRamp Am am_overload_design SearchOverload

The designs are made by the parts FdiaGenerator holds (engine/core.py), the classes of engine/attacks/. They run on every test system. A timeline asks every family the same thing, the episode of a window (EpisodeFamily.designed, engine/attacks/family.py); the designs answer as the families SearchRamp and SearchOverload (engine/attacks/search.py). A source also takes a family of your own in place of one of them. The attack families describes both families and their designs.

You now have: the episodes, each with its frames, its buses and its attack vectors.

docs.title: The timeline file
docs.text:
generation/ holds the stages that walk a timeline: the plan, the designs, the frames and the writer. TimelineSource.generate in generation/source.py is the one path every timeline takes: open the file, cut the train, validation and test splits, place the episodes, design them, walk the frames in time order, and finish the file.

  • The steps are written once. A source is a subclass that builds the generator, the pool and the designer of its families, and says what its files record. The package has one: SearchSource (generation/search.py), the original generator, built on a Network. IeeeSource in generation/ieee.py builds it for an IEEE case by name, and SearchSource.for_pool builds it on a pool file, as the New York case has. How the splits are cut is a setting of the source, split_by: three blocks in time order, or whole weeks, which need each frame's time (an IEEE pool stores none, so the caller passes time=).
  • TimelineWriter (generation/write.py) is the one writer of the HDF5 file.
  • schema.py defines every group, dataset and attribute name of the file, once.
  • Settings arrive as one model from models/config.py, TimelineSettings.

fg.generate starts an IEEE timeline through generate_timeline in timeline.py. On the New York case you build the source yourself, with SearchSource.for_pool. Generate a timeline has every step and every setting, and Layers and labels what the file stores per frame.

You now have: one HDF5 file. fg.generate also registers it under a name, for fg.load.

docs.title: Loading
docs.text:
fg.load(name, split="train") returns an FdiaGraph, the dataset class in dataset/. It reads the static graph once and slices records on request, so the whole file is never in memory.

  • registry.py turns a name and a data release into a file. download.py fetches the file to the cache and checks its sha256.
  • dataset/ has one concern per file: base.py (shared state), graph.py (the static graph), physics.py (admittances and clean flows), records.py (one record, batches), export.py (whole-split arrays) and sequence.py (windows and episodes).
  • clients.py reads a timeline that records the owners of its buses as federated clients.
  • errors.py defines every error the package raises on purpose.

The package's __init__.py imports the heavy helpers only when they are called, so fg.load never imports torch or pandapower. The data dictionary says what every array means.

You now have: the timeline as records, batches, windows and episodes.

docs.title: Analysis
docs.text:
The second toolkit, fdia_analysis, measures things on a loaded timeline. Its code is under analysis/src/fdia_analysis/. Each package has a page with its results.

Package Question Page se what is the true state? State estimation localization which buses are attacked? Localization trust which meters should be secured? Trusted meters federated can clients train without pooling records? Federated

se/detect/ holds the alarm rules, which turn a detector's score per scan into a first alarm, and results/ the code of the results store, where every measured number is kept.

docs.title: Two toolkits, one direction
docs.text:
The generation toolkit is the distribution fdia-graph, the package fdia_graph under src/. The analysis toolkit is the distribution fdia-analysis, the package fdia_analysis under analysis/.

fdia_analysis imports fdia_graph: it reads timelines through fdia_graph.dataset and uses the generation toolkit's formulas and records. Nothing in fdia_graph imports fdia_analysis, and tests/test_toolkit_boundary.py checks it. The generation toolkit installs and runs alone. Install and data versions lists every extra.

docs.title: Where next
docs.text:
Read in this order.

  1. The three tutorials: load a dataset, generate a timeline and analyse a timeline.
  2. Test systems and Solving: the grids, and how their operating points are solved.
  3. Meters and noise, The attack families and Layers and labels: what a frame of a timeline holds.
  4. Generate a timeline and Build the operating points: the steps and the settings.
  5. Glossary and Data dictionary: every term, every array and its shape.
  6. Modules: what every file does, in one line.
  7. Concepts to code and Formulas: the function behind each idea and equation.
  8. Class map and Examples: the class diagrams, and runnable baselines to copy.
  9. State estimation guide: fitting and scoring an estimator.
  10. The four study pages in the table above: what was measured, on what, and the result.
  11. Contributing: the rules and the pull-request flow.

docs.title: Layers and labels
docs.text:
Every frame of a timeline is stored three times: as the operator saw it, as it would have been without the attack, and as it truly was. This page explains the three layers, the labels beside them, and which of them a detector may read.

The data dictionary lists every array with its shape and columns. This page explains what they are for.

docs.title: The three layers
docs.text:
Layer Arrays What it is observed node_x, edge_x the scan with noise, and with the attack where attacked benign benign, edge_benign the same scan with the attack removed, the same noise clean clean, edge_clean the true state, with no noise and no attack

Each layer exists for the buses and for the branches. A file with PMU currents has pmu_i and pmu_i_benign as well.

Two differences are exact, on the metered channels.

Difference Is observed minus benign the attack benign minus clean the meter noise

Each frame draws its noise once. The benign scan is the true readings plus that noise. The observed scan is the benign scan plus the attack on the meters the attack moves. So node_x - benign is the attack vector exactly, and zero outside the episode.

clean covers every bus, with no mask. edge_clean holds the true flows at the metered branch ends. The loader also derives edge_clean_full, the true flow on every branch, from clean when it reads the file.

docs.title: What each layer is for
docs.text: Layer Use observed the input of a detector or an estimator benign evaluation: what a meter would read if it were secured clean the target of state estimation, and evaluation

docs.title: The masks
docs.text: Metering is sparse: not every bus has a voltmeter and not every branch has a flow meter. node_m and edge_m are 1 where a meter exists and 0 where none does. A reading with no meter is stored as zero, so read the mask to tell a missing reading from a true zero. The masks are the same on every frame (Meters and noise).

docs.title: The labels
docs.text:
Label Shape Meaning y [N] per frame 1 at each attacked bus family one per frame which attack; 0 is benign stealthy one per frame 1 for a family that is a local false state seq_id one per frame the episode's row; -1 is benign tamper masks as the readings 1 at each meter the attack changed ds.episodes one row per episode onset, length, family, buses

y answers "which buses". family answers "which attack". There is one family per frame because episodes never overlap. The attack families says what each family is and what a 1 in a tamper mask means.

Two more columns place a frame: split (0 train, 1 validation, 2 test) and timestep, the frame's row in the file.

docs.title: The temporal features
docs.text:
A file also stores two features computed from the observed frames alone (formulas/temporal.py, written by TimelineWriter.write_temporal_layers).

Feature Definition temporal_delta the change of P_inj and Q_inj from the frame before; zero on frame 0 swing temporal_delta divided by the bus's recent-change scale

The scale is the standard deviation of the bus's absolute scan-to-scan change over the 60 scans before the frame (SWING_WINDOW_SCANS), plus 0.001. A sudden jump reads as a large swing at its first frame. The slow ramp At changes by less than the typical recent change on every frame, so its swing stays near the benign level.

ClientView.temporal() is a third: it computes each client's change from its own readings when a file is read as clients.

docs.title: Which layers a feature may read
docs.text:
At test time a feature may use only measurements and quantities derived from them.

  • Measurements: node_x, edge_x, pmu_i, the masks, temporal_delta, swing, and the previous frame's readings and row (prev_node_x, prev_edge_x, prev_swing, prev_timestep).
  • Not inputs: clean and benign. They exist for evaluation and for fitting.
  • Labels: y, family, stealthy, seq_id, the tamper masks and the magnitudes.

What each analysis class reads:

Class Reads Role SEBase.estimate node_x, edge_x measurements SEBase.fit(calibrate="truth") measurements, family, clean fitting: the meter error scales at the true state SEBase.fit(calibrate="measured") measurements, family fitting from accuracy classes SEBase.score measurements, then family, clean evaluation against the truth JacobianFeatures, JacobianWeighting node_x, edge_x, prev_node_x, prev_edge_x, prev_timestep measurements SwingThreshold, DeltaThreshold swing, temporal_delta measurements ResidualLocalizer node_x, edge_x measurements BusCNN, BusMLP, FedBusCNN, FedBusMLP what the feature set names (below); y as the training label measurements GatedPrior(GateConfig(gate="oracle")) y an evaluation ceiling only TrustSelector.fit measurements, family measurements TrustSelector.score benign, edge_benign evaluation trust.secured.secured_copy benign, the tamper masks writes a copy in which chosen meters read benign

A learned localizer reads node_x, node_m, edge_x and y. A feature set with full14 adds temporal_delta and swing, one with prev adds prev_swing, and one with jac adds the previous frame's readings and prev_timestep.

secured_copy also rewrites the tamper masks and the two stored temporal features of its copy.

The state estimators default to calibrate="truth". ResidualLocalizer, the Jacobian features and TrustSelector fit their estimator with calibrate="measured". So a detector never reads the clean layer.

docs.title: The groups of a file
docs.text:
A timeline is one HDF5 file. Its group, dataset and attribute names are defined once, in src/fdia_graph/schema.py.

Group Holds data/ the observed layers, the masks, the labels and the per-frame columns benign/ the benign layers clean/ the clean layers attack/ the tamper masks and the designed magnitudes episodes/ one row per episode graph/ the static graph: the branches and what gives the admittance matrix attributes what identifies the file, and the settings it was generated with

The frames are chunked along time, so a window of consecutive frames is one read. The data dictionary lists the datasets of each group.

docs.title: One layout
docs.text:
One writer writes every timeline, in one layout: flows at the from end of a branch [E, 2], PMU currents as real and imaginary part, and both temporal features. A file that declares another layout in its attributes (flows at both branch ends in edge_feat, or a current_form other than rectangular) was written elsewhere. It is refused with NotATimeline when it is opened, so no column of it is read as something else.

A New York file has the form of an IEEE file. Its injections are positive for load, like an IEEE file's, and it holds the solved frames of its pool only.

Some datasets are in a file only when the source was given what they hold:

Where Dataset or attribute Holds Written when data/ time each frame's time, int64 seconds the pool has times (a New York pool), or time= is passed graph/ bus_client the client that owns each bus; -1 for none the source has own= attributes client_names the clients' names, in the order bus_client indexes the source has own=

Generate a timeline says what time= takes, and its section on clients what own= does.

The unit table, the bus names and the bus coordinates of the New York case are not in a file. They are the case file's (Test systems).

The attributes record the settings as JSON (settings) with their hash (settings_hash).

docs.title: Meters and noise
docs.text:
A pool holds the true state of the grid at every frame. The operator does not see the state. The operator sees meter readings, and each reading has an error. This page explains how the package turns a state into a scan: the meter plan, the measurement function and the noise.

The three classes are in src/fdia_graph/sensing/ and serve every test system.

Class File Holds MeterPlan sensing/meters.py every meter, as one row of a table Measurement sensing/measure.py the readings a state gives, and their Jacobian NoiseModel sensing/noise.py each meter's error: a bias and a jitter

A benign scan is NoiseModel.sample(Measurement.h(state)). It needs no new solve: the readings follow from the stored state.

docs.title: The meter plan
docs.text:
MeterPlan is a table with one row per meter.

Column Meaning kind what the meter reads (MeterKind, below) bus the bus it sits at branch, end the branch and its end (0 from, 1 to); -1 for a bus meter owner the client that owns the meter's bus sigma_rel, sigma_abs the accuracy class bias the meter's constant error

The plan is made once per timeline, from the seed. It is the same on every frame.

docs.title: What a meter reads
docs.text:
The meters follow the SCADA and PMU plan of [WU26, eqs. 17-20]. A SCADA voltmeter reads the voltage magnitude only. A PMU reads the magnitude, the angle, and the current phasor of every branch end at its bus.

MeterKind Reads Unit V voltage magnitude at a bus p.u. VA voltage angle at a PMU bus degrees P, Q power injection at a bus MW, MVAr PF, QF power flow at one end of a branch MW, MVAr IR, II PMU current as real and imaginary part p.u.

docs.title: The placement
docs.text:
MeterPlan.from_coverage places the meters at random, on every test system.

Meter Where P, Q injection every bus P, Q flow the from end of a random share of branches Voltmeters a random share of buses PMUs a random share of buses, at least one PMU currents every branch end at a PMU bus, as real and imaginary part Owner one client; with the owners of the buses, the client of the meter's bus

MeterSettings gives the shares: vbus_frac 0.6, pmu_frac 0.2 and flow_frac 0.9. The voltmeter buses are int(0.6 N) buses drawn at random, the PMU buses max(1, int(0.2 N)). Each branch gets a flow meter with probability 0.9.

On the New York case the meters are drawn over all 140 buses, the neighbouring grids' included. A source built with own= gives each meter the client of its bus; a meter at a bus that belongs to no client has owner -1 (Generate a timeline).

import numpy as np

from fdia_graph.constants.meters import MeterKind
from fdia_graph.models.config import MeterSettings
from fdia_graph.sensing.meters import MeterPlan
from fdia_graph.systems.case import Case

case = Case.from_ieee(14)  # needs fdia-graph[generate]
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
plan = MeterPlan.from_coverage(case, MeterSettings(), rng)
for kind in (MeterKind.V, MeterKind.VA, MeterKind.PF):
    print(kind.name, int((plan.kind == kind).sum()))
# V 10, VA 2, PF 17

docs.title: The table and the file
docs.text:
In the code the readings of one frame are a flat vector z, one value per row of the plan. In a timeline file they are layers: one array per bus, per branch and per PMU current.

Method Does MeterPlan.scatter puts one value per meter at its place in the layers MeterPlan.gather reads the flat vector back from the layers MeterPlan.from_masks rebuilds the table from the meter masks of a file that records the client of each bus

The round trip is exact. A client's data is the columns of z whose meter it owns.

docs.title: The measurement function
docs.text:
Measurement.h(vm, va) gives the exact reading of every meter of the plan for a state: the voltage magnitudes vm (p.u.) and angles va (degrees). The flows and currents follow from the voltages through the admittances of the Network.

The injections can be taken two ways.

  • From the voltages. This is the default.
  • From the pool, passed as injections=. An IEEE pool stores its own injections, and the generator passes them.

Measurement.jacobian(vm, va) is the derivative of the readings with respect to the state. Measurement.for_client(c) is the same function over one client's meters.

from fdia_graph.sensing.measure import Measurement
from fdia_graph.sensing.noise import NoiseModel
from fdia_graph.systems.network import Network

# case, plan and rng: from the snippet above
measure = Measurement(Network(case), plan)
z = measure.h(case.vm, case.va)       # exact readings
scan = NoiseModel(plan).sample(z, rng)  # one noisy scan
print(z.shape, scan.shape)            # (86,) (86,)

Measurement.h computes an injection from the voltages as generation minus load. A file stores load as positive, the sign an IEEE pool uses (Data dictionary).

docs.title: Accuracy classes
docs.text:
Each meter kind has an accuracy class: the standard deviation of its total error. The classes follow [ASP14] and are in constants/meters.py (ACCURACY_CLASS, KIND_ACCURACY).

Meter Standard deviation Kind of error power injection and flow 1.7 % of the reading relative voltage magnitude 0.0012 p.u. absolute voltage angle 0.00168 rad absolute PMU current 1/300 of the current's magnitude relative PMU current angle 1/300 rad absolute

The PMU current class is the 1 % total vector error of IEEE C37.118.1 [C37118], taken as three standard deviations (PMU_CURRENT_CLASS). It is relative to the phasor's magnitude, on the real and the imaginary part alike.

A relative meter also has a floor, so a reading near zero still has noise: 0.001 MW or MVAr on a power meter (POWER_NOISE_FLOOR_MW) and 0.00001 p.u. on a current (CURRENT_FLOOR_PU).

docs.title: Bias and jitter
docs.text:
A meter's error is mostly a fixed calibration offset. The package splits each class in two.

Part Share of the class Drawn jitter 0.25 (JITTER_FRAC) again at every scan bias sqrt(1 - 0.25^2), about 0.97 once per meter, with the plan

The squares of the two shares add to 1 (0.25² + 0.97² = 1), so bias and jitter together have the standard deviation of the class. On a relative meter the bias is a gain error. On an absolute meter it is an offset.

The biases are drawn with the plan: one draw for every bus and branch, metered or not (MeterPlan.from_placement).

A reading is the exact value with its bias, plus the jitter of that scan (NoiseModel.sample). NoiseModel.sigmas(z) gives the total of both, which an estimator weights by.

Treating the whole class as per-scan noise would make consecutive scans jump more than real meters do, and would hide the slow changes a detector looks for.

docs.title: How the noise is keyed
docs.text:
The jitter of frame t comes from the frame's own random stream, keyed by the seed, a fixed stream code (JITTER_STREAM in constants/streams.py) and the frame's position in the pool.

So the noise of a frame does not depend on which attacks are placed, nor on where the walk stops and starts. Two timelines built from one seed and one pool with different families carry the same benign scans. Only the attacks differ.

The biases are part of the plan, so they are fixed by the seed too.

docs.title: What is not in a file
docs.text: A timeline file stores the meter masks, not the table. It does not store each meter's accuracy class (the table KIND_ACCURACY gives it) or its bias (drawn from the seed).

docs.title: Where next
docs.text:
• The attack families: what an attack adds to a scan.
  • Layers and labels: how a scan is stored.
  • Formulas: the noise equations and their sources.

docs.title: Solving: power flow and optimal power flow
docs.text: A timeline starts from a pool: the AC operating point of every frame (How the package flows). Solving is the step that builds the pool (Build the operating points has the commands). There are two kinds of solve, and every model in the package is AC.

docs.title: The two kinds
docs.text:
Power flow. The loads and each generator's output are given. The solve finds the voltage at every bus that satisfies the AC equations. Nothing is chosen.

Optimal power flow (OPF). The generator outputs are not given. The solve chooses them to make a cost as small as possible, while the AC equations and the limits of the units and the voltages hold. It is an optimization problem and needs a nonlinear solver.

docs.title: Where each is used
docs.text:
Building the pool, with each builder's own choice (the setting changes it):

Test system Solve Code IEEE cases one power flow per step, in pandapower generate_states in data/ieee_pool.py New York one OPF per frame, in Pyomo with Ipopt IpoptSolver.dispatch in data/ipopt_solver.py New York then one power flow at the OPF's outputs, in pandapower PandapowerSolver.power_flow in data/pandapower_solver.py

The two engines are two classes behind one interface, Solver (data/solver.py). IpoptSolver is the package's own OPF, a Pyomo model solved by Ipopt. PandapowerSolver builds a pandapower net from the Case and runs pandapower's power flow and its OPF.

Only one solve is shared by both engines: opf(pd, qd, costs), the AC point of least cost for the bus loads, with every unit and every voltage within the case's limits and no branch limit. power_flow is PandapowerSolver's only. project and dispatch, the New York dispatch's own OPFs, are IpoptSolver's only.

The released IEEE power flow does not go through Solver. generate_states runs it on the net pandapower ships, as it always has, because the released pools depend on that net bit for bit.

PoolBuilder (data/pool.py) runs the New York solves in time order. First, IpoptSolver.project solves one OPF per hour: the AC point closest to the source model's hourly outputs. The nuclear, hydro and external units follow these hourly points. Then each frame is dispatched. A thermal unit's output may differ from its output in the frame before by at most its ramp. A New York frame that does not solve keeps its place in the pool with an empty state. An IEEE step whose power flow does not converge is dropped from the pool.

After the pool exists, a benign scan needs no solve: it is read from the stored state. Only the attacks solve again, and only on a small area of the grid.

Attack design Solve Code At and Am, on every test system a local AC solve in numpy local_ac_solve, local_flow_solve in formulas/network.py

data/ipopt.py has one function, ipopt. Every OPF in Ipopt gets its solver from it. It finds Ipopt, checks that it starts, and raises SolverUnavailable with the fix when it does not.

Case.from_ieee also solves the base power flow of an IEEE case once, in pandapower.

docs.title: What to install
docs.text:
You want to Install load a released timeline pip install fdia-graph generate an IEEE timeline pip install "fdia-graph[generate]" (pandapower) build the New York pool pip install "fdia-graph[ny]" (pandapower, Pyomo), and Ipopt generate a New York timeline from a pool pip install "fdia-graph[ny]"; no Ipopt

Ipopt is a program, not a Python package, so pip does not install it:

conda install -c conda-forge ipopt

Check that the package finds it:

from fdia_graph.data.ipopt import ipopt

print(ipopt().version())

docs.title: The solve setting
docs.text:
The pool-building step of every test system takes one setting, SolveSettings (models/config.py). It has two fields:

Field Values Meaning method "power_flow", "opf" how each step is solved engine "pandapower", "ipopt" what runs the solve

Leave the setting out and each builder solves as the first table says: generate_states with a power flow in pandapower, PoolBuilder.from_settings with an OPF in Ipopt. The generator reads the pool and does not solve again.

import numpy as np

from fdia_graph.data.ieee_pool import generate_states
from fdia_graph.models.config import SolveSettings

profile = np.sin(np.arange(288) / 46.0)
pool = generate_states(118, profile, solve=SolveSettings(method="opf", engine="ipopt"))

What each choice does:

Test system method engine Result IEEE power_flow pandapower the default: the released pools IEEE opf ipopt a least-cost OPF per step IEEE opf pandapower the same problem, in pandapower New York opf ipopt the default: the dispatch described above New York opf pandapower refused New York power_flow pandapower refused any power_flow ipopt refused

docs.title: An IEEE pool by OPF
docs.text:
An IEEE OPF step scales the loads as the power-flow step does, then chooses each generator's output. The limits are the case's own. The cost is the case's own cost curve, read by Case.pandapower_costs into a UnitCosts: the linear term ($/MWh) and the quadratic term ($/MW^2h) of each unit. The constant term is not read. It does not change the optimum, and it is not in the cost an OPF reports. Branch ratings are not enforced, and the voltage at the reference bus is free within its limits.

Every step is solved from the same start, the case's base state. The pool is therefore the same for any number of workers.

A step with no optimum is dropped, as a step whose power flow does not converge is. At their base loads IEEE-57, IEEE-145, IEEE-200 and IEEE-300 have no optimum within the case's limits in either engine. An OPF pool in which no step has an optimum raises DataConditionError.

docs.title: Why a choice is refused
docs.text:
Each refusal is a ConfigError.

  • A power flow in Ipopt: the Ipopt engine solves an OPF only. pandapower runs every power flow.
  • New York with a power flow: PoolBuilder builds by OPF only. The source model gives hourly generator outputs, and a power flow at those outputs leaves voltages far below the case's limits. A power flow at given outputs is PandapowerSolver(case).power_flow.
  • New York with pandapower's OPF: the dispatch limits each unit's change between frames by its ramp and holds the hydro and external units near their schedule by a penalty. pandapower's OPF solves plain least cost only.

The New York power flow was measured on 40 hours of 2019, every 219th hour, each from a flat start at the source model's outputs and the case's voltage setpoints. All 40 converged. The lowest bus voltage was between 0.72 and 0.82 p.u., where the case's lower limit is 0.9, and the reference bus made up between 1,001 and 2,532 MW. No hour was within the voltage limits.

One New York operating point at plain least cost can be solved in either engine, with IpoptSolver(case).opf(pd, qd, costs) or PandapowerSolver(case).opf(pd, qd, costs).

docs.title: The two OPF engines compared
docs.text:
tests/nygrid/test_solve_engines.py solves the same case, loads and costs in both engines and checks that they agree.

The cost is what the OPF makes as small as possible: each unit's cost curve at the output the solve gives it, summed over the units. It is a rate at one operating point, in dollars per hour. It is the generators' running cost, not a price anyone pays, and it holds no fixed or start-up cost. Two engines that report the same cost found dispatches that are equally cheap; where units tie on cost, the outputs can still differ.

Case Cost, Ipopt ($/h) Cost, pandapower ($/h) Time, Ipopt Time, pandapower IEEE-14 8,081.526 8,081.527 0.09 s 0.40 s IEEE-30 574.517 574.517 0.09 s 0.33 s IEEE-118 129,668.852 129,668.854 0.18 s 0.71 s New York, 70 % load 417,428.790 417,428.797 0.22 s 3.69 s

The IEEE rows use the case's base loads and its linear and quadratic cost, the curves pandapower ships with the case. The New York row uses a flat linear cost per fuel that the test sets (FUEL_PRICE): it is not the cost of running New York. On these four the cost agrees within 0.01 %, the losses within 0.01 MW and every unit's output within 0.1 MW. The times are one solve on one desktop machine, after the model is built.

The engines agree on every unit's output only where the optimum is one point. IEEE-89 has linear costs and several units at the same cost: the two costs agree to 2 parts in 10 million, and single units differ by up to about 20 MW. Over a load profile on IEEE-14, a unit near its lower limit differs by up to 0.3 MW between the engines at the same cost.

pandapower's OPF of the net it ships gives 8,081.527 $/h on IEEE-14, the same problem. On IEEE-30 it gives 578.486 $/h against 574.517 here. That net's OPF also enforces branch ratings, which this problem does not: with the ratings lifted it gives 575.352 $/h. The rest of the difference is not accounted for.

pandapower's OPF is fragile on the New York case. At the case's base load, and at 80 %, 90 % and 105 % of it, it does not converge where Ipopt does. The comparison therefore uses 70 % of the base load. Even there it depends on the machine: it converges on Windows and not on the Linux test runner, where the test reports that it was skipped. The IEEE comparisons run everywhere Ipopt is installed.

docs.title: Repeating a solve
docs.text: On the machine that records the repository's reference digests, two builds of the same New York pool in one process are identical to the last bit. On the Linux test runner the Ipopt solve repeats a voltage to about 1e-6 p.u., and a reactive injection less closely, so two builds there are not the same bytes. tests/nygrid/test_solve_engines.py therefore compares the builders, the frames solved and the voltages to 1e-3 p.u., not bytes or injections.

docs.title: Test systems
docs.text: A test system is a power grid the package can build a timeline on. Every system is the same class, a Case, and goes through the same stages (How the package flows).

docs.title: What a Case is
docs.text:
Case (systems/case.py) is one grid as a frozen record of arrays: the buses, the branches, the generating units, the HVDC links if any, and a base operating state. Powers are in MW and MVAr, impedances in per unit on base_mva, angles in degrees. Branch ends are positions into the bus arrays, not bus numbers.

There are three ways to make one.

Call Reads Case.from_ieee(118) the case of that bus count that pandapower ships, with its base power flow solved Case.from_pandapower(net) a pandapower net whose power flow is solved Case.from_matpower(path) a MATPOWER case file laid out like the New York one

Each of them ends with case.check, which refuses a bus type that is not MATPOWER's 1, 2 or 3, a case without exactly one reference bus, and a list of names, coordinates, fuels or ramps with the wrong number of rows. from_pandapower refuses a net that holds something a Case does not model, such as a three-winding transformer or an element out of service. Every refusal is a DataConditionError that says what is wrong.

from fdia_graph.systems.case import Case, nygrid_case
from fdia_graph.systems.network import Network

ieee = Case.from_ieee(14)      # needs fdia-graph[generate]
new_york = nygrid_case()       # needs fdia-graph[ny]
net = Network(new_york)        # admittances, built once
print(len(ieee.bus_id), len(new_york.bus_id))  # 14 140

docs.title: The systems
docs.text:
System Source case Buses Branches ieee14 case14 14 20 ieee30 case30 30 41 ieee57 case57 57 80 ieee89 case89pegase 89 210 ieee118 case118 118 186 ieee145 case145 145 453 ieee200 case_illinois200 200 245 ieee300 case300 300 411 New York case_nygrid.m 140 227

The first eight source cases are builders of pandapower.networks, listed in IEEE_CASES (constants/grid.py). A branch is a line or a transformer. The New York grid has 271 units.

ratings/ holds PGLib-OPF line ratings for ieee14, ieee118 and ieee300. The cases pandapower ships carry none.

docs.title: The New York case file
docs.text:
src/fdia_graph/systems/case_nygrid.m is the project's own test system. It is one MATPOWER case file, shipped inside the package. A change to the grid is an edit to that file.
