docs.title: Class map
docs.text:
How the pieces of the two toolkits connect, the generation toolkit fdia_graph and the analysis toolkit fdia_analysis: one module diagram of both and eight class diagrams, all drawn from the source by tools/class_diagrams.py (the AST gives each class's public methods, its bases and the classes of other modules it names), so they cannot drift from the code. CI checks that the committed sources match; python tools/class_diagrams.py rewrites them and tools/render_mermaid.py renders. Read with MODULES.md (what each file is for) and CONCEPTS_TO_CODE.md (which function implements which idea).

An open arrowhead is inheritance, a dashed arrow is a class using another (an argument type, a return type or a collaborator it builds), and a box marked with another package's name is a participant that lives there.

The diagrams are wide and are best viewed on a wide screen. Each picture links to its full-size file.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text: Which module imports which, in one picture with a box per toolkit: every arrow between the boxes runs from the analysis toolkit to the generation toolkit, never back. Five foundations are read by nearly every module and are left out so the real dependencies show: each toolkit's models/ (the returned records and the settings; the one validation engine is fdia_graph.models.validation) and formulas/ (the equations), and the generation toolkit's constants/ (the facts, each with its unit and source), schema.py (the file protocol) and errors.py (the named errors). Each package's own __init__.py (for fdia_graph, the fg.* public API, which imports everything) is left out for the same reason.

docs.title: The dataset
docs.text: FdiaGraph is the file. Five mixins over DatasetBase give it its faces: the static graph physics (GraphMixin), the admittance matrices (AdmittanceMixin), records and batches (RecordsMixin), the exports (ExportMixin) and the time-ordered windows and episodes (SequenceMixin). The methods that produce records return models bundles (a record, a batch, an exported split, the episode table, the summary); the graph properties are tensors or arrays, loader() is a DataLoader and windows() a tuple.

docs.title: The engine
docs.text: FdiaGenerator is the AC model of one test system with its meter plan: the Network of its Case (an IEEE case's is Network.from_ieee), a MeterPlan (MeterPlan.from_coverage, or a plan given), a Measurement and a NoiseModel. It also holds one object of each of its parts (engine/base.py, Part): a part does one job and holds the generator, so it reads the grid as self.g.case and calls another part as self.g.area.hop_area(...). ScanLoads (g.scan_loads) reads a scan's load and generation and Emitter (g.emitter) emits scans; the parts of engine/attacks/ build every attack (next section). Emitter.benign_frame emits a benign scan, and a designed episode (engine/attacks/family.py, DesignedEpisode) asks the parts for each attacked one; timeline.py decides when and where each episode runs.

docs.title: The attacks
docs.text: Every attack is built in engine/attacks/, one part of the generator per module: AttackArea (g.area) finds the attacker's area, FalseState (g.false_state) solves and checks its false state, AttackFrames (g.attack_frames) writes the attack vector onto the true scan, RampFrames (g.ramp_frames) builds the ramp frames, Minimizer (g.minimizer) finds the support that tampers the fewest devices over an attack window [WU26, eq. 12] (AttackWindow, window.py, counts what a support costs), Overload (g.overload) builds the overload Am, and EpisodeDesigns (g.episode_designs) designs what an At or an Am episode attacks. RampFrames.ramp_frame is the one entry for an attacked At scan; an Am frame comes from overload_step. The walk reaches both through a designed episode (engine/attacks/search.py: RampEpisode, OverloadEpisode).

docs.title: State estimation
docs.text: SEBase holds the shared solve: the measurement function, the chord Jacobian, the meter weights and the chord-Newton loop. Each estimator overrides one hook. GatedPrior takes a fitted localizer as its gate; JacobianFeatures is the per-bus feature block the localizers can consume.

docs.title: Localization and trusted meters
docs.text: LocalizerBase calibrates any per-bus score to one false-alarm budget; the threshold arms score a stored feature, ResidualLocalizer runs an estimator, the learned arms train a per-bus network. TrustSelector chooses the meters to secure on the WLS Jacobian, by row reduction (TrustedMeters) or by a deep Q-network (TrustedMetersDQN), and scores the residual test with them secured.

docs.title: Federated training
docs.text: FederatedLocalizer is a LearnedLocalizer whose fit runs FedAvg over a Partition of the buses: each client trains its own copy with the shared LocalTrainer on its own buses, and FedBusMLP and FedBusCNN take their encoder from BusMLP and BusCNN. RoundLog records every round. RegionalPrior is a SubspacePrior whose basis is fitted per client of a Partition.

docs.title: The records
docs.text: Everything a call returns is a Bundle, a dict with attribute access and a fixed key order. The record forms share one base, RecordFields, which declares every field once, so a record, a batch and an exported split carry the same names. An exported split adds the export-only prev_* fields (the previous frame's readings on a timeline).

docs.title: The scores
docs.text:
The result of every score() is a Bundle too, defined in the analysis toolkit (fdia_analysis.models.scores) on the generation toolkit's Bundle: ErrorPair and EstimatorScores for the estimators, OverallMetrics, BenignMetrics, FamilyMetrics and LocalizerScores for the localizers, TrustScores for the trusted meters, JacobianOutputs for the feature block; TrueState (fdia_analysis.models.data) is the truth an estimator is scored against.

The named tuples of models/frames.py (Scan, Frame, OperatingLimits, FrameKnobs), models/grid.py (BranchModel, Admittances) and models/assets.py (AssetSpec) are plain value types with no hierarchy, so they appear only where a class above uses them.

docs.title: Concepts to code
docs.text: Paper ideas → the function that implements them. Pair with DATA_DICTIONARY.md. Paths are under src/fdia_graph/; se/ and localization/ are under analysis/src/fdia_analysis/.

docs.title: One record, start to finish
docs.text:
Each frame of a timeline is one record. Its operating state is one frame of the pool. The clean layer is Measurement.h of that state with no noise (Emitter.exact); the node layer clean is the state itself. Emitter.emit_from_state adds each meter's bias and the scan's jitter (NoiseModel), which gives the benign layer. On an attacked frame AttackFrames.frame_from_state adds the attack vector on the meters it moves, which gives the observed layer; on a benign frame the observed layer is the benign one. TimelineWriter.store writes the three layers with the labels y, family and seq_id and the tamper masks. An episode designed as a vector over the meters (VectorEpisode) uses AttackFrames.frame_from_vector instead. Layers and labels says what each layer and label is for.

Every attack is built in engine.attacks, by the parts the generator holds: a local false state (engine.attacks.false_state) designed per episode (ramp_design for At, am_overload_design for Am, engine.attacks.episodes) on a support the search or [WU26]'s row reduction chooses (Minimizer.min_tamper, RrefSupport); AttackFrames.frame_from_state adds the attack vector to the benign scan.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
The paper's math lives in engine/. generation/ drives it in stages (TimelineSource.generate is the one path of them for both grids, timeline.py its IEEE entry point), data/ turns load series into operating points (data/profiles.py the load profiles, data/ieee_pool.py the solve); se/ and localization/ analyze the timelines; the rest load and serve data. What every file does, from its docstring, is MODULES.md (generated by tools/layout.py); FORMULAS.md maps each formula to its function.

engine/ file formula it implements core.py FdiaGenerator: grid + noise setup (__init__), attack targeting; holds one object of each part (measurement, loads, the attacks) measurement.py emit_from_state (a scan: Measurement.h, the measurement function h(x), with NoiseModel's noise), clean_flows_from_states, currents_from_states physics.py true_load, scan_generation: a scan's load and generation from its stored state attacks/ the false states, the fewest-tamper search, the At ramp and the overload Am

One column order everywhere: the operating-state pool, node_x, and clean are all [|V|, P_inj, Q_inj, theta]. Pools saved before 0.12 were P-first; generation.as_v_first detects and converts them on load.

docs.title: State estimation
docs.text:
concept code WLS x̂ = argmin (z−h(x))ᵀW(z−h(x)) se/base.py SEBase._w_solve (chord-Newton); h(x) is ac_measurement (analysis/src/fdia_analysis/formulas/measurement.py) Robust reweighting (Huber), residual removal, subspace prior se/methods.py: one class per arm, each overrides one hook Bad-data test r_i=(z_i−h_i)/σ_i, J=Σr_i² σ_i is the RMS of the benign residuals at the training truth (se/base.py SEBase.fit); residuals in se/base.py SEBase._nres. The stealthy flag marks the families that evade it by construction (Aq/At/Al/Am, constants.families.STEALTHY_FAMILIES) Noise model FdiaGenerator.SD (accuracy class): reading = true + per-meter bias + per-scan jitter. The estimator does not read it; it calibrates σ_i from data Meter model (hybrid SCADA and PMU) MeterPlan.from_placement (the angle at the PMU buses only; the generator's masks, a MeterLayers, are its masks) and the kinds IR and II of Measurement.h (the PMU branch currents I_f = Y_f V, I_t = Y_t V, formulas.network.branch_currents, noise formulas.noise.current_sigma); chosen by generate_timeline(..., redundancy={"meter_model": ...}) through models.config.MeterSettings PMU pseudo-measurements V_f = (I_n − y_nn V_n)/y_nf [WU26, eq. (3)] formulas.estimation.pmu_pseudo_links, pmu_pseudo_voltages (with the propagated variance), used by SEBase(solve=SolveConfig(pmu_pseudo=True)) in _build_pseudo and _z_of

Walkthrough: ../guides/state_estimation.md. Results: ../analysis/estimation/README.md.

docs.title: Attack families
docs.text:
family paper build code At A_t slow ramp, 0.2 percent per frame, a local false state per frame engine/attacks/episodes.EpisodeDesigns.ramp_design + EpisodeDesigns.ramp_step Am A_m the overload attack of [WU26]: a line's reported flow driven to its rating over the window, the fewest devices tampered engine/attacks/episodes.EpisodeDesigns.am_overload_design + overload.overload_step
  • At and Am are local false states: the buses around the attack are re-solved with the boundary voltages held true, inside the case's voltage limits and the region's generator limits, and the attack vector h(x') − h(x) is added to the benign scan. The residual test flags them at the benign rate by construction. Both satisfy equations (13)-(23) of [WU26] (the SCADA measurements, the PMU voltage magnitudes, angles and branch currents, and the operating limits). Am also drives a line's reported flow to its rating, eqs. (24)-(25) (by default 1.25 times its peak pool flow), on the support that tampers the fewest devices, eq. (12); At is held on that support when min_tamper=True (the default), else on the region within hops (../concepts/attacks.md). The single-snapshot families of older releases (Aq, Al, and the in-place Ad, As, Ar) are read-only: fdia-graph 0.20 generates them.
  • With min_tamper=True an At episode is held on the support that tampers the fewest devices over the episode, the objective of [WU26, eq. 12] (engine/attacks/minimize.Minimizer.min_tamper, called by engine/attacks/episodes.EpisodeDesigns.ramp_design).
  • The At ramp moves in per-frame steps under the noise floor, by design.

docs.title: Temporal feature
docs.text:
field meaning built in temporal_delta scan-to-scan [ΔP, ΔQ] of the observed frames generation.write.TimelineWriter.write_temporal_layers (formulas.temporal.temporal_delta) swing temporal_delta as a z-score of the recent observed change generation.write.TimelineWriter.write_temporal_layers (formulas.temporal.swing_zscore, scale from recent_change_scale)

Both layers are written after the walk from the observed injections only, so a detector reads what an operator sees.

Any above-noise attack spikes the swing, so localization is per-bus and needs no graph. The slow ramp At stays inside the swing, so it is the open case.

docs.title: The papers' per-bus feature vector and localizers
docs.text: concept code 14-dim per-bus vector: [|V|,P,Q,θ] + meter mask + partial KCL residual + temporal_delta + swing localization/learned.py full14, kcl_residual standardize all 14 channels on train (sd floored at 1e-3) LearnedLocalizer._fit_stats 1-D CNN across the bus axis (best localizer) BusCNN per-bus MLP (lightweight arm) BusMLP validation-best global threshold on a 0.05..0.95 grid LearnedLocalizer.tune_threshold

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text: metric definition code node precision / recall / F1 micro over every (record, bus) pair localization/base.py LocalizerBase.score per-sample macro-F1 F1 per record, averaged same strict localization accuracy predicted attacked set equals the truth exactly same DR with FA detection rate, always reported next to the benign false-alarm rate same localization macro-F1 per-bus F1 averaged over the active buses, those attacked somewhere in the records scored (the papers' headline) LocalizerBase.score(...)["all"]["macro_f1"]; also EXAMPLES.md macro_f1

docs.title: Data dictionary
docs.text:
What every array from fg.load() holds, as a record (order="random") or as a frame of the timeline (order="time").

N = number of buses (nodes), E = number of branches (edges). A shape is "values per item": [N,4] = 4 numbers per bus, [E,8] = an 8-dim vector per branch, [2,E] = 2 rows × E branches.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text:
field shape columns meaning node_x [N,4] |V|, P_inj, Q_inj, theta bus meter readings node_m [N,4] same columns 1 metered, 0 not (value zero-filled) edge_x [E,2] P_from, Q_from power leaving the branch (sign = direction) edge_m as edge_x same columns 1 metered, 0 not edge_index [2,E] row 0 from_bus, row 1 to_bus connectivity edge_attr [E,8] r, x, b, g, gs, bs, tap, shift static branch electrical properties y [N] 1 attacked, 0 clean. Which buses family scalar 0 benign, 1 Aq, 2 Ad, 3 As, 4 Ar, 5 At, 6 Al, 7 Am. Which attack temporal_delta [N,2] ΔP, ΔQ injection change against the previous frame swing [N,2] ΔP, ΔQ temporal_delta as a z-score of recent volatility benign [N,4] same as node_x the same scan with the attack removed, noise kept (timelines) edge_benign [E,2] same as edge_x the same flows with the attack removed, noise kept (timelines) clean [N,4] same as node_x noiseless truth, all buses. The SE target (v0.7.2+) edge_clean [E,2] same as edge_x noiseless true flows, unmetered branches zeroed edge_clean_full [E,2] same as edge_x noiseless true flows on every branch, metered or not (computed from clean through yf on load; equals edge_clean where a flow meter exists)

One layout. Every file the package writes has from-end flows [E,2], currents as real and imaginary parts, and both temporal features. A file that declares another layout (attrs["edge_feat"] naming four flows, or attrs["current_form"] other than rectangular) is refused with NotATimeline when it is opened. A file built from a pool with times carries data/time (int64 seconds), and one built with the owners of its buses carries graph/bus_client with the attribute client_names. Layers and labels says more.

docs.title: Labels: y says which buses, family says which attack
docs.text:
Two fields, two questions. y [N] is binary per bus because a bus is either tampered with or not. family is one code per record because the generator runs one attack episode at a time, on one or more buses at once; episodes never overlap, so each frame has one active family. That is a property of how these files were built, not of the schema: concurrent attacks of different families would need a separate per-bus family map, say bus_family [N] with 0 on clean buses (so y = bus_family > 0), added next to the scalar family in a new data release.

shape values in a batch y [N] 0 clean, 1 attacked batch["y"] [B,N] (PyG: batch.y [B*N]) family scalar 0 benign, 1 Aq, 2 Ad, 3 As, 4 Ar, 5 At, 6 Al, 7 Am (timelines only) batch["family"] [B] (PyG: batch.family [B])
  • Names: fg.FAMILIES[code]. Stealthy subset: fg.STEALTHY_FAMILIES = {1, 5, 6, 7}.
  • Per-bus family label, if a model needs one: y * family[:, None] gives [B,N] with 0 on clean buses.
  • Every attacked record flags at least one bus. Benign records flag none.
  • Per-family evaluation: filter by family and score y inside each group. fg.load(..., families=[...]) does the filtering at load time.

docs.title: node_x [N,4]: bus measurements (voltage first)
docs.text:
The column order is defined once, in fdia_graph.constants.channels.NodeChannel (V, P_INJ, Q_INJ, THETA). A member is its column number, so it indexes a numpy array or a tensor directly, and the generator, the loader and the estimator index columns through NodeChannel and EdgeChannel rather than literals:

from fdia_graph.constants.channels import NodeChannel

rec = ds[0]
rec.node_x[..., NodeChannel.THETA]  # the angle column, a view of rec.node_x[..., 3]
ds.export(["clean"]).clean[..., NodeChannel.V]  # any [..., 4] array, a split's clean layer included
col name physical units pu units 0 |V| per-unit per-unit 1 P_inj MW pu 2 Q_inj MVAr pu 3 theta degrees radians

Sign of P_inj/Q_inj: + = net consumption (load), − = net injection (gen). This is pandapower's res_bus convention. Example (case14): the slack bus reads ≈ −235 MW, a 94 MW load bus reads ≈ +93 MW. Every file the package's source writes has this sign, a New York file too: SearchSource.for_pool turns the pool's injections to it.

docs.title: edge_attr [E,8]: static branch properties (per-unit, never change)
docs.text:
col name meaning 0 r series impedance, real part (resistance). Z = r + jx 1 x series impedance, imag part (reactance) 2 b total line-charging susceptance. The pi model puts b/2 at each end; it is stored whole, not halved 3 g total charging conductance (transformer iron losses, 0 on lines), also stored whole 4 gs series admittance, real part (conductance). Y = 1/(r+jx) = gs + j·bs 5 bs series admittance, imag part (susceptance) 6 tap transformer tap ratio (1.0 = plain line) 7 shift transformer phase shift, degrees (0 = plain line)
  • r,x and gs,bs are the same branch inverted (Y = 1/Z). Both ship so you never compute one from the other.
  • Bus shunts are not branch properties and are not in this table: ds.bus_shunt_g / ds.bus_shunt_b in MW / MVAr at 1 pu (divide by ds.baseMVA for per-unit admittance). ds.ybus already includes them on the diagonal, together with the halved charging and the tap / shift handling.
  • In PyG format (fg.load(..., format="pyg")), Data.edge_attr is the [E,2] flows (also exposed as Data.edge_x) and this [E,8] table is Data.edge_phys. On the dataset object it is ds.edge_attr.

docs.title: Where the branch flows live, per format
docs.text:
you have flows [E,2] flow mask [E,2] static line physics [E,8] dict record ds[i] or a ds.loader() batch ["edge_x"] ["edge_m"] ["edge_attr"] PyG Data or DataBatch (format="pyg") .edge_attr or .edge_x .edge_mask .edge_phys ds.export() ["edge_x"] [n,E,2] ["edge_m"] ds.edge_attr

One name to watch: the static table's graph/edge_x is the per-unit series reactance of each branch (ds.branch_x), unrelated to the per-record flow layer edge_x above; the on-disk name changes at the next data release, the reader already spells the two apart.

The [E,8] physics keep the name edge_attr on dicts and the dataset, and become edge_phys on PyG objects because PyG's edge_attr slot is its conventional home for per-edge model input, which here are the flows.

Flows are per record, so they only exist on records and batches. The static per-unit branch physics live on the dataset as ds.edge_attr [E,8] and one column each as ds.branch_r, ds.branch_x, ds.branch_b, ds.branch_g, ds.branch_gs, ds.branch_bs, ds.branch_tap, ds.branch_shift. They are named branch_* because edge_x is the flows' name.

docs.title: The rest
docs.text: field shape meaning edge_x [E,2] [P_from, Q_from], power leaving the from-end (sign = direction). MW/MVAr or pu. node_m, edge_m [N,4], as edge_x 1 metered, 0 not. Metering is sparse: read the mask. edge_index [2,E] row 0 from-bus, row 1 to-bus y, family [N], scalar see Labels above (Aq = paper A_o) slack dataset attribute index of the reference (slack) bus, ds.slack. Derived from the clean layer. Also Data.slack in PyG format ybus dataset attribute full nodal admittance matrix [N,N], complex per-unit, in node_x bus order: ds.ybus (torch complex128) or ds.ybus_np. Built from edge_attr and the bus shunts with pandapower's branch model, equal to the engine's matrix. Static per shard, so it lives on the dataset, not on each record yf, yt dataset attributes from-end and to-end branch admittance matrices [E,N] (rows follow edge_index, columns node_x bus order): ds.yf / ds.yt (torch complex128) or ds.yf_np / ds.yt_np. For a complex bus voltage vector V, V[from] * conj(Yf @ V) is the from-end branch flow in per-unit (times baseMVA gives edge_x / edge_clean units). Same construction as makeYbus stealthy scalar 1 for the re-solve families Aq/At/Al/Am (fg.STEALTHY_FAMILIES, BDD-evading by construction), 0 for benign and Ad/As/Ar seq_id scalar index of the attack episode the frame belongs to, for every family; -1 on benign frames split scalar 0/1/2 = train/val/test timestep scalar position in the source load profile

docs.title: clean, edge_clean and edge_clean_full (v0.7.2+, edge_clean_full v0.15.0+)
docs.text:
• The noiseless, attack-free truth at the record's timestep, in node_x column order.
  • clean covers every bus with no mask, whatever the meter placement.
  • edge_clean zeroes unmetered branches, like edge_x.
  • edge_clean_full is the same true flow on every branch, metered or not, computed from clean through yf when the file is loaded (V[from] * conj(Yf @ V), times baseMVA). It equals edge_clean wherever a flow meter exists, so a graph model can supervise every edge.
  • On benign records node_x − clean is the meter error.
  • This is the state-estimation target.

docs.title: The three layers of a frame
docs.text:
Every frame of a timeline carries three aligned layers, for node and for edge measurements (Layers and labels explains what each is for and which a feature may read):

layer meaning node_x / edge_x observed (attacked + noise). The model input. benign / edge_benign attack removed, noise kept clean / edge_clean noiseless true state. The SE target.
  • benign − clean = noise.
  • observed − benign = the attack, exactly, for every family: the observed scan is the benign draw plus the attack. For Aq/At/Al/Am that is the attack vector of the local false state on the meters it moves (the tamper masks); the rest read benign exactly. clean is the SE target.

docs.title: The timeline file
docs.text:
group datasets note attrs system, N, E, baseMVA, seed, T, families, kind="timeline", the knobs, attacked_frac ds.summary() and the registry read these data/ node_x, node_m, edge_x, edge_m, y, family, stealthy, seq_id, timestep, split, temporal_delta, swing one row per frame, time order benign/ node_benign, edge_benign the attack removed clean/ node_clean, edge_clean the noiseless truth per frame graph/ edge_index and the static branch physics and bus shunts the same for every frame episodes/ onset, length, family, bus_ptr, bus_idx ds.episodes attack/ mag_ptr, mag_bus, mag, node_tamper, edge_tamper designed magnitude per attacked bus, unsigned (a load rise and a drop of the same size record the same value); the meters the attacker wrote data/, benign/, attack/ pmu_i, pmu_i_m; pmu_i_benign; pmu_i_tamper hybrid-meter files only (attrs["meter_model"] == "hybrid", new generation): the PMU branch currents [T, E, 4], see below

On a hybrid-meter file a SCADA voltmeter reads no angle, so node_m[:, 3] is 1 at the PMU buses only, and each PMU reads the current phasor of every in-service branch at its bus [WU26, eqs. 19-20]. The columns of pmu_i are defined in fdia_graph.constants.channels.CurrentChannel (RE_FROM, IM_FROM, RE_TO, IM_TO): the real and imaginary part of I_from = Y_f V and I_to = Y_t V in per unit on the base current, the same on a units="pu" or "physical" view, zero where no PMU reads that end (pmu_i_m is 0 there). pmu_i_benign is the attack-removed twin and pmu_i_tamper marks the channels the attacker wrote. A file without these datasets (every released file) loads unchanged and its records carry no pmu_i. export(["prev_pmu_i"]) gives the previous emitted frame's currents on a hybrid-meter timeline, like prev_node_x.

Chunked along the frame axis so a window of W frames is one read. A file without the kind attribute timeline (a record shard of a data release before v0.8.0) is refused with NotATimeline.

docs.title: Where the constants and the models are defined
docs.text:
A value nothing in a run changes is a constant. Each one is defined once, with its unit and its source, in a module of src/fdia_graph/constants/. The modules import nothing from the rest of the toolkit.

Module, under src/fdia_graph/ Holds constants/channels.py the column of each quantity in a measurement array, as enums: node_x[..., NodeChannel.P_INJ] constants/families.py the attack families and their codes constants/meters.py the meter kinds, the accuracy classes and the noise floors constants/grid.py the IEEE cases, the bus types, the "no limit" ratings constants/time.py the calendar, the New York frame, and how a load profile is correlated from scan to scan constants/streams.py the keys of the random streams constants/numerics.py the fixed tolerances constants/records.py the fields of a record, by group constants/files.py the names and layouts of the files around a timeline constants/releases.py where the datasets are published, the pinned data release and its sha256 values constants/newyork.py the New York grid: the NYISO zones, the fields of the case file, the pinned inputs, the dispatch numbers and the fitted load model

schema.py holds the file protocol instead: every group, dataset and attribute name of a timeline file. A value a user tunes is not a constant: it is a field of a settings model.

Every bundle of values a toolkit passes or returns is a model. A model is imported from its module; a models/ package exports no name.

Module, under src/ Holds fdia_graph/models/base.py Bundle, the base of every model fdia_graph/models/fields.py the fields the record bundles share fdia_graph/models/grid.py the static description of a system: the branch model and the admittance matrices fdia_graph/models/frames.py what the generator passes around per scan: a scan, a frame, an episode's design fdia_graph/models/plan.py a timeline's plan and its design records fdia_graph/models/data.py what a user gets back: a record, a batch, a whole split, a summary, the episode table fdia_graph/models/assets.py where a dataset comes from and where its bytes are fetched from fdia_graph/models/config.py the settings fdia_graph/models/inputs.py what the formulas and the parsers accept fdia_graph/models/validation.py the one engine that checks them fdia_graph/models/choices.py the arguments with a fixed set of values Module, under analysis/src/ Holds fdia_analysis/models/config.py the settings of the analysis packages, checked by the generation toolkit's engine fdia_analysis/models/inputs.py what the analysis formulas accept fdia_analysis/models/choices.py the arguments with a fixed set of values fdia_analysis/models/scores.py the score tables fdia_analysis/models/data.py the truth an estimator is scored against fdia_analysis/models/grid.py the estimator's pseudo-measurement records fdia_analysis/models/federated.py how the buses split into clients fdia_analysis/models/training.py what the learned localizers pass between their fitting pieces fdia_analysis/models/results.py the records of the results store

The section below lists every field of the models a user receives.

docs.text: Every dict the two toolkits return is a typed bundle (fdia_graph.models.base.Bundle): a frozen dataclass that is also the dict it always was, so out["node_x"], **out and iteration keep working and out.node_x is new. Fields set to None are absent from the dict. The loader's bundles are the generation toolkit's (fdia_graph.models), the score tables the analysis toolkit's (fdia_analysis.models). docs.title: Examples and dataset statistics
docs.text:
Runnable baselines to copy, the temporal state-estimation recipe, and per-system statistics of the released data.

Loading a dataset is a tutorial of its own: Load a dataset has the loader's options, batches, exports, windows and episodes. The three layers of a frame are explained in Layers and labels, and every field is defined in DATA_DICTIONARY.md.

docs.title: Recipe: a temporal state estimator (attacked window → clean V/θ)
docs.text:
Feed an LSTM/TGN windows of the attacked measurements and train it to recover the clean state.

import fdia_graph as fg
import numpy as np

ts = fg.load("ieee118", split="train", order="time")

W, stride = 24, 12
Xw, yw = ts.windows(W, stride)  # Xw [n,W,N,4] attacked measurements, yw [n,N] attack label
Cw, _ = ts.windows(W, stride, layer="clean")  # [n,W,N,4] the clean state, windowed the same way

# column order is [|V|, Pinj, Qinj, angle]; the SE target is clean |V| and angle:
target = Cw[..., [0, 3]]  # [n,W,N,2] clean V and theta

# training loop (sketch):
#   pred = model(Xw)                             # your LSTM/TGN: [n,W,N,2] estimated V, theta
#   loss = mse(pred, target)                     # estimated state vs clean V/theta
  • Xw is the attacked, noisy input. target is the clean V/θ it should reconstruct.
  • For a full SE measurement set, window edge_x the same way (ts.export(["edge_x"])) and feed node + edge together. That is exactly what a WLS/robust estimator consumes.
  • Line physics: ts.edge_attr ([E,8]), ts.ybus, ts.yf.
  • Custom timeline: fg.generate(system, name, attacked_frac=0.5, families=[...], seed=...).
  • Temporal features compare each frame to the previous emitted frame, so a stealthy ramp stays a small per-step change while a spike reads as an abrupt jump.

docs.title: Three runnable baselines
docs.text:
All three report DR / FA / F1, never raw accuracy. About 98% of bus-scans are clean, so an all-negative model scores 0.98 accuracy while detecting nothing.

The printed outputs and the tables in this section were recorded on the v0.7.1 ieee118 record shards, before the timeline replaced them in v0.8.0. The code runs unchanged on the default release, and its numbers there differ. Current localization results are in ../analysis/localization/README.md.

  • Thresholds are picked on the val split (best F1). Test is evaluated once at that threshold.
  • Baseline 1 follows the papers' protocol: train on benign + Aq + Ad, hold out As/Ar zero-shot, exclude At, Al and Am, score macro-F1 over the active buses.
  • Baselines 2 and 3 train on every family so the hard ones stay visible.
  • Each trains in a few CPU minutes.
# shared helpers, used by all three examples
import torch


def pick_tau(logits, y):
    """Decision threshold with the best F1 on the VALIDATION split (never tune on test)."""
    best, tau = 0.0, 0.0
    for q in torch.linspace(0.80, 0.999, 60):
        c = torch.quantile(logits, q)
        p = logits > c
        f1 = 2 * (p & y).sum() / (p.sum() + y.sum()).clamp(min=1)
        if f1 > best:
            best, tau = float(f1), float(c)
    return tau


def report(p, t):
    dr = (p & t).sum() / t.sum()
    fa = (p & ~t).sum() / (~t).sum()
    prec = (p & t).sum() / p.sum().clamp(min=1)
    print(f"DR {dr:.3f}  FA {fa:.4f}  F1 {2 * prec * dr / (prec + dr):.3f}")


def macro_f1(p, t):
    """Per-bus F1 averaged over the buses attacked in t (the papers' localization metric)."""
    f1s = []
    for b in range(t.shape[1]):
        if not t[:, b].any():
            continue
        tp = (p[:, b] & t[:, b]).sum()
        fp = (p[:, b] & ~t[:, b]).sum()
        fn = (~p[:, b] & t[:, b]).sum()
        pr = tp / max(tp + fp, 1)
        dr = tp / max(tp + fn, 1)
        f1s.append(2 * pr * dr / max(pr + dr, 1e-12))
    return sum(f1s) / len(f1s)

docs.title: 1. Per-bus MLP on the papers' 14-dim feature vector (the headline localizer)
docs.text:
Each bus is described by 14 numbers:

features count why standardized measurements 4 the readings meter-availability mask 4 tells an unobserved channel from a genuine zero on this sparsely metered grid local Kirchhoff power residual 2 injection minus incident metered flows. Partial where a branch is unmetered; the mask lets the model discount those temporal_delta 2 scan-to-scan change swing 2 windowed z-score of that change

A 28k-parameter MLP under the published protocol, a few CPU minutes; the printed output below is an example recorded on the v0.7.1 shards, not a stored result. Needs pip install "fdia-graph[torch]".

import numpy as np
import torch.nn as nn, torch.nn.functional as F
import fdia_graph as fg

torch.manual_seed(0)
FIELDS = ["node_x", "node_m", "edge_x", "temporal_delta", "swing", "y", "family"]
splits = {
    "train": fg.load("ieee118", split="train", families=[0, 1, 2]).export(FIELDS),
    "val": fg.load("ieee118", split="val", families=[0, 1, 2]).export(FIELDS),
    "test": fg.load("ieee118", split="test", families=[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]).export(FIELDS),
}
ei = fg.load("ieee118", split="train").edge_index_np
N = splits["train"]["node_x"].shape[1]


def kcl(d):
    """Partial nodal power balance: injection minus incident metered branch flows (a true balance only
    where all incident branches are metered; the meter-mask channels flag the rest)."""
    r = np.array(d["node_x"][:, :, 1:3], np.float32)  # start from [P_inj, Q_inj]
    np.subtract.at(r, (slice(None), ei[0]), d["edge_x"])  # flows leaving the from-bus
    np.add.at(r, (slice(None), ei[1]), d["edge_x"])  # arriving at the to-bus
    return r


def feats(d, stats=None):
    """The papers' 14-dim per-bus vector: measurements(4) + meter mask(4) + KCL(2) + delta(2) + swing(2)."""
    raw = np.concatenate([d["node_x"], kcl(d), d["temporal_delta"]], -1)
    if stats is None:
        stats = (raw.mean((0, 1)), raw.std((0, 1)) + 1e-9)  # train statistics only
    z = (raw - stats[0]) / stats[1]
    return np.concatenate([z, d["node_m"], d["swing"]], -1).astype(np.float32), stats


Ftr, st = feats(splits["train"])
X = {"train": torch.tensor(Ftr).reshape(-1, 14)}
for s in ("val", "test"):
    X[s] = torch.tensor(feats(splits[s], st)[0]).reshape(-1, 14)
Y = {s: torch.tensor(d["y"], dtype=torch.float32).reshape(-1) for s, d in splits.items()}

m = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Linear(14, 160),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Dropout(0.1),
    nn.Linear(160, 160),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Dropout(0.1),
    nn.Linear(160, 1),
)
opt = torch.optim.AdamW(m.parameters(), 1e-3)
pw = (1 - Y["train"].mean()) / Y["train"].mean()  # class weight from the TRAIN base rate
for step in range(12000):
    j = torch.randint(0, len(X["train"]), (4096,))
    opt.zero_grad()
    F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(m(X["train"][j]).squeeze(-1), Y["train"][j], pos_weight=pw).backward()
    opt.step()
m.eval()

with torch.no_grad():
    lo = {
        s: torch.cat([m(X[s][i : i + 65536]).squeeze(-1) for i in range(0, len(X[s]), 65536)])
        for s in ("val", "test")
    }
tau = pick_tau(lo["val"], Y["val"] > 0)  # threshold tuned on VAL ...
p = (lo["test"] > tau).reshape(-1, N).numpy()
t = (Y["test"] > 0).reshape(-1, N).numpy()
print(f"localization macro-F1: {macro_f1(p, t):.3f}")  # ... reported on TEST
report(torch.tensor(p.ravel()), torch.tensor(t.ravel()))
# localization macro-F1: 0.915
# DR 0.859  FA 0.0002  F1 0.916          (~5 min CPU)

On those shards the zero-shot families (As, Ar) were the hardest of the four trained-for ones, and adding the excluded families back lowered the pooled F1, almost entirely because the slow ramp At evades the temporal feature by construction. That gap is the open problem this dataset poses. The next two baselines keep it visible by training on every family.

docs.title: 2. Graph model: ARMAConv (PyTorch-Geometric), all families
docs.text:
• format="pyg" yields ready Data objects. swing rides along as a node attribute, the branch flows as edge_attr (alias edge_x) with their mask as edge_mask, and the static [E,8] line physics as edge_phys (pass g.edge_phys as edge_attr to a layer that wants line parameters).
  • preload=True caches the split in RAM so epochs take seconds instead of minutes.
  • Needs pip install "fdia-graph[pyg]".
import torch, torch.nn.functional as F
from torch_geometric.nn import ARMAConv
import fdia_graph as fg

ds = {s: fg.load("ieee118", split=s, format="pyg", preload=True) for s in ("train", "val", "test")}
stats = fg.load("ieee118", split="train").export(["node_x"])["node_x"]
MU = torch.tensor(stats.mean((0, 1)))
SD = torch.tensor(stats.std((0, 1)) + 1e-9)


class GNN(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c=6, h=32):
        super().__init__()
        self.a = ARMAConv(c, h)
        self.b = ARMAConv(h, 1)

    def forward(self, g):
        x = torch.cat([(g.x - MU) / SD, g.swing], -1)  # measurements + the swing feature
        return self.b(F.relu(self.a(x, g.edge_index)), g.edge_index).squeeze(-1)


net = GNN()
opt = torch.optim.Adam(net.parameters(), 1e-3)
pw = torch.tensor(43.0)
for epoch in range(8):
    for batch in ds["train"].loader(batch_size=64):
        opt.zero_grad()
        F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(net(batch), batch.y, pos_weight=pw).backward()
        opt.step()

with torch.no_grad():
    ev = {
        s: [(net(b), b.y > 0) for b in ds[s].loader(batch_size=256, shuffle=False)] for s in ("val", "test")
    }
lo = {s: torch.cat([x for x, _ in ev[s]]) for s in ev}
yy = {s: torch.cat([y for _, y in ev[s]]) for s in ev}
tau = pick_tau(lo["val"], yy["val"])
report(lo["test"] > tau, yy["test"])
# DR 0.455  FA 0.0009  F1 0.609          (~2.5 min CPU; val F1 is flat from epoch 1, saturated)

The graph model saturates below the per-bus MLP, and the papers report the same with both models reading the identical 14-dim input. Message passing smooths the localized per-bus signal that swing carries. Beating the lightweight baseline with graph or physics information is a research target, not a given.

docs.title: 3. Temporal model: a plain LSTM on the timeline
docs.text:
• The example builds its features in place from the raw measurements: train-normalized channels plus a per-window z-score.
  • Inside a sustained attack episode the rolling window is already contaminated, so the anomaly fades after onset. The file's swing avoids this: it compares each observed frame with the previous one (generation.write.TimelineWriter.write_temporal_layers).
  • Needs pip install "fdia-graph[torch]".
import torch, torch.nn as nn, torch.nn.functional as F
import fdia_graph as fg


def seqs(split):  # one sequence per bus from the file's chronological split, as tensors
    X, y = fg.load("ieee118", split=split, order="time").windows(W=16, stride=8, label="last", per_bus=True)
    return torch.as_tensor(X), torch.as_tensor(y, dtype=torch.float32)


(Xtr, ytr), (Xva, yva), (Xte, yte) = seqs("train"), seqs("val"), seqs("test")
mu = Xtr.mean((0, 1))
sd = Xtr.std((0, 1)) + 1e-9


def feats(X):  # measurements (train-normalized) + per-window z-score (the temporal spike feature)
    return torch.cat([(X - mu) / sd, (X - X.mean(1, keepdim=True)) / (X.std(1, keepdim=True) + 1e-6)], -1)


Xtr, Xva, Xte = feats(Xtr), feats(Xva), feats(Xte)


class LSTMDet(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c=8, h=32):
        super().__init__()
        self.lstm = nn.LSTM(c, h, batch_first=True)
        self.fc = nn.Linear(h, 1)

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.fc(self.lstm(x)[0][:, -1]).squeeze(-1)


m = LSTMDet()
opt = torch.optim.Adam(m.parameters(), 1e-3)
pw = (1 - ytr.mean()) / ytr.mean()
for epoch in range(10):
    for i in range(0, len(Xtr), 256):
        opt.zero_grad()
        F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(m(Xtr[i : i + 256]), ytr[i : i + 256], pos_weight=pw).backward()
        opt.step()

with torch.no_grad():
    lova = torch.cat([m(Xva[i : i + 4096]) for i in range(0, len(Xva), 4096)])
    lote = torch.cat([m(Xte[i : i + 4096]) for i in range(0, len(Xte), 4096)])
tau = pick_tau(lova, yva > 0)
report(lote > tau, yte > 0)
# DR 0.372  FA 0.0055  F1 0.463          (~3.5 min CPU; val F1 0.39 -> 0.47 from 5 to 10 epochs, headroom left)

These are minutes-of-CPU baselines with deliberate headroom, not the dataset's ceiling. layer="benign"/"clean" on windows swaps the model input layer (the label stays the attack target).

docs.title: Dataset statistics
docs.text:
Bad-data statistic relative to the alarm threshold, per family, on data release v0.8.3. Green families are indistinguishable from benign; red ones trip the alarm. Meter error follows an accuracy-class model (per-meter bias plus per-scan jitter). Report per-family node-F1 next to the false-alarm rate, never accuracy.

The tables in this section describe data release v0.8.3 (the results store's data.release_stats). Its Aq and Al episodes are one frame each, so a timeline holds more episodes than v0.8.0 and v0.8.1, whose Aq and Al were held over several frames; the pools, the other knobs and the seed are unchanged.

Per-system size. One timeline of 72,000 frames per system, about half under attack, split chronologically 60/20/20 by frame with no episode cut (so the split sizes differ slightly per system):

system N buses E branches frames train val test episodes ieee14 14 20 72,000 43,200 14,400 14,400 24,790 ieee30 30 41 72,000 43,200 14,400 14,400 24,790 ieee57 57 80 72,000 43,200 14,400 14,400 24,679 ieee89 89 210 72,000 43,220 14,380 14,400 24,495 ieee118 118 186 72,000 43,200 14,408 14,392 24,469 ieee145 145 453 72,000 43,200 14,400 14,400 24,485 ieee200 200 245 72,000 43,200 14,400 14,400 24,436 ieee300 300 411 72,000 43,200 14,400 14,400 24,672

Every system converges at every frame. In these releases a split boundary moved to the end of the episode it would cut; from the split-first generation the splits are cut before any episode is placed, so they are exactly 60/20/20.

Attacks per split (ieee118 shown; every system uses the same recipe). Families are drawn with weights inversely proportional to their episode length, so each gets about the same share of attacked frames. Each episode is placed at a uniform random onset where it fits, so a partition can hold a few more of one family. The one-frame families (Aq, Al, Ad, As, Ar) are thousands of episodes and land near their share; At and Am are about 100 sixty-frame episodes each, so one episode more or less moves 60 frames and their split counts vary most:

docs.title: Formulas: from the equation in the source to the function in the code
docs.text:
Every operation in the package that appears in a paper or a textbook gets one named function, even when it is called once, so a reader can go from an equation to the code and back. This catalogue is the index: one row per formula, the function that implements it, the equation in plain text, the source with a key from REFERENCES.md, and where it is used.

A formula is a pure function in a formulas/ package, cited here once, and the rest of the code calls it rather than repeating the expression. A new formula function gets its row here in the same change.

Each toolkit has its formulas/. The generation toolkit's (fdia_graph.formulas) holds what the generator and the loader compute: the network model (formulas.network), the meter noise (formulas.noise), the attack shapes (formulas.attacks), the temporal features (formulas.temporal) and the row reduction of the attack search (fdia_graph.formulas.trust). The analysis toolkit's (fdia_analysis.formulas) holds the rest: estimation (formulas.estimation, formulas.linalg, and the estimator's measurement function in formulas.measurement), the Jacobian projections (formulas.projection), the metrics (formulas.metrics), the federated statistics (formulas.federated) and trusted-meter selection (fdia_analysis.formulas.trust). A row below names a function by its module, which is in one toolkit only; the two trust modules are named with their toolkit.

docs.title: How a formula function is written
docs.text:
def swing_zscore(nx: np.ndarray, prev: np.ndarray, scale_t: np.ndarray, metered: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """The one-step injection change as a z-score of the bus's typical recent change [FED26], [N, 2]
    float32, dimensionless: swing[b] = ([P_inj, Q_inj](t) - [P_inj, Q_inj](t-1)) / scale_t[b].
    The difference is divided before it is rounded to float32, as the writer does (`generation.write`)."""
    sw = np.zeros((nx.shape[0], 2), np.float32)
    sw[metered, 0] = (nx[metered, 1] - prev[metered, 1]) / scale_t[metered, 0]
    sw[metered, 1] = (nx[metered, 2] - prev[metered, 2]) / scale_t[metered, 1]
    return sw

The rules: the name is the operation, not the caller; the first line of the docstring names the quantity and cites the key with its equation number; the equation follows in plain text, with the shape and unit of the result; the docstring is one to three lines (a few more when the equation needs them) and says of an argument only what its name and type do not; the function is pure (numpy in, numpy out, no I/O, no dataset objects); one test checks it on a case small enough to verify by hand.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: One definition per term and where it lives in the code: under src/fdia_graph, or under analysis/src/fdia_analysis for se, localization, trust and federated. The generation pipeline behind the data terms is in ../guides/generation.md, the meters in ../concepts/meters.md, the attacks in ../concepts/attacks.md and the layers in ../concepts/layers.md; citation keys are in REFERENCES.md.

docs.title: Data
docs.text: term definition in code scan One emission of every meter in the plan from one grid state: readings and masks. models.frames.Scan, engine.measurement.Emitter.emit_from_state frame One row of a timeline: the scan at one pool timestep with the attack of its episode applied, or none. models.frames.Frame, generation.write.TimelineWriter.store record One row as the loader serves it, ds[i]: a frame of a timeline. dataset/records.py, models.data.RecordBundle timestep The index of the pool state a frame was emitted from; on a timeline frame t is timestep t. data/timestep, schema.TIMESTEP episode A run of consecutive frames under one attack of one family on one design; episodes never overlap. models.plan.Episode, episodes/ group, data/seq_id onset The first frame of an episode, drawn uniformly among the positions of its split where the episode fits. generation.plan.uniform_onset, episodes/onset pool The operating-point pool: one converged AC state per frame, in time order. An IEEE pool is an array [T, N, 4] in |V|, P_inj, Q_inj, theta order, one state per minute of the load profile. The New York pool is a Pool record, one state per five-minute frame; a frame that did not solve is kept empty. data.ieee_pool.generate_states, generation._load_states, pool_ieee{C}.h5; data.pool.Pool, data.pool.PoolBuilder timeline One HDF5 file per system: every pool timestep scanned in time order, with attack episodes placed on it; the file format of every data release from v0.8.0. timeline.generate_timeline, schema.KIND_TIMELINE release A tagged set of data assets (data-v<x.y.z> from v0.8.0), pinned by sha256; registry._RELEASE is the default. registry.py, tools/upload_assets.py split The train, val and test partition (0, 1, 2), cut before any episode is placed, so every episode lies inside one split: three blocks in time order by default, or whole weeks (the setting split_by). generation.plan.split_bounds, generation.plan.split_weeks, generation.source.TimelineSource.cut_splits, data/split, models.choices.Split, schema.SPLIT_CODE family The attack type of a frame: 0 benign, 1 Aq, 2 Ad, 3 As, 4 Ar, 5 At, 6 Al, 7 Am. constants.families.FAMILIES, constants.families.FAMILY_CODE, data/family stealthy 1 for the families built as local false states (Aq, At, Al, Am), which pass the residual test. constants.families.STEALTHY_FAMILIES, data/stealthy area The buses an attacker may act in: by default the buses within hops branches of the goal's buses, the slack left out, grown over the zero-injection buses of its boundary, with hops reduced until a boundary is left. A support is chosen inside it. engine.attacks.area.AttackArea.hop_area, attack_area support The buses whose voltages a local false state moves; only meters that depend on them can change. The fewest-tamper search chooses it; without the search it is the whole area. engine.attacks.minimize.Minimizer.min_tamper boundary The buses one branch outside a support (or an area). Their voltages stay true; their reported injections take up the change. engine.attacks.area.AttackArea.boundary reach A support with its boundary: every bus whose reported injection a false state on that support can change. engine.attacks.false_state.FalseState.reach snapshot One state of an attack window, counted from the window's first frame. engine.attacks.window.AttackWindow device One SCADA terminal (a bus's injection meters, the flows metered at that bus, a voltage meter without PMU) or one PMU (a bus's voltage magnitude and angle, and under the hybrid meter model the branch currents it reads at the bus), the unit [WU26] counts. formulas.attacks.tampered_devices meter model What the meters read: "hybrid", new generation's, where a SCADA voltmeter reads |V| only and each PMU reads |V|, the angle and the current phasor of every in-service branch at its bus; or "v083", the released files', with an angle at every voltmeter bus and no currents. models.choices.MeterModel, models.config.MeterSettings, generate_timeline(..., redundancy={"meter_model": ...}) PMU branch current The current phasor a PMU reads at its end of a branch, I_f = Y_f V or I_t = Y_t V, stored as real and imaginary part per end in pmu_i [WU26, eqs. 19-20]; noise at IEEE C37.118.1's 1% total vector error [C37118]. formulas.network.branch_currents, formulas.noise.current_sigma, the generator's masks.current overload attack Am in new generation: the apparent flow of two lines at once by default (OverloadSettings.n_lines; FlowGoal.more), as the tampered measurements carry it before noise, driven snapshot by snapshot to the line's rating over the window, on the support that tampers the fewest devices, its attackable loads and generators free inside the limits [WU26, eqs. 12-25]. engine.attacks.overload.Overload free injection A bus whose injection a flow-goal attacker may change: an attackable load or a generator (the latter inside its limits, [WU26, eqs. 22-23]); a zero-injection bus is held at zero. engine.attacks.false_state.FalseState.free_injection_buses load cap The overload attack's load-plausibility bound: every load bus the attack moves, in its support or on the support's boundary (a bus with a base load, no generator, not the slack), shows an active change of at most load_cap times its true load [YUA11]; 0.5 by default. models.config.OverloadSettings.load_cap, generate_timeline(..., am_attack={"load_cap": ...}), engine.attacks.false_state.FalseState.solve_flow_local line rating A branch's thermal limit S_max in MVA: by default rating_margin (1.25) times its peak true apparent flow over the operating pool, or on request the PGLib-OPF rate_a matched by end buses (generate_timeline(..., am_attack={"rating_source": "pglib"}), the margin as am_attack={"rating_margin": ...}, both through models.config.OverloadSettings); the IEEE cases pandapower ships carry only a 9,900 MVA placeholder. engine.attacks.overload.Overload.use_line_ratings, models.config.OverloadSettings, fdia_graph.ratings, formulas.attacks.branch_ratings stealth scale A multiplier on At's stealth bound, whose unit is the meters' rated accuracy; 1 by default. Am has no stealth bound, as in [WU26]. generate_timeline(stealth_scale=...) paper noise [WU26]'s case-study noise, 0.03 pu on SCADA and 0.01 pu on PMU channels, in the stored units; the threshold of Am's tamper count. constants.meters.WU26_NOISE, formulas.noise.paper_sigma tamper cost The devices with a channel moved beyond the family's threshold at some snapshot of an attack window, the objective of [WU26, eq. 12]. The threshold is the accuracy-class sigma for At and the paper noise for Am. formulas.attacks.tampered_channels, tampered_devices accuracy-class sigma A meter's rated accuracy at a reading (relative for power channels plus a floor, absolute for voltage and angle): the sigma the measured calibration uses and the threshold of the fewest-tamper search for At. NoiseModel.sigmas, formulas.noise.accuracy_class_sigma jitter sigma The per-scan random part of a meter's error, a quarter of its accuracy class; the emitter draws each reading's noise with it. Emission only. NoiseModel.sample local false state A state in which only the support is re-solved under false loads, boundary voltages held true, and the attack vector h(x_false) - h(x_true) is added to the true scan; it meets constraints (13)-(18) and (21)-(23) of [WU26], and in new generation the branch-current phasors (19)-(20); new generation also holds it on the fewest-device support of eq. (12). engine.attacks.ramp_frames.RampFrames._stealthy_frame, engine.attacks.false_state.FalseState.solve_local, engine.attacks.area.AttackArea.hop_area theta_ref The one slack angle every estimate is referenced to, fixed at fit time from the training split. se.base.SEBase._fit_reference, ref_angles active buses The buses attacked somewhere in the records being scored; macro scores average over them. models.scores.OverallMetrics, formulas.metrics.tau_from_counts attackable buses Buses whose load an attack may target: nonzero active load, not the slack, at most max_load_mw; the stealthy families also skip generator buses [BOY22]. A learned localizer's _attackable is the buses labelled attacked in its training split. engine.core.FdiaGenerator._load_tables (attackable_pos, stealthy_pos), localization.learned.LearnedLocalizer

docs.title: Estimation
docs.text: term definition in code WLS Weighted least squares state estimation, each meter weighted by the inverse square of its calibrated error [SCH70]. se.methods.WLS, formulas.estimation.wls_step chord-Newton The Gauss-Newton iteration with the Jacobian fixed at the benign mean state instead of recomputed per iteration. se.base.SEBase, formulas.estimation Huber Iterative reweighting that scales a meter's weight by min(1, c / abs(r_n)), r_n its normalized residual [HUB64]. se.methods.AdaptiveWeighting, formulas.estimation.huber_weights BDD / residual test Bad-data detection: an alarm when the largest normalized residual of a WLS solve exceeds a level calibrated on benign training records. trust.base.TrustSelector._alarm_level, _max_residual LNR (largest normalized residual) The residual divided by its standard deviation, largest per record or per bus; removed one meter at a time in ResidualRemoval [HAN75]. formulas.estimation.normalized_residual, se.methods.ResidualRemoval, localization.methods.ResidualLocalizer prior (SubspacePrior) The estimate restricted to mean + VK c, a low-rank basis of whitened benign training states, optionally composed with Huber [EST26]. se.methods.SubspacePrior, formulas.estimation.whitened_svd_basis gate / oracle gate A fitted localizer's flagged buses down-weight their meters before the solve; the oracle gate uses the true labels y and gives the ceiling. se.methods.GatedPrior, formulas.estimation.gate_weights PMU pseudo-measurement The voltage phasor at the far end of a PMU-metered branch computed from the PMU's voltage and current, V_far = (I_near - y_nn V_near) / y_nf [WU26, eq. (3)], averaged over the branches reaching the bus; the estimator option pmu_pseudo places it in the |V| and angle slots no meter reads. formulas.estimation.pmu_pseudo_voltages, se.base.SEBase(solve=SolveConfig(pmu_pseudo=True)) geo The geometric mean of the per-class errors over the record classes present (benign and each family). se.base.SEBase.score, models.scores.EstimatorScores.geo

OverallMetrics.macro_dr, FamilyMetrics.detection_rate, PerBusMetrics.dr FR False-alarm rate: the mean per-bus alarm rate on benign records, or over every record with fr_over="all". docs.text: What every folder of the repository holds, then what every Python file does, in one line: the first paragraph of its docstring. Generated by tools/layout.py; edit the docstring (or REPO and DOCS in the tool), not this page. A toolkit's section names each file by its module under the toolkit's package: dataset.base is src/fdia_graph/dataset/base.py, se.base is analysis/src/fdia_analysis/se/base.py.
