docs.text: folder what it holds src/ the generation toolkit, the package fdia_graph (the distribution fdia-graph): generating a timeline and loading it analysis/ the analysis toolkit, the package fdia_analysis (the distribution fdia-analysis, which depends on fdia-graph): state estimation, localization, federated training, trust selection and the results store's code, with its own pyproject.toml, src/ and tests/ tests/ the generation toolkit's test suite, and the helpers both suites share (their shared fixtures are in the root conftest.py) examples/ scripts a user copies: the quickstart, the training examples, the New York extension points results/ the results store: data only (one CSV per experiment and runs.csv), with the queries the docs read it through pipelines/ the builds of released data: the New York pool and timeline, and the MATLAB reference they are checked against tools/ repository tooling only: the gates, the generated docs, pull requests and releases docs/ the documentation, one folder per kind of page docs/getting-started/ tutorials: load a dataset, generate one, analyse one, each start to finish docs/guides/ how to do one task docs/concepts/ explanations: how a part is built and why docs/analysis/ one page per study with its figures: what was measured, on what, and the result docs/reference/ facts to look up: the file map, the data dictionary, the glossary, the formulas, the references docs/figures/ the images pages share, each with its data or its diagram source docs/stylesheets/ the docs site's stylesheet: the display width of the phone diagrams .github/ the CI workflows and the dependency updates

docs.title: The generation toolkit, fdia_graph
docs.text: file what it does fdia_graph fdia-graph: load and generate datasets for locating false data injection attacks on a power grid. constants The toolkit's constants, one module per subject: facts only, each with its unit and its source. constants.channels The column of each quantity on the last axis of a measurement array: node_x[..., NodeChannel.P_INJ]. constants.families The attack families: the code a file's data/family column carries for each, and the named subsets. constants.files The names and layouts of the files around a timeline: the unfinished file, the index of local datasets, and an operator's load export. A timeline file's own names are in schema.py. constants.grid The power systems: the IEEE cases the toolkit builds, the bus types and the "no limit" ratings. constants.meters The meters: their kinds, their accuracy classes and noise floors, and where each kind's reading sits in a timeline file. constants.newyork The New York grid: NYISO's zones and neighbors, the fields of the case file, the pinned inputs and their addresses, NYgrid's dispatch numbers, the fitted load model and the operating rules. constants.numerics The fixed numerical tolerances and finite-difference steps of the algorithms. constants.records The fields of a record, by group: the names a record, a batch and an export carry, in their order. constants.releases The data releases: where the built-in datasets are published, which release is pinned, and the sha256 of every asset of the releases the registry verifies. constants.streams The keys of the random streams a timeline draws from. Each stream is seeded with the timeline's seed, a key below and a position, so a draw of one kind never shifts a draw of another. The keys are arbitrary and fixed: a different key gives a different file. constants.time Time: the calendar, the New York frame, and how a load profile is correlated from scan to scan. data Where the load data and the operating points come from, for every test system. data.config Build settings and the one place random generators are made. data.dispatch Hourly unit dispatch, NYgrid's allocation of the NYISO fuel mix to the fixed unit list. data.ieee_pool The pool of an IEEE case: one AC operating state per step of a load profile. data.inputs Historical inputs: NYgrid's hourly 2019 tables and NYISO's 5-minute zonal load, and fetch_inputs, which downloads everything the build reads at its pinned version. data.ipopt The optimization solver every OPF of the New York grid runs on, found and checked in one place. data.ipopt_solver The package's own OPF engine: one polar AC-OPF model of a Case in Pyomo, solved by Ipopt. data.load_sources Where the bottom-up load profiles come from ([LI21]), each downloaded once into a cache: the NREL ResStock and ComStock county profiles, each utility's EIA-861 sector sales, the census county centroids and the IAC industrial plants, with the clock rules the plants run on. LoadModel (loads.py) builds the bus profiles from these. data.loads Per-bus load profiles by the bottom-up method of [LI21], scaled to the real zone load. data.pandapower_solver pandapower as a solve engine of a Case: its Newton AC power flow and its interior-point AC OPF. data.pool The pool: one AC operating state per 5-minute frame, from a ramp-constrained real-time dispatch, and the pool file of the build, HDF5. A timeline is written by the writer every grid uses (fdia_graph.generation.write) and read through fdia_graph.dataset. data.profiles Load profiles: a real load time series as a load-scaling vector, read from a file or fetched from an operator's feed. data.solver The AC solves of a Case, behind one interface with two engines. dataset FdiaGraph: a PyTorch-ready dataset over one HDF5 file, a timeline (one row per frame in time order, kind="timeline"). dataset.base The loader's shared state and the constants its concerns read. dataset.clients The timeline as federated clients: each utility sees only its own meters, buses and labels. dataset.export A whole split at once: summary, and the arrays/tensors/frames of every kept record. dataset.graph The static graph of a shard: connectivity and the per-branch and per-bus physics, as tensors. dataset.physics The admittance matrices built from the static graph, and the clean power flow on every branch derived from the clean state through them. dataset.records One record at a time: unit conversion, __getitem__ in dict/PyG form, collate, and a ready DataLoader. dataset.sequence The timeline as sequences: sliding windows over a time-ordered view, and the episode table. download Fetch the built-in datasets from the GitHub Release and cache them under ~/.cache/fdia_graph. engine The generation engine — the math/physics/theory half of the SDK, behind fg.generate(). engine.attacks Every attack the generator builds, one line per file. engine.attacks.area Given seed buses, the attacker's area and the boundary of any set of buses. engine.attacks.blas One BLAS thread for the length of a search (one_blas_thread). engine.attacks.episodes The design of one episode (EpisodeDesigns): At's drawn at its onset, Am's from its window. engine.attacks.false_state Given a true state, a support and a goal, the false state: the support's voltages re-solved with every other voltage true, inside the limits. engine.attacks.family What the timeline asks of any family, and the base of a family of your own. engine.attacks.frames Given a true and a false state, the attack vector a = h(x_false) - h(x_true) and the frame that adds it to the true scan. engine.attacks.minimize The search: the area first, then supports grown from the goal's buses, smallest first, the cheapest of at most min_budget [WU26 eq. 12]. engine.attacks.overload Am's inputs and frames: ratings, eligible lines, the flow schedule of [WU26 eqs. 24-25], one frame. engine.attacks.ramp_frames One At frame: the false state of the frame's AttackDesign, written as a frame. engine.attacks.rref The other way to choose a support: [WU26]'s row reduction of the transposed area Jacobian. engine.attacks.search At and Am as families: how EpisodeDesigns, RampFrames and Overload are called frame by frame. engine.attacks.window What one candidate support costs over a window (AttackWindow.cost). engine.base A part of the generator: one job (emitting scans, choosing an area, solving a false state, ...) as one class that holds the generator it belongs to. engine.core The generator: the grid, the meter plan, the load table, the case limits, and one object per part. engine.measurement The readings of a stored state: exact, then with bias and jitter, laid out per bus and per branch. engine.physics How a stored load-positive injection divides into load and generation. errors Every error the package raises on purpose, defined in this one module. formulas The mathematics of the generation toolkit as named, pure functions: numpy in, numpy out, no files, no dataset objects, no torch. Each function carries its equation and a source key from docs/reference/REFERENCES.md; docs/reference/FORMULAS.md is the catalogue. Import a formula from its module (formulas.network, formulas.noise, formulas.attacks, formulas.temporal, formulas.trust). The formulas of estimation, localization, federated training and trust selection are the analysis toolkit's (fdia_analysis.formulas). formulas.attacks Attack shapes defined by the dataset [DAT26] that are pure functions of their parameters. formulas.network The AC network model: branch admittances, bus injections and branch flows [AE04, ch. 2], [MP19]. formulas.noise The meter error model: the standard deviation an accuracy class gives a reading [ASP14], and the noise [WU26]'s case studies state. sensing.noise.NoiseModel splits a class into a constant per-meter bias and a per-scan jitter (ours) and draws both. formulas.temporal The temporal features of a scan [FED26]: the one-step injection change and its z-score against the bus's typical recent change, and the recent-change scale itself. formulas.trust Row reduction for stealthy attacks under trusted meters [WU26]: the reduced row echelon form of a matrix, and the sparsest rows of a row space, which the attack generator searches for an attack vector the trusted meters leave open. generation generate(system, name, **knobs) — build a custom dataset and register it as name. generation.design The design stage of a timeline: every placed episode of a split gets its design before the split is walked, from its family (engine.attacks.family.EpisodeFamily.designed). generation.emit The emit stage of a timeline: every frame in time order, benign or under its episode's design. generation.ieee An IEEE case by its name as the source of a timeline: the original generator (generation.search.SearchSource) on the case's network and its pool of operating points. generation.plan The plan stage of a timeline: where its splits are cut and where each split's episodes go. generation.search A test system as the source of a timeline, the original generator: coverage meters and the search-based designs, on any grid. generation.source The one source of a timeline: a grid, its pool of operating points, and the path that generates it. generation.write The one writer of a timeline file, for every grid: TimelineWriter owns the open HDF5 file. models Every data model of the generation toolkit, one module per subject; import a model from its module. models.assets How files are found: where a dataset comes from and where its bytes are fetched from. models.base Bundle: a typed record that is also a dict. models.choices Every argument that takes one value from a fixed set, in one place. models.config The settings every consumer accepts, one model each, checked when built (models.validation). models.data What a user gets back: one record, a batch, a whole split, a summary and the episode table. Each is a Bundle, so it is also a dict. models.fields The fields the record bundles share, each one's meaning written once. models.frames The records the attack code passes around: a scan, a frame, an attack vector, a goal, a design, the operating limits, a search result. models.grid The static description of a system (the per-branch pi model and the admittance matrices built from it, which never change from one scan to the next) and one solved operating point of it. models.inputs What the formulas and the parsers accept, one model each, checked when built (models.validation). models.plan The records of a timeline's plan and design stages: a placed episode (Slot), a split and its frames (SplitSpan), a placed episode on its way through the design stage (Planned), the attack as it is written (Episode, EpisodeRecord), what the placement asked for and got (Placement), and what a design worker rebuilds its generator from (GeneratorSpec). models.validation The one place inputs are checked (CONTRIBUTING.md, "an input is checked in one place"). ratings Branch thermal ratings for the overload attack of [WU26] (eqs. 24-25), stored with the package. registry The dataset registry: the built-in (downloadable) datasets and the locally generated ones. schema The file protocol: every group, dataset and attribute name an fdia-graph HDF5 file carries, defined once. The writer (generation) and the readers (dataset) agree through these names; tools/readability.py refuses a path-shaped literal ("data/...", "graph/...") in any other module. Field names (node_x, clean, ...) stay as words in the code; FIELD_PATH maps them to paths. sensing The meters: what each client measures, and how wrong each meter is. sensing.measure The measurement function: the meter readings a grid state gives, and their derivatives. sensing.meters The meter plan: every meter of a grid as one row of a table, with its owner and accuracy class. sensing.noise Meter noise: the accuracy class of each meter split into a constant bias and a per-scan jitter. systems The test systems: a grid as a Case with its Network, whichever grid it is. systems.case The grid as one frozen record of arrays, read from a MATPOWER case file or from a pandapower net. systems.fixes Two variants of a case, applied when one is asked for: the external areas held at the base load, and NYgrid's HVDC links in place of the AC branch 81-125. The changes every build has (zone J's split, the 765 kV line) are in the case file itself (case.py reads it). systems.network Admittances of a Case, built once, and the AC quantities they give for any state, from the SDK's network formulas (formulas.network). systems.ownership Federated clients: each NY bus belongs to the electric utility whose service territory holds it. systems.pandapower_types The pandapower objects the package reads, as types. systems.states The pool of operating points a timeline walks, one frame per point: an array [T, N, 4] in memory, or PoolStates, which keeps a year of solved voltages as they are and gives a frame's state when it is asked for. systems.tables The CSV tables of the inputs, read whole and closed: the NYgrid checkout's bus, unit and renewable tables and the bus locations. One reader, so no input file is left open. timeline One continuous attacked timeline per system, written as one HDF5 file.

docs.title: The analysis toolkit, fdia_analysis
docs.text: file what it does fdia_analysis fdia-analysis: what is measured on an fdia-graph timeline: state estimation, attack localization, federated training, trusted-meter selection, and the store the measured results are kept in. federated Federated training over K clients (utilities) that never pool their records [FED26]. federated.aggregate Averaging torch state dicts across clients with formulas.federated.fedavg [MCM17]. federated.localizer Federated per-bus localizers: the paper's BusMLP and BusCNN trained by FedAvg over K clients [MCM17], [FED26], with records never leaving a client. federated.partition The split of a system's buses into K clients (utilities) for federated training [FED26]. federated.se Federated fitting of the state estimator's learned part [EST26], [FED26]. formulas The mathematics of the analysis toolkit as named, pure functions: numpy in, numpy out, no files, no dataset objects, no torch. Each function carries its equation and a source key from docs/reference/REFERENCES.md; docs/reference/FORMULAS.md is the catalogue. The network model, the meter noise and the attack shapes are the generation toolkit's (fdia_graph.formulas). Import a formula from its module (formulas.estimation, formulas.federated, formulas.linalg, formulas.measurement, formulas.metrics, formulas.projection, formulas.trust). formulas.estimation Weighted least squares state estimation and its robust variants, one function per equation [SCH70], [HAN75], [HUB64], [EST26]. formulas.federated Statistics that combine across federated clients without moving their records [FED26]. formulas.linalg Numerical linear algebra the estimators lean on: a guarded inverse of a normal matrix, its condition number without an eigen-decomposition, and per-record normal matrices in sub-batches. formulas.measurement The estimator's AC measurement function h(x) and its closed-form Jacobian [AE04, ch. 2], [MP19], assembled from the network model the generator and the loader use (fdia_graph.formulas.network: bus_injections, branch_flows). The estimator's torch twin (se.base.SEBase._h_t) is kept for callers that differentiate through it; analysis/tests/test_formulas.py pins it to the functions here. formulas.metrics Per-bus localization metrics from confusion counts, so they can be summed across clients or thresholds before any ratio is taken [KEC25]. formulas.projection Projections through the measurement Jacobian: the explained and unexplained parts of a measurement change, leverage, the weak directions, and the meter-to-bus aggregation of the Jacobian-informed features [JAC26], [HAN75]. formulas.trust Trusted-meter selection against stealthy attacks [WU26]: the attack subspace a secured set leaves open, the cost of the cheapest attack in it, and the greedy selection that closes it. localization Per-bus FDIA localization on fdia-graph datasets, sklearn style. localization.base Per-bus FDIA localization on fdia-graph datasets — the shared machinery behind every method class. localization.learned Learned per-bus localizers: the graph-free encoders that gave the best localization numbers in the federated localization paper, on that paper's 14-dim per-bus feature vector. localization.methods The localizer method classes. Each changes exactly one thing about LocalizerBase — the per-bus score — so a difference between two arms is a difference between detection signals, not between calibration or metrics code. models Every data model of the analysis toolkit in one place: the ones only the estimators, the localizers, the federated trainers, the trust selectors and the results store use. A model the generation toolkit also uses is in fdia_graph.models, and is imported from there. models.choices The fixed sets the analysis settings choose from, beside fdia_graph.models.choices (its Choice is their base): a member is its string value, and a settings model declares a field's set as Annotated[str, OneOf(Features)]. models.config The settings the estimators, the localizers, the trust selectors and the federated trainers accept, one model each, checked when built by the validation engine of fdia_graph.models.validation. models.data What the analysis packages hand back that is neither a score table nor a setting: the truth an estimator is scored against. models.federated What the federated layer passes around: how the buses split into clients. models.grid The pseudo-measurement records of the estimator's PMU current channels [WU26 eq. 3]: where a pseudo voltage phasor can be placed, and the phasors with their propagated noise. models.inputs What the analysis formulas accept, one model each, checked when built by the validation engine of fdia_graph.models.validation. models.results The models of a results table: the metric registry, a Record (one measured value with the keys that say what it is) and a Provenance (which run made it), plus the parsers that read loose input (a nested score report, a filter value, a run's settings) by its type. Every check lives here, per the validation rule, so a store never holds an unknown metric, a non-finite value or a malformed key; fdia_analysis.results builds these models and never checks its input itself. models.scores The result tables: an estimator's error pair per record class, a localizer's metric rows per class, and the Jacobian feature outputs. Each is a Bundle, indexable by family name as before. models.training What the learned localizers pass between their fitting pieces (a centralized fit and a federated client share them). results Measured results as data: typed records with their provenance, one tidy store, and the renderers that put the numbers into docs and figures, so no measured number is typed by hand. results.docs Measured numbers in markdown come from the store, never from a keyboard. results.render Turning records into what a reader sees: a formatted cell, a markdown table, a pivot of records by two keys, and the CSV sidecar a figure is drawn from. Nothing here measures or stores anything. results.run How a harness records what it measured: open a Run, add values, and the run writes them to the store with its provenance when it closes. results.store The results store: one tidy CSV per experiment plus one table of runs, in a folder kept in git. se State estimation on fdia-graph datasets, sklearn style. se.base State estimation on fdia-graph datasets — the shared machinery behind every method class. se.detect Detection: when a detector alarms, as a building block. se.detect.rules When a detector alarms: the rule that turns a statistic per scan into a first alarm. se.jacobian Jacobian-informed features (Abdulin & Narimani): the measurement Jacobian as a physics transform of the scan-to-scan measurement change, not as raw model input. se.methods The estimator method classes. Each changes exactly one thing about SEBase, so a difference between two arms is a difference between estimators rather than between implementations. trust Which meters to trust so that stealthy attacks stop being stealthy [WU26], sklearn style. trust.base The shared machinery of the trusted-meter selectors: the measurement Jacobian at the benign mean (from a WLS estimator of fdia_analysis.se), the attack-cost kernel, and the scoring that pins the secured meters and asks the residual test whether the attack shows. trust.meter_dqn The trusted-meter selection as a Markov decision process solved by a deep Q-network (the learned selection of [WU26]). trust.secured A copy of a timeline with a set of meters secured: the attacker locked out of them, so on every frame their observed reading is the benign one, and the stored temporal features recomputed from the pinned observed frames (generation.write.TimelineWriter.write_temporal_layers). The estimators and the localizers then read the copy like any timeline, which is how a trusted-meter selection is measured on state estimation and localization rather than on the residual test alone (TrustSelector.score). The copy is rewritten in blocks of frames, so a 72,000-frame timeline of any ladder system fits in bounded memory.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text: file what it does tools/bench.py Time the estimators and the generator on the tiny timeline, and store the timings as a run of the bench experiment in the results store (results/bench.csv), where docs/reference/BENCHMARKS.md renders them from (a results block). tools/class_diagrams.py Write the class and module diagrams of the two toolkits (fdia_graph and fdia_analysis) from their source, as Mermaid sources under docs/figures/diagrams/, so the pictures in docs/reference/CLASS_MAP.md never drift from the code. tools/count_lines.py Count the lines of the two toolkits: all lines, code lines (no docstring, comment or blank line), and the code inside and outside the homes of constants (constants/ and schema.py). tools/layout.py The repository's layout rules, and the file map they keep current (docs/reference/MODULES.md). tools/models_doc.py Render the public data models into docs/reference/DATA_DICTIONARY.md. tools/pr.py Pull requests from the command line, without the gh CLI (CONTRIBUTING.md, "The pull request"). tools/prereview.py Every check a pull request must pass, for both toolkits of the repository (fdia_graph and fdia_analysis, sources.PACKAGES), run locally in one command before the review is requested (CONTRIBUTING.md, "The pull request"). tools/readability.py Readability measures for the two packages (fdia_graph and fdia_analysis, sources.PACKAGES), the limits below (LIMITS), and the file-protocol rule: a dataset path ("data/...", "graph/...", any group of schema.Group) or a group name used as one (f.create_group("data"), f["attack"], "episodes" in f) may be spelled only in src/fdia_graph/schema.py; every other module goes through schema. And the validation rule (CONTRIBUTING.md, "an input is checked in one place"): raise ValueError / raise TypeError and isinstance(...) only inside a models package (fdia_graph.models, fdia_analysis.models), where the one engine checks every input and the parser models read loose input by its type; everywhere else an input is checked or parsed by building its model, and a condition only the data reveals raises a named error from errors. And the typing rule: an annotation says Any only where ANY_ALLOWED lists it with the reason the value can be anything; every other annotation carries its real type. tools/release.py Cut a package release after the version-bump PR has merged (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Releasing"). tools/render_mermaid.py Render a Mermaid source file to a standalone SVG and a PNG next to it. Every diagram in the docs is such a rendered image, because the README is also the PyPI page and the docs are read in the GitHub mobile app, and neither renders a Mermaid block. tools/results_docs.py Fill and check the results blocks of the docs from the results store (results/). tools/site_index.py Stage the three root pages of the repository for the docs site: README.md becomes docs/index.md, CONTRIBUTING.md docs/contributing.md and CHANGELOG.md docs/changelog.md. The README is the single source for the landing page; its links carry a docs/ prefix that is wrong once the file lives inside docs_dir, so the prefix is stripped on copy, and links between the three root pages are rewritten to their staged names. Runs in the Vercel build (vercel.json) and in the versioned deploy (.github/workflows/docs.yml); the three staged files are generated output and stay untracked. tools/sources.py Where the repository's two toolkits live, said once for every tool: the generation toolkit fdia_graph and the analysis toolkit fdia_analysis, each a package under its own source root. tools/upload_assets.py Publish data-release assets to a GitHub release (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Releasing", data releases).

docs.title: The generation toolkit's tests
docs.text: file what it does tests/case_studies.py [WU26]'s case studies as test inputs: the lines each scenario overloads, its PMU buses and the attacker's area, in MATPOWER bus numbers, and their positions in a generator's grid. tests/digests.py Whole-file digests of a generated HDF5 file: the proof that a refactor did not move a number. tests/helpers.py The plain helpers the two test trees share (tests/ and analysis/tests/): where the checkout's parts are, the tiny timeline's recipe, the old releases' files, and the checks both toolkits hold their own package to. The fixtures are in the repository root's conftest.py. tests/nygrid/inputs.py The inputs of the nygrid tests in one place, and which tests each one lets run. tests/nygrid/test_any_case.py The New York grid is a test case of the original generator like any IEEE case: coverage meters and the search-based designs on the packaged case file and the checked-in days' pool (no solver, no NYgrid data), through SearchSource.for_pool. tests/test_any_case.py has the IEEE side. tests/nygrid/test_case_file.py Case.from_matpower on a three-bus case file written here: what it reads and what it refuses. Needs no input data. tests/nygrid/test_dataset.py A timeline read back as clients (dataset.clients): with the Ownership of the buses the source gives each meter to the client of its bus, and the file reads as one view per client and one for the operator. On the packaged New York case with made-up clients and the checked-in days' pool: no NYgrid data, no solver. tests/nygrid/test_examples.py The extension examples of docs/guides/extending.md run as published, so the guide never shows code that broke (no data needed). tests/nygrid/test_grid.py The New York grid's case file: what it holds, its exact round trip through the MATPOWER reader and writer, the recipe that made it from NYgrid, the two case variants and the utility of each bus. tests/nygrid/test_public.py The public surface of the New York code: every module of its packages imports, a package exports no name of its own, and reading a dataset stays light (no data needed). tests/nygrid/test_scenario.py The hourly operating points against NYgrid's own MATLAB output: the inputs, the dispatch, the AC projection and the pool, and the bottom-up load profiles with their within-hour calibration. tests/nygrid/test_sensing.py The meter plan on the New York case and its readings: each meter owned by the client of its bus, the measurement Jacobian against finite differences, observability and the meter noise. On the packaged case file with made-up clients: no NYgrid data. tests/nygrid/test_solve_engines.py The two OPF engines against each other: the package's (Pyomo and Ipopt) and pandapower's, on the same case, loads and costs. Also the choices the New York pool refuses. The comparisons read no NYgrid data and are skipped where Ipopt cannot start. tests/nygrid/test_solvers.py The checked Ipopt every OPF of the New York grid runs on: a solver that is missing, or found but unable to start, raises SolverUnavailable with the fix, instead of reading as an infeasible model downstream. tests/nygrid/test_tables.py The input tables are read whole and closed: no ResourceWarning, a byte-order mark dropped (no data needed). tests/test_any_case.py The per-case choices are settings of the one source: each works on any case whose data allows it, and is refused with the reason where the data is missing. The New York grid's side of these tests is in tests/nygrid/test_any_case.py. tests/test_attack_area.py The attacker's area [WU26] Sec. III-A and the window ratings of the overload attack: the paper's own area where it states one, the area its four principles pick otherwise (rules 1 and 2 as checks, 3 and 4 as a score of ours), the "delta" ratings matched to its Fig. 4 magnitudes, and the validity of every attack the search returns (the goal met, every untampered channel within its noise, trusted buses true). tests/test_edges.py The public edges: wrong arguments fail early with a message naming what is allowed, and the filters mean what the docs say. The other test files prove the happy path; this file is the rest. tests/test_formulas.py The generation toolkit's formulas: each function on a case small enough to check by hand. The analysis toolkit's formulas, and the estimator's torch measurement function pinned to the numpy kernel here, are checked in analysis/tests/test_formulas.py. tests/test_ieee_case.py An IEEE case as a Case: Case.from_pandapower against the pandapower net it reads, what it refuses, and the Network admittances against pandapower's makeYbus on the same net. tests/test_loader_timeline.py fg.load on a timeline file: the record table and the timeline from one file, order, the benign layer on records, batches and exports, ds.windows and ds.episodes. Uses the timeline fixture of conftest. tests/test_malformed_inputs.py A malformed setting or argument is a ConfigError, never a raw TypeError, KeyError, ValueError or IndexError from deeper in the code (docs/reference/REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md, item 4). tests/test_minimize.py The fewest-tamper support search [WU26 eq. 12]: exact against brute force on IEEE-14, a lower bound that never exceeds a cost, the two sigmas (the emitter's per-scan jitter, the meters' accuracy class the search counts against), and a continuous reweighted-l1 cross-check the search is never beaten by. tests/test_models.py Bundle, the dual-access base of the typed records: every dict use the package's callers rely on must keep working, and the attribute view must agree with it. tests/test_models_doc.py The models section of the data dictionary is generated from the dataclasses; this keeps it so. tests/test_models_package.py Every data model of a toolkit lives in its models package: they are defined nowhere else, each is imported from the module that defines it, and the package's own modules depend on nothing but numpy, the standard library, the named errors (fdia_graph.errors) and the constants (fdia_graph.constants, which imports nothing of the package). The checks are functions of the package (tests/helpers.py), so the analysis toolkit holds its own fdia_analysis.models to them (analysis/tests/test_models_package.py). tests/test_namespace.py The package namespace: the heavy helpers resolve lazily to the real functions, so their docstrings and signatures cannot drift from a wrapper's, and import fdia_graph stays light. tests/test_old_releases.py The pinned data releases stay readable. Checked in the source (no import, no module name in a lazy table) and by running: a fresh interpreter in which fdia_analysis is blocked (so the check is the same whether or not it is installed) loads every module of fdia_graph, generates a timeline and reads it back. tests/test_tools.py Four repository tools on small samples: the constants rule of tools/layout.py on a temporary tree, tools/count_lines.py on a file whose lines are easy to miscount, the phone rules of tools/render_mermaid.py on two flow diagrams, and the plain-pages rule of tools/prereview.py on a page. tests/test_trust_formulas.py The row reduction the attack search and the trusted-meter kernel share (the kernel itself, the open attack subspace, its cost and the greedy selection, is checked in analysis/tests/test_trust_formulas.py). tests/test_trusted_pmus.py [WU26]'s trusted-PMU schedule as a constraint on the fewest-tamper search: a PMU trusted at slot s keeps its bus's /V/ and angle true at every snapshot t >= s (eqs. 26-32), its branch currents stay untrusted (eq. 27), and one support is held for the window. tests/test_validation.py The validation engine (models.validation): rules declared on fields, one message shape, and the public entry points that build their config models before any work. tests/test_versions.py The two toolkits are released together at one version: both pyproject.toml files and both __version__ values say the same number, and fdia-analysis requires exactly that fdia-graph (a released fdia-graph of another version may lack a name fdia_analysis imports). No data needed; tools/release.py refuses to tag a commit where this does not hold.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
Keys cited by docstrings in the code and by FORMULAS.md, in the form [KEY, eq. n] or [KEY, ch. n]. Add a key here before citing it; keep the list alphabetical.

key reference [AE04] A. Abur and A. Gómez Expósito, Power System State Estimation: Theory and Implementation, Marcel Dekker, 2004. [ASP14] M. Asprou, E. Kyriakides and M. Albu, "The effect of variable weights in a WLS state estimator considering instrument transformer uncertainties," IEEE Trans. Instrum. Meas., vol. 63, no. 6, pp. 1484–1495, 2014, and the companion "The effect of instrument transformer accuracy class on the WLS state estimator accuracy," IEEE PES General Meeting, 2013. The accuracy-class meter error model (maximum error divided by √3). [BOY22] O. Boyaci, A. Umunnakwe, A. Sahu, M. R. Narimani, M. Ismail, K. R. Davis and E. Serpedin, "Graph neural networks based detection of stealth false data injection attacks in smart grids," IEEE Systems Journal, vol. 16, no. 2, pp. 2946–2957, 2022. Algorithm 1: every load and generator at a bus scaled by one factor per time step; the local attacker skips generator and zero-injection buses. [C37118] IEEE Standard for Synchrophasor Measurements for Power Systems, IEEE Std C37.118.1-2011, and its amendment C37.118.1a-2014. A total vector error of at most 1% in steady state, the PMU accuracy class of the branch-current channels. [CGL79] T. F. Chan, G. H. Golub and R. J. LeVeque, "Updating formulae and a pairwise algorithm for computing sample variances," Stanford University, Tech. Rep. STAN-CS-79-773, 1979. Pooling means and variances of disjoint parts. [DAT26] The fdia-graph dataset description: this repository's README and docs/reference/DATA_DICTIONARY.md (attack families, plausibility band, ramp profile). [DG06] J. Davis and M. Goadrich, "The relationship between precision-recall and ROC curves," Proc. 23rd Int. Conf. Machine Learning (ICML), pp. 233–240, 2006. Average precision as the step area under the precision-recall curve. [EST26] The project's state-estimation work (the subspace prior, its Huber composition and the localization gate); see docs/analysis/estimation/README.md. [FED26] The project's federated per-bus FDIA localization work (the swing and temporal-delta features); see docs/analysis/localization/README.md. [HAG84] W. W. Hager, "Condition estimates," SIAM J. Sci. Stat. Comput., vol. 5, no. 2, pp. 311–316, 1984. The 1-norm estimate of an inverse from a few solves, the fallback when SciPy lacks LAPACK's dtrcon. [HAN75] E. Handschin, F. C. Schweppe, J. Kohlas and A. Fiechter, "Bad data analysis for power system state estimation," IEEE Trans. Power App. Syst., vol. PAS-94, no. 2, 1975. Normalized residuals and the residual covariance. [HUB64] P. J. Huber, "Robust estimation of a location parameter," Ann. Math. Statist., vol. 35, no. 1, 1964. The Huber weight function. [JAC26] R. Abdulin and R. Narimani, Jacobian-informed features for FDIA localization (working digest, 2026); see docs/analysis/localization/README.md, section "Jacobian-informed features". [KEC25] C. Keçeci, K. R. Davis and E. Serpedin, "Federated learning-based distributed localization of false data injection attacks on smart grids," IEEE Systems Journal, vol. 19, no. 3, pp. 719–729, 2025. Per-bus localization metrics. [MCM17] B. McMahan, E. Moore, D. Ramage, S. Hampson and B. Agüera y Arcas, "Communication-efficient learning of deep networks from decentralized data," Proc. 20th Int. Conf. Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS), pp. 1273–1282, 2017. Federated averaging. [MP19] R. D. Zimmerman and C. E. Murillo-Sánchez, MATPOWER User's Manual, version 7.0, 2019. Branch model and makeYbus. [PGL19] S. Babaeinejadsarookolaee et al., "The power grid library for benchmarking AC optimal power flow algorithms," arXiv:1908.02788, 2019; PGLib-OPF v23.07, https://github.com/power-grid-lib/pglib-opf, licensed CC BY 4.0. The branch ratings (rate_a) of IEEE-14, 118 and 300 in fdia_graph.ratings are taken from it unchanged. [SCH70] F. C. Schweppe and J. Power App. Syst., vol. PAS-89, no. 1, 1970. [VLX07] U. von Luxburg, "A tutorial on spectral clustering," Statistics and Computing, vol. 17, no. 4, pp. 395–416, 2007. docs.title: Review checklist
docs.text:
Run this before a pull request leaves draft. It is built from the 313 findings of the automated reviewer the repository once used, on 80 pull requests (#52 to #148), grouped by kind and ordered by how often each kind came up; the repository runs no automated review now, and this page is what the one review before a pull request reads the diff against. python tools/prereview.py runs every mechanical check. This page covers what only a reader can check.

A third of all findings were one failure mode: code changed, but a doc, a docstring, a changelog line, a number or a generated file describing it did not. Most of those findings pointed at a file the pull request never touched. So the review starts from the diff and searches outward through the whole repository, not just the changed lines.

The review reads every file a pull request touches from top to bottom, not only the changed lines: on #140 to #152, more than a third of the findings were in lines the pull request did not change. A kind of finding that keeps coming up becomes a checklist item or a mechanical check.

docs.title: Since #140
docs.text:
The kinds, most frequent first.

kind what now catches it input escapes validation (a raw TypeError or KeyError, an argument used before its model, a missing Integer(), a negative count) the integer-field check; the malformed-input test that arrives with #147; item 4 doc claim does not match the code (a release, a file, a count, an unmerged pull request, an uncited outside claim) the cited-path check; item 15 logic and edge cases item 3 cache and resume item 10 tooling item 9 generated file stale the class-diagram, data-dictionary and rendered-diagram checks compatibility item 8 export missing item 8 performance item 11

docs.title: The checklist
docs.text:
1. Sweep for drift. For every changed name, setting, default, path or behaviour, search the rest of the repository for the old wording and fix every hit. That covers docstrings in the same module, docs/, README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, the tool docstrings and older bullets in the same ## Unreleased section. For example: rg -n "<old name>|<old value>|<old path>" docs src tools tests README.md CHANGELOG.md CONTRIBUTING.md.
  2. Every claim holds end to end. When the change says "no longer needs X", "unchanged", "exact" or "bounded memory", trace every call path (fit, score, estimate and their helpers) and confirm it. "Unchanged numbers" means the pinned search answers and scenario tests pass unchanged.
  3. Degenerate inputs. Check 0, 1, a fraction that rounds to 0, an empty candidate list, every retry failing, a validation set with no attacked (or no benign) record, and a refit after tuning. A retry loop must never emit the last candidate it rejected.
  4. Every new input is declared on a model.
  5. An integer field carries Integer(); AtLeast alone accepts 1.5.
  6. A float that must be finite carries Finite(); NaN and inf pass a > 0 check.
  7. An option is a OneOf(<Choice>).
  8. Arrays have their shape stated.
  9. Paired lists have a length invariant.
  10. Nothing is checked in a function body, and everything is checked before any download or file read.
  11. Tests prove the claim.
  12. No or True and no assertion that holds by construction.
  13. Each new fast path and each feature branch gets its own test.
  14. A test's name matches what it loads.
  15. A test that reads a published data file runs only under FDIA_SLOW=1 (the slow workflow), never in the default suite.
  16. Numbers in docs are recomputed from the committed results file: the right metric (macro-F1 versus node-F1), the right denominator, the right rounding, and no placeholders left.
  17. Generated files are regenerated and committed together. That means the diagram .mmd, .svg and .png, and the data dictionary.
  18. Backward compatibility.
  19. A new parameter goes last or is keyword-only.
  20. A removed or renamed public name is a changelog entry; no alias, shim or warning period is kept (old behaviour lives in the released versions).
  21. Dataclass field order does not change.
  22. A new public name is imported from its defining module; no package __init__.py re-exports it.
  23. Tooling and CI.
  24. Workflow inputs reach a shell through env:, never through ${{ }} inside run:.
  25. List endpoints are paginated.
  26. HTTP errors other than 404 surface.
  27. A failure exits non-zero.
  28. Files and np.load are opened in context managers.
  29. Caches and resumes are keyed by every input (frames, seed, K, the source pool, the release). The release is pinned explicitly, and a corrupt cache recomputes.
  30. Memory and hot loops.
    • Nothing of size T x N is materialized in float64 on a timeline path.
    • Nothing is allocated per Newton iteration.
    • Estimate the size at IEEE-300 over 72,000 frames; python tools/bench.py --check gates the timings.
  31. The readability contract. Channel indices come from NodeChannel, EdgeChannel and CurrentChannel (constants.channels), file paths and attributes from schema, every other constant from its module of constants/ (a knob is a field of a settings model), each formula exists once, and there are no positional tuples.
  32. Extras. A new import of scipy, torch or pandapower is declared in the matching extra, guarded with an install message, and kept off the import fdia_graph path.
  33. Prose. Read every added paragraph once for grammar, empty code fences and the docs' tone.
  34. Every factual sentence holds in this checkout.
    • A release named as the default or current matches registry._RELEASE.
    • A count (files, systems, findings) is recounted, not remembered.
    • A feature that arrives with an unmerged pull request is said to depend on it.
    • A claim about another project links the file or page that shows it.
  35. Read every touched file whole. The reviewer does, and a third of its findings sit in lines the pull request did not change. Look for the same kind of problem the change fixes (an argument still used before its model, a second copy of the old wording) elsewhere in the file.
  36. Every supported Python. CI runs 3.9 and 3.12 on Linux and one job on Windows, and the local gate runs one interpreter. A parser of loose input can differ between versions: from 3.11 date.fromisoformat also reads '20240131', which failed #147 on CI only. Pin a parsed form with a pattern before handing it to the standard library, and run the suite on a second interpreter with python tools/prereview.py --also-python <path> (or FDIA_PREREVIEW_PYTHONS, set once).

docs.title: The order
docs.text:
1. python tools/prereview.py until it passes.
  2. Work through the checklist above against the diff and every touched file, searching outward from every change, and fix what it finds.
  3. One review of the diff by review agents against this page, its findings fixed in one round; then mark the draft ready. It merges on green once the owner approves (CONTRIBUTING.md, "The pull request").
